We didn't apply for a ballot; we were there talking to election clerks, posing hypotheticals, and getting answers so that Americans could know what was happening in the elections. Many people in the United States did not even know about vouching for eight, and this investigative report educated them. By the way, we conducted training and specifically told each journalist NEVER TO SIGN AN AFFIDAVIT, NEVER TO PROCURE A BALLOT, NEVER TO EVEN TOUCH A BALLOT. We even did exercises training the journalists to say “the name is” rather than “my name is.” We were very intentional about what we were there to do, namely was to inform the public. Moriarty admitted that we stopped short of signing any oath or carrying out any fraud. “Both men stopped short of signing the oath we all sign before receiving our ballot.” — MORIARTY The reporters in the room questioned Moriarty on what exactly we're being prosecuted for. “Does that give them a way to say that we didn't commit a crime because we didn't take it all the way? ... Can you explain why you think it's still a crime?” — A REPORTER AT THE PRESS CONFERENCE So again, what exactly are we being prosecuted for? What is this really about? MAKE NO MISTAKE, THIS IS ABOUT PROSECUTING THE PRESS, AND THIS ISN'T THE FIRST TIME SOMETHING LIKE THIS HAS HAPPENED TO ME. STAND WITH JAMES → [ In New Orleans, LA, they falsely accused me of a felony and later admitted there was no felony. The U.S. attorneys involved in that case were eventually disbarred. The federal prosecutor was so furious about this case that he literally threw my book at me. “You're a nasty, little, cowardly spud. You are scum! I recused from your case!” — PROSECUTOR JIM LETTEN Then there was the case when the FBI came knocking at my house. Agents stormed into my home and unlocked my phone to get access to my Signal in order to intimidate me and to intimidate the sources that come to me. It was such a landmark First Amendment case that the American Civil Liberties Union (ACLU) filed amicus, and the Reporters Committee for Freedom of the Press came to my defense. I have been to the Ninth Circuit Court of Appeals, challenging the constitutionality of Oregon's recording laws. Got a reversal there. I went up to the 1st Circuit Court of Appeals in Massachusetts there. We won a partial victory. In another civil case, Shirley Teter v. O'Keefe, I won at directed verdict. For that case, there were six pro-bono lawyers representing the plaintiff, who stated, “We're not paid by the Hillary Clinton campaign or by the Democratic Party or anything like that.” The federal judge pointed out the unsolicited statement only raised further questions, and ordered them to pay my legal fees. I have been sued so many times and have had so many criminal threats made against me that even the media that hates me is forced to acknowledge that I have established legal 1st Amendment precedent throughout the nation. We also overturned a jury verdict against me in the D.C. Circuit Court of Appeals last month before a panel of judges, which were appointed by Democrats. We convinced the panel to side with the 1st Amendment, creating a new standard for undercover journalism across the board. It's now called the “O'KEEFE PRINCIPLE.” On publication injury when undercover journalism is involved. I've won these fights before. STAND WITH ME AND HELP ME WIN THIS ONE. [ The politics of fear and weaponized lawfare don't seem to work against me. It never has. Actually, it has always backfired against the people who come after me. Why is that? It's because what's at issue here is not actually political; it's fundamental. This is about whether citizens still have a right to ask questions of their government servants, and such a fundamental right will always prevail if you do not cower at their threats. AND THE THING ABOUT ME IS — I NEVER SETTLE. Most people find lawsuits stressful. The process becomes a form of punishment, but not to me. I actually love this process. I enjoy this process. I'm going to have fun with this process. Because it allows me to expose injustice at the highest levels. THERE IS NOTHING AS SWEET AS JUSTICE, AND THERE IS NOTHING AS MOTIVATING AS INJUSTICE. And in this case, they have put your right to speak on the line. EVERYTHING WE BELIEVE IN AS AMERICANS HAS BEEN PUT ON THE LINE. [ But it does seem to indicate the direction of where our country is going. I recognize that we're well past the point of being completely divided in this country, but this case isn't about what divides us; it's about what unites us. What unites us is so much stronger than what divides us. Because the right to question authority and educate people matters to people on all sides. Ironically, Moriarty put out a statement on social media and restricted the comments section on her official X government account, which violates the 1st Amendment. And now, I'm summoned to appear before the Hennepin County judge on Monday, Nov. 16th, just four days after our Citizen Journalism Gala, where we'll host many people who don't all agree with each other on public policy. And yet, each of them all stands united behind the 1st Amendment. It is neck and neck. Election Day is less than a week away, _**and Darline's seat could swing either way.**_

Here's what I told the folks there:
> _-> You don't want a Senate run by Chuck Schumer.
> -> You don't want Elizabeth Warren to chair the Senate Banking Committee.
> -> And you don't want Bernie Sanders setting environmental policy that kills jobs in South Carolina._
That's the radical Democrat agenda, _and it's what Annie Andrews would be voting for._

She's raised over $25 million - nearly $4 million in the last couple of weeks - from liberal donors who don't share South Carolina's values. **She built her campaign attacking Lindsey, and now her whole mission is to defeat his sister.**

Darline stands for common sense: low taxes, good jobs, and backing the police. She won't vote to put violent criminals back on the street or to let boys compete in girls' sports. She has thirty years of experience working for the people of her state, and she has a backbone.

clean_body: I just left South Carolina. This race is neck and neck, and Darline needs us now. | Peter, On Monday, I was in South Carolina, on the campaign trail with Darline Graham. I want to tell you what I saw, because this race is closer than anyone in Washington wants to admit. It is neck and neck. Election Day is less than a week away, and Darline's seat could swing either way. Here's what I told the folks there: -> You don't want a Senate run by Chuck Schumer. -> You don't want Elizabeth Warren to chair the Senate Banking Committee. -> And you don't want Bernie Sanders setting environmental policy that kills jobs in South Carolina. That's the radical Democrat agenda, and it's what Annie Andrews would be voting for. She's raised over $25 million - nearly $4 million in the last couple of weeks - from liberal donors who don't share South Carolina's values. She built her campaign attacking Lindsey, and now her whole mission is to defeat his sister. Darline stands for common sense: low taxes, good jobs, and backing the police. She won't vote to put violent criminals back on the street or to let boys compete in girls' sports. She has thirty years of experience working for the people of her state, and she has a backbone. What Darline doesn't have is Hollywood money. Schumer needs JUST FOUR SEATS to take the majority, and he's betting South Carolina hands him one because Darline is being outspent after running two elections back-to-back. Peter, races this close are decided in the final days by who can stay on the air, keep volunteers knocking doors, and get voters to the polls. They tried this playbook on me in Texas. National Democrats dumped millions to attack me because they thought the bigger bank account would win. Now I'm making a personal plea: show up for Darline. | | | | | | We have less than a week. | | **_Meet Russell:_** Born and raised in Surfside Beach, SC, Congressman Russell Fry is the proud and homegrown Representative for South Carolina’s 7th Congressional District. Growing up in a cinder block home with no heating or air conditioning, Russell learned at an early age that hard work and perseverance pave the only true path to the American Dream. He watched his parents work day in and day out to make ends meet. And the values they instilled in him during his upbringing led Russell to self-fund both his undergraduate education at the University of South Carolina, and later his law studies at the Charleston School of Law. At Charleston, Russell served as the President of the Student Bar Association and even helped the school achieve its American Bar Association accreditation. He went on to practice law in the Grand Strand area for over a decade before entering the political arena to serve in the South Carolina House of Representatives for State House District 106 (Horry County). During his seven-year tenure in the SC House, Russell fought to safeguard Constitutional liberties, lower taxes, and put the best interests of South Carolina families above all else. He climbed the ranks to become Chief Majority Whip, and also chaired the House Opioid Prevention Study Committee. Under Russell’s leadership, 18 policy initiatives to combat the opioid crisis were signed into law. Since the first day he stepped foot in Washington, Russell has strived to shake up the corrupt status quo and deliver real change for the American people. He believes adamantly that so long as the American people stand united, we can keep the American Dream alive for every citizen of our great nation. Russell is a dedicated husband to his wife, Bronwen, and a loving father to his son, James. The family lives in Murrells Inlet with their chocolate lab, Jasper.

To do this, we need everyone to get out and VOTE.****Patriot, this is why I’m reaching out to you. | | | | | - | | This is our LAST end-of-month push before Election Day, and we need your help. Our volunteers are out knocking doors and pounding the pavement, but our field operations are running low on funds. America cannot afford for Republicans to lose this election. == Please chip in before the clock strikes midnight on Halloween.****The only thing spooky this season should be the costumes—not the thought of a Democrat-controlled House. | | | | | | Meet Russell: Born and raised in Surfside Beach, SC, Congressman Russell Fry is the proud and homegrown Representative for South Carolina’s 7th Congressional District. Growing up in a cinder block home with no heating or air conditioning, Russell learned at an early age that hard work and perseverance pave the only true path to the American Dream. He watched his parents work day in and day out to make ends meet. And the values they instilled in him during his upbringing led Russell to self-fund both his undergraduate education at the University of South Carolina, and later his law studies at the Charleston School of Law. At Charleston, Russell served as the President of the Student Bar Association and even helped the school achieve its American Bar Association accreditation. He went on to practice law in the Grand Strand area for over a decade before entering the political arena to serve in the South Carolina House of Representatives for State House District 106 (Horry County). During his seven-year tenure in the SC House, Russell fought to safeguard Constitutional liberties, lower taxes, and put the best interests of South Carolina families above all else. He climbed the ranks to become Chief Majority Whip, and also chaired the House Opioid Prevention Study Committee. Under Russell’s leadership, 18 policy initiatives to combat the opioid crisis were signed into law. Since the first day he stepped foot in Washington, Russell has strived to shake up the corrupt status quo and deliver real change for the American people. He believes adamantly that so long as the American people stand united, we can keep the American Dream alive for every citizen of our great nation. Russell is a dedicated husband to his wife, Bronwen, and a loving father to his son, James. | | Friend, **Pete Buttigieg is coming to southern Minnesota this weekend.** On Sunday he’s joining my opponent, Jake Johnson, at a Vikings watch party in Rochester. Johnson’s campaign is using it to kick off their final weekend of door-knocking before Election Day.Let’s be clear about what this is. Pete Buttigieg isn’t on anybody’s ballot this year. He’s been campaigning in more than 30 districts across the country, and when reporters ask whether he’s running for president in 2028, he won’t rule it out. Rochester is just one more stop on the tour.**He says he’s excited to “show up” for Jake Johnson.** When a train derailed and spilled toxic chemicals in East Palestine, Ohio, it took Secretary Buttigieg nearly three weeks to show up there. But a football party in Rochester two days before an election? He’ll be there.And I’ll let Vikings fans decide how they feel about Biden’s green new deal czar crashing game day. Here’s the pattern. First, Tim Walz’s PAC endorsed Johnson. Then, the DCCC put this seat on its target list. Now, national Democrats are sending in their favorite 2028 hopeful to close the deal.**To them, southern Minnesota is a seat to flip.** A photo op on the road to the White House. **To me, it’s home.** But I won’t pretend Sunday doesn’t matter. A big-name visit brings cameras, a wave of volunteers, and a flood of online donations from liberals who couldn’t find Olmsted County on a map. Johnson’s campaign has spent all year bragging about outraising me.Early voting is open. Ballots are being cast right now. Less than a week from today, it’s over. I need to answer their final weekend push with one of our own.**Will you chip in right now to help us fight back?**

Peter, if you've ever been to a Hawkeyes game, you know the moment. The cymbals crash. The band calls out, “WHAT'S THE WORD?”

And there's only one answer for our sea of black and gold in the stands: **“FIGHT! FIGHT! FIGHT FOR IOWA!”** Thousands of voices become one, and they don't stop until the game is won.

You'll hear it again in just a couple of days when the Hawkeyes take the field. Here in Iowa, we know what it means to fight for something you believe in.

With Election Day on November 3 just around the corner, our team is giving this race everything we have. We're knocking doors, making calls, talking with voters, and making sure people across IA-01 know what Christina Bohannan is fighting for. If you've walked through a neighborhood in the district lately, there's a good chance you've seen one of us doing everything we can to give our campaign a fighting chance.

From the very beginning, we've fought for every inch of ground we've gained. We've put in the long days, weathered the hard moments (and the hard weather!), and kept going because we believe the people of this district deserve a representative who will work just as hard for them as they work for their families. _We won't stop until the polls close._

subject: Denver Post endorses! "Unrivaled enthusiasm"
body:
In their words, "Bridges will bring unrivaled enthusiasm to a statewide office that is often overlooked."

| | | | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/f6dd3ec2a81f/get-more-smarter-on-colorados-budget-10379842?e=b48bb2b4f4)

[|

| | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | Hi there,

Here’s what [The Denver Post](https://us.list-manage.com/LZhYNpb7D9S?e=b48bb2b4f4&c2id=bbe572662fdb5fed2d0855c1bcb00da8) said in their endorsement of our campaign: **“Bridges will bring unrivaled enthusiasm to a statewide office that is often overlooked.”**
As I said in my [campaign video](https://us.list-manage.com/wNjLm2CZyTg?e=b48bb2b4f4&c2id=bbe572662fdb5fed2d0855c1bcb00da8), Treasurer is anything but boring.
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/18MWkOtB2YI?e=b48bb2b4f4&c2id=bbe572662fdb5fed2d0855c1bcb00da8)
| | And it’s not just my attitude they like! The Post also praised my plan to invest Colorado dollars in Colorado.
“Bridges wants to advocate for a small amount of the investment funds the state holds... to be invested in safe and investment income-generating Colorado businesses and projects. **We think that is a great idea.** ”
As I’ve said for two years now, we have billions of dollars parked in Washington and Wall Street. We should put more of that money to work right here at home in housing, infrastructure, and creating good jobs. The Post agrees.

This is the clear opportunity in the Treasurer’s office. Not just managing money, but finding ways to lower the cost of living for Colorado families. I’m grateful to the Denver Post for their endorsement and for recognizing the potential of our approach.
And—of course—if you’re in a place to help us finish this campaign strong, I would appreciate the support.
---

# Iran
* **Vance requests renewed talks in letter to Iran 's security chief: **Vice President JD Vance [sent](https://substack.com/redirect/18e0106e-ee75-4a38-a3d4-1d62ef096bf6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a letter to Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, proposing renewed direct negotiations as the Trump administration considers launching a short, intense military campaign against Iran after next week's U.S. midterm elections, the Wall Street Journal reported.
* The letter was delivered through Qatari mediators on Sunday. In it, Vance proposed a meeting as early as next week, to be potentially held in Qatar or Turkey. Vance would lead the U.S. delegation, the New York Times [reported](https://substack.com/redirect/d883e228-44fa-4906-ad90-a66486971863?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Discussions have so far focused on a negotiating framework rather than specific terms, as Washington demands upfront nuclear concessions while Tehran seeks immediate economic relief.
* President Donald Trump confirmed on Wednesday that he had approved Vance's outreach, but he characterized it as an effort to facilitate medical supplies. "They need help with medical supplies and various things," Trump told reporters. "He asked me what I thought. I said, 'If you want to do that, that's OK.'"
* Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi [wrote](https://substack.com/redirect/582d5933-d59e-4247-9c8b-dd735772e40a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on X: "While our Brave Armed Forces are fully prepared to defend the Homeland, Iran continues to give diplomacy a chance to succeed." He added that Tehran remained "in close and ongoing contact with intermediaries" to explore implementing Iran's seven-day plan "in even less than a week."
* **AP: U.S. warns regional allies to prepare for possible renewed war in Iran:** U.S. officials told several Middle East allies to prepare for renewed military action against Iran after the U.S. midterm elections next week, two diplomats briefed on the matter [told the Associated Press](https://substack.com/redirect/dce3b3c6-28ad-4732-bfb8-094a3e3b3de3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
* The diplomatic sources told the AP that the U.S. informed regional allies that the new round of military action could last for several days, but regional officials are preparing for Iranian retaliation that could lead to a longer fight.
* U.S. officials urged regional allies to take precautionary measures against Iranian retaliatory strikes targeting energy facilities and other crucial infrastructure, according to AP.
* President Trump has not made a final decision on whether to carry out new strikes against Iran, the diplomats said.
* **Iran claims three oil tankers struck mines near Strait of Hormuz:** Three oil tankers [caught fire](https://substack.com/redirect/81a6f27b-a471-469d-8961-364b89c215ec?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) after striking naval mines south of the Strait of Hormuz on Wednesday and Thursday, Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) Navy said on Thursday.
* The IRGC said the vessels had switched off their radar and navigation systems, ignored warnings, and attempted to pass through an "unauthorized" southern route.
* Separately, the UK Maritime Trade Operations said on Thursday that a ship had been spotted on fire nine nautical miles north of Khasab, Oman. The crew's condition, the extent of the damage, and the environmental impact remain unknown.
* IRGC spokesperson Hossein Mohebi reiterated that the Strait of Hormuz remains "under the strategic control of the Iranian armed forces and will never be opened until the Islamic Republic's conditions are fully met," in comments quoted by the Fars news agency on Thursday.
* **Iran claims capture of one U.S. spy drone, downing of another over Hormuz:** The IRGC [claimed](https://substack.com/redirect/2bed1c2a-d7b7-4321-b9ef-66b7b751fcb3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Thursday that it captured an intact U.S. MQM-170 reconnaissance and decoy drone west of the Strait of Hormuz. The IRGC electronic warfare unit allegedly took control of the aircraft's guidance systems and took it down.
* The IRGC said, without providing evidence, that the U.S. deployed the drone to identify Iranian air defense positions along the Persian Gulf coast and had taken off from an unnamed Gulf country.
* Separately, the IRGC said that it intercepted and destroyed a U.S. MQ-1 drone over the eastern Strait of Hormuz, the 14th MQ-1 drone it says it has shot down.
* The U.S. military has not commented on the IRGC's claims.
* **Hegseth fires Pentagon 's top military planner: **U.S. War Secretary Pete Hegseth [fired](https://substack.com/redirect/68a08b39-302c-4180-b564-ab013d123518?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Brett Sylvia, the Pentagon's top military planner. Sylvia served as director of strategy, plans, and policy on the Joint Staff, a key position responsible for coordinating military planning and advising the chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff and the president.
* A Pentagon official accused Sylvia of leaking classified information related to the wars in Iran and Ukraine, according to CBS News, though the allegations have not been independently substantiated. Sylvia's dismissal is the latest in a series of departures involving nearly two dozen senior military leaders under Hegseth.

# Palestine
* **Israeli drone strike in central Gaza kills two Palestinians:** Two Palestinians were killed and several others wounded on Thursday in an Israeli [drone strike](https://substack.com/redirect/f3763fc5-6bcd-4bc5-b7c9-82bf440fdbdf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) targeting a vehicle near the entrance to the Maghazi refugee camp in the central Gaza Strip, according to WAFA.
* **Israeli forces demolish homes in the occupied West Bank as Hebron siege enters seventh day:**
* **Hebron:** Israel's military assault [entered](https://substack.com/redirect/855c1e78-0e1d-478c-9bc1-2f5512a7b6f7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) its seventh consecutive day on Thursday, with more than 780 families affected and approximately 5,000 Palestinians forcibly displaced or confined to their homes, particularly in the sealed-off neighborhoods of Al-Jalda and Deir Bahha, WAFA reported. More than 115 Palestinians have been arrested since the operation began.
* Israeli restrictions have disrupted in-person education for an estimated 80,000 students across the governorate, with 66 schools directly affected.
* On Thursday, Israeli forces arrested seven Palestinians and injured two others during raids.
* In Tarqumiya, northwest of Hebron, Israeli bulldozers demolished an inhabited home, leaving seven family members homeless.
* **Salfit:** Israeli forces [demolished](https://substack.com/redirect/fac342ad-8a27-4734-bebc-0d70e054640a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) three homes in Deir Ballut and Bruqin. In the Wadi Al-Ahmar area, Israeli settlers stole olives from Palestinian farmland that owners had been prevented from accessing. Settlers fired live ammunition toward a Palestinian farmer who encountered them.
* **Jericho:** Israeli forces [demolished](https://substack.com/redirect/9db02791-f52b-43d4-a054-2b7c642c7622?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) agricultural structures and bulldozed farmland east of Jericho.
* **Ramallah and Al-Bireh:** Israeli settlers [attacked](https://substack.com/redirect/c4bac5b4-a0a8-4f8d-8d63-e3cfc7e2b838?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Palestinian olive harvesters in Kafr Malik, northeast of Ramallah.
* **Israeli settlers beat U.S. journalist and Russian activists in West Bank:** Israeli settlers attacked U.S. journalist Jasper Nathaniel and two Russian activists in the Palestinian village of Umm Al-Khair in Masafer Yatta, in the occupied West Bank, before Israeli authorities arrested two of the victims, according to Russian activist Adele Shoko.
* Videos [shared](https://substack.com/redirect/4de1ec7f-ad66-478c-bd0b-2aa46a7aec1c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) by Shoko show several men, some armed, beating Nathaniel and Russian activist Andrey X. "Andrey was severely beaten and lost consciousness several times in front of police," Shoko wrote, adding that he was denied hospital treatment and taken to a police station instead.
* "Jasper and I were also beaten. Jasper was then pepper-sprayed and arrested." Another video showed Nathaniel shouting, "I just got beat up," as Israeli forces led him away.
* **Health Ministry stresses urgency of increased medical evacuations through Rafah:** On Thursday, the Gaza Health Ministry reiterated its call for the opening of the Rafah crossing to allow for patients requiring medical treatment to leave and to increase the number of people allowed to travel on medical evacuations.
* "The successive and sudden closures of the crossings, and the deliberate slowness in the procedures, have turned the file of medical transfers from a humanitarian rescue path to a fatal obstacle; which caused a serious deterioration in the health conditions of thousands of wounded and sick, and the loss of dozens of them to their lives while waiting to be allowed to travel," the ministry said in a statement.
* Last week, Drop Site News [reported](https://substack.com/redirect/16e289a9-6674-4a40-88b0-2fb4bef13470?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that the entire functioning of the Rafah crossing was in jeopardy after the UN informed Palestinian officials that, beginning in mid-November, it would stop receiving Palestinians returning from Egypt and coordinating their entry into Gaza, citing the dangers facing returnees and repeated Israeli arrests.
* In response to inquiries from Drop Site, UN Public Information Officer Daria Carmon responded: "At this time we are reassessing the UN facilitated return operations into Gaza through Rafah crossing. We will make a public pronouncement about our position once the review is completed later this month. The UN remains fully committed to continue supporting medical evacuation missions through Rafah Crossing."

# Yemen
* **Nearly 1,700 killed and 281,000 displaced in Yemen since August:** At least 1,677 people have been killed and 7,395 injured in Yemen since August amid escalating fighting, according to the World Health Organization. Between October 20 and 25 alone, the WHO recorded 559 casualties, averaging approximately 93 killed or injured per day.
* More than 281,000 people have been [displaced](https://substack.com/redirect/10db0dee-770b-4e36-900c-7d9f477bb47b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) by fighting in Yemen since the beginning of August, with over half sheltering in Taiz governorate, according to the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs.
* Humanitarian access has deteriorated over the past three weeks after damage to a key road connecting Taiz to southern governorates forced aid deliveries onto narrow mountain routes.
* Three-quarters of displaced Yemenis are sheltering in sites with inadequate water, sanitation, and shelter, while more than 35,000 families lack shelter assistance and over 230,000 people need emergency water and sanitation support.
* In Marib, only six of 31 mobile medical teams remain operational, and 15 health facilities have shut down entirely.
* **Ansarallah reports 101 airstrikes by Saudi-backed forces across Yemen:** Ansarallah [reported](https://substack.com/redirect/7cfd552a-2ad3-427d-9836-40afb0252723?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) 101 airstrikes by the Saudi-led coalition across the country over the past 24 hours, including strikes targeting the Dhubab and Mocha districts near the strategic Bab al-Mandab Strait.
* Separately, Saudi-backed Yemeni forces said that they carried out two airstrikes on an Ansarallah military camp in the al-Ash'oub area west of Taiz.
* Meanwhile, air traffic at Aden International Airport resumed following a sixth Ansarallah attack on the facility, which caused casualties and damage.
* The National Human Rights Authority in Sana'a said on Thursday that a Saudi strike on a paint factory near the city of Taiz caused a large fire and could release toxic gases and contaminate nearby soil and groundwater. It said that the attack was a war crime.
* **HRW: Ansarallah depriving civilians of food, medicine in Taiz:** Human Rights Watch on Thursday [accused](https://substack.com/redirect/1fff34f8-8cd6-4e80-849b-31fa41ba4198?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Ansarallah, also known as the Houthis, of endangering civilians in Taiz city by enforcing a siege on hundreds of thousands of residents in the city.
* "Renewed efforts by the Houthis to cut off food, water, and medicine to Taizz show their utter disregard for civilian lives,"[ Niku Jafarnia](https://substack.com/redirect/abd442b6-349c-41a2-bd35-2c29e4b81639?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), Yemen and Bahrain researcher at Human Rights Watch, said in a statement. "Throughout the 12-year-long siege of [Taiz], the Houthis have bombed, starved, and denied humanitarian aid to a million residents of the city with scant adherence to international law."
* An Ansarallah spokesperson told Human Rights Watch that Saudi-backed government forces were blocking roads into the city. But residents, civil society workers, and United Nations officials blamed Ansarallah for the shortages, Human Rights Watch said.

# Lebanon
* **Hezbollah leader calls Israeli election results "an expression of defeat," rejects disarmament: **Israel's election results were "one of the expressions of defeat," Hezbollah Secretary-General Naim Qassem said on Wednesday, pointing to what he described as Israel's internal political, economic, and social crises.
* "We do not concern ourselves with who governs Israel, but let it be perfectly clear that it cannot continue its occupation and must leave our land," he said, vowing to continue resistance regardless of the election outcome.
* Qassem insisted there was "no room for discussion" about disarming Hezbollah as long as Israel continues its occupation and attacks on Lebanon, and called for an Israeli withdrawal under the November 2024 ceasefire agreement and UN Security Council Resolution 1701.
* He also declared the June 26 Lebanon-Israel framework agreement "null and void." Amid concerns that Hezbollah could enter another war in support of Iran, Qassem did not clarify whether the group would intervene if the U.S. or Israel launched new attacks, but said the U.S.-Iran agreement had helped reduce Israeli attacks on Lebanon.

# U.S. News
* **DoorDash buys Instacart for $17 billion:** The food delivery giant Doordash [announced](https://substack.com/redirect/689ad1e4-b55a-45f2-a011-183a6e52d17b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Thursday that it purchased the grocery delivery app Instacart for $17 billion, the New York Times reported. It is DoorDash's largest acquisition to date. The deal could face antitrust scrutiny and pushback from grocers and gig workers. The deal is expected to close in 2027 or 2028. DoorDash completed 993 million orders in the third quarter, up 28%, while Instacart, once valued at $39 billion by private investors, has a market capitalization of about $14 billion and relationships with more than 2,200 retailers.
* **Dolores Huerta, labor leader and civil rights figure who co-founded United Farm Workers, dies at 96:** Labor and civil rights leader **Dolores Huerta** [died](https://substack.com/redirect/34101df9-9924-4aa9-ad81-37932416473b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Wednesday at her home in Bakersfield, Calif., of cancer, a family spokesman said. Alongside **Cesar Chavez** she founded the National Farm Workers Association in 1962, and led the 1960s and '70s strikes and boycotts that helped many California grape-growers consolidate worker power. She served as the union's vice president for nearly four decades. Over her working life, police arrested her 22 times. In 1988, she was severely beaten by a San Francisco police officer--a case settled by the city for $825,000. Huerta is widely believed to have coined the phrase "Si se puede." President **Barack Obama** awarded her the Presidential Medal of Freedom in 2012. In early 2026, she told the New York Times that Chavez raped her in 1966, and that two of her children resulted from sexual encounters with him. She is survived by 13 of her 14 children, 24 grandchildren, 23 great-grandchildren, and seven great-great-grandchildren.
* **Fed holds rates steady:** The Federal Reserve [kept](https://substack.com/redirect/a103f2b5-4fb0-432a-8b82-0cd0d0805265?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) its benchmark rate at 3.75% to 4% on Wednesday, with governor **Lisa Cook** and Cleveland Fed President **Beth Hammack** dissenting in favor of a quarter-point increase. The Fed rated economic activity as "strong," up from "solid." Traders see an 85% chance of a rate hike in December, according to CME's FedWatch Tool. Inflation has come in above target and Thursday's PCE report is expected to show a rate of 3.6% for the year through September. Federal Reserve Chairman **Kevin Warsh** said that starting next year, one of the eight annual Federal Open Market Committee meetings will focus solely on monetary policy strategy.
* It was Cook's first dissent, coming ahead of a White House hearing next week on Trump's bid to remove her over alleged mortgage fraud, which her lawyers call a pretext.
* **Leak exposes records of more than 41,000 DHS employees and contractors, including undercover ICE agents:** The transparency nonprofit Distributed Denial of Secrets [published](https://substack.com/redirect/5ef93ab1-436a-459c-af2d-935f0f04ec50?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) an archive it calls "Icepick" on Wednesday, which contains the records of more than 41,000 DHS employees and contractors. In a press release, DDoSecrets said the information comes from DHS's Okta login system and was obtained by a group that calls itself the Department of Peace. That group attached a note that said, "They have our information, so it's only fair that we have theirs." The records, last updated on August 19, cover the DHS and seven component agencies, including emails, phone numbers, office addresses, supervisor names, and permission groups referencing undercover agents, and surveillance programs. DHS said it was working to address a potential security breach.
* **Judge rejects Trump administration bid to set aside 20,000 California ballots:** Judge **David O. Carter** , a **Bill Clinton** appointee, [ruled](https://substack.com/redirect/48e128f8-c51a-475d-8a84-3dedcd0f0a36?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Wednesday that the Trump administration's demand that California sequester 20,000 ballots "would wreak havoc and disrupt the election that is already underway" and "discount the votes of United States citizens." Carter wrote that "never before in American history has the federal government, on the eve of an election, sought to coerce a state and local government to abandon their own constitutional elections procedures." He noted that the Department of Justice has filed at least 31 suits seeking state voter rolls and has won "precisely zero" of the 26 suits decided so far. He called the DOJ's effort part of "a broad, ongoing pattern of attempted election interference." The DOJ immediately appealed the ruling.
* **DOJ turned a rights-group informant into the government 's own:** The rights group Southern Poverty Law Center said one of its informants was flipped by the Trump administration, and became a government informant, according to court papers the SPLC [filed](https://substack.com/redirect/1428685f-a2af-4359-b7b0-b55563b0b388?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Wednesday. SPLC lawyers said that the informant "F-9," who worked with the group from 1996 and was paid at least $1.2 million over 16 years, has met DOJ prosecutors more than 20 times since November 2025 under immunity, exchanged about 1,800 texts with FBI and IRS agents, and given at least four "intelligence briefings" to federal authorities as part of the DOJ's ongoing fraud case against the group. One of the informant's PowerPoint presentations bore FBI and IRS seals, as though "he were an actual member of the prosecution team," the SPLC filings said. The group requested that the court order the informant to preserve all documents, and to grant a subpoena for his materials. In April, the DOJ charged the SPLC with defrauding donors, alleging that the group funneled money to informants inside white-supremacist groups. Defense lawyers said that the case began after a coalition of right-leaning groups complained to senior White House advisor **Stephen Miller** about the SPLC's work.
* **Trump administration issues more than 100 subpoenas for voter records in at least 13 states ahead of midterms:** Reuters [identified](https://substack.com/redirect/fba3954a-f160-4745-9b30-6e513803adb5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) more than 100 subpoenas issued by the Trump administration, mostly in the past three months, to state and local election officials. The Trump administration sought records on tens of thousands of voters. The federal government targeted Democratic strongholds like Minneapolis, Philadelphia, and Los Angeles, and Republican-leaning Texas, Kansas, and Georgia. Legal experts told Reuters that the federal government could use the records to contest close election results. One expert said that the probes are "setting up" post-election challenges.
* **California elites spend $612 million to defeat billionaire tax:** Seventy past and current California billionaires have spent a record-setting $612 million to block a one-time, 5% tax on their wealth, [a Politico analysis found](https://substack.com/redirect/7019c36d-e9d8-4b02-8418-f42298769b2c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). That spending has pushed support for the tax below 50%, [according to two new polls](https://substack.com/redirect/5ea1591d-9f61-4990-a379-970da749d09c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
* **Company linked to Darline Graham 's husband was sanctioned for arming Russia against Ukraine: Lindsey Graham**'s central political ambition was to confront and contain Russia. The former South Carolina senator died within hours of returning from Ukraine, where he toured a drone factory as one of his last acts on his earth. His sister **Darline Graham** now holds his seat and is on the ballot next week. It turns out that her husband works for a company linked to a Chinese firm sanctioned in 2024 for providing sophisticated military tech to Russia. [Read more here](https://substack.com/redirect/e9814c5c-198d-405e-b371-967f1b32489a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
* **CNN Senate poll finds Democrats up in Michigan, Kansas, Maine, and Texas:** President Trump is heading to South Carolina to stave off Republican catastrophe there, while polls show potentially competitive races in Iowa, Nebraska, Florida, Mississippi, and Arkansas. Four [new surveys](https://substack.com/redirect/56f25c88-aea4-4048-a4e1-19eeb0f7239c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) from CNN put Democrats on top in critical races:
* **Michigan**
* Abdul El-Sayed (D): 49%
* Mike Rogers (R): 42%
* **Kansas**
* Adam Hamilton (D): 49%
* Roger Marshall (R): 45%
* **Maine**
* Troy Jackson (D): 49%
* Susan Collins (R): 45%
* **Texas**
* James Talarico (D): 49%
* Ken Paxton (R): 43%

# Other International News
* **Russian drone strike on Ukraine train station kills at least 14:** A Russian jet-powered drone [hit](https://substack.com/redirect/8845f5dc-00e0-481f-a846-d551f61d3113?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a busy train platform in Dnipro, Ukraine, on Thursday, killing at least 13 people. At least 14 others were injured in the attack, six of whom are in critical condition.
* Russian strikes also hit Kharkiv, damaging an educational institution, and a strike on the Rivne region killed one man.
* **Fl avio Bolsonaro declares himself Brazil's rightful "leader" after arriving in Miami:** Brazil's [failed](https://substack.com/redirect/ba38ac58-b41a-4945-92b8-83bb5ba99c2d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) right-wing presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro, who left Brazil in secret after losing the election to Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, said in a Wednesday letter that he was the rightfully "elected president" of the country. He claimed that the Supreme court and Lula had carried out an "electoral coup" against him. He later amended the letter to say he was Brazil's "leader" and added that he "did not flee Brazil." He thanked Argentina's Javier Milei for helping him travel to the U.S., and thanked Trump for securing visas for him and his family.
* **Pakistani court sentences human rights lawyers to 10 years in prison:** A Pakistani anti-terrorism court [sentenced](https://substack.com/redirect/1afb9ef4-ebc7-4836-81e5-68e56e6d33fc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) prominent human rights lawyers Imaan Mazari and her husband, Hadi Ali Chattha, to 10 years in prison on Thursday. Their sentences will run concurrently with additional one-year and two-year sentences for obstructing and assaulting government servants. Mazari and her husband were accused of holding a protest in 2024 that blocked a road, and thereby endangered an international cricket team's security plans. They denied the charges, calling themselves "prisoners of conscience" targeted for their human rights work. Mazari's mother, Shireen Mazari, a former member of Imran Khan's cabinet, said that they were not allowed access to their lawyer or given key legal documents in the case. The couple had earlier been sentenced to 17 years in prison for social media posts. That sentence was suspended by Pakistan's Supreme Court--they were re-arrested for the 2024 protest on the same day.
* **Clashes on Pakistan-Afghan border kill one:** Clashes on the border of Afghanistan and Pakistan [killed](https://substack.com/redirect/332e0b05-2b79-4b3e-9b73-2344b11e6348?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) one person and injured five others, a Pakistani official said on Wednesday, accusing the Afghan Taliban of firing at civilian houses and a market in Pakistan's Waziristan region on Tuesday. He added that Pakistani forces would respond "effectively and heavily" to the attack.
* Afghan's Taliban government said Pakistan carried out four drone attacks on the district commissioner's office and nearby security facilities in Paktika province, and Afghan defense ministry spokesperson Sedeequllah Nasrat said Afghan forces retaliated against a nearby Pakistani military base, causing several casualties.
* Pakistan accuses Kabul of harboring militants who stage cross-border attacks, a charge the Afghan government denies. The conflict has killed hundreds of people this year. Drop Site's latest reporting on the clashes is available[ here](https://substack.com/redirect/31a72dda-ba67-4d09-a2c5-250cae07f85f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
* **South Korean prosecutors again seek death penalty for ex-President Yoon:** South Korean prosecutors [renewed](https://substack.com/redirect/1bd4f0f2-86b5-4e18-bed1-15dad7f26ad0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) their effort to impose the death penalty on former President Yoon Suk-yeol at a Seoul High Court hearing on Thursday. Earlier this year, Yoon was convicted of leading an 2024 insurrection against the state. South Korea halted state executions in 1997, but prosecutors said that was "no reason to hesitate" in sending Yoon to his death. In January, prosecutors failed to secure a death penalty at Yoon's trial. He was sentenced to life in prison instead.
* **Iraq PM visits Damascus:** Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi [met](https://substack.com/redirect/7d4ec18d-c5ad-43c2-acd7-7220627021f9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa on Wednesday. The two reportedly discussed exporting Iraqi oil through Syrian territory, boosting bilateral trade and joint agricultural development, Iraqi News Agency reported. Since the U.S.-led war on Iran began, Iraq has exported oil through Syria. In July, Iraq and Syria signed deals to revive the Haditha-Baniyas pipeline, entrusting a Chevron-led consortium to implement the deal.
* **North Korea fires short-range ballistic missiles into Sea of Japan:** North Korea [fired](https://substack.com/redirect/966f9314-d2be-4973-999b-fa1051b43658?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) about 10 missiles into the Sea of Japan on Thursday, South Korea's Defense Ministry said. The test firings come just days after South Korea proposed military talks with North Korea over a border dispute. In September, a landmine blast in the Demilitarized Zone separating North Korea and South Korea injured three South Korean soldiers, which joint South Korea-UN blamed on mines North Korea planted over a year ago. North Korea rejected the finding, and told the UN Security Council that South Korea fabricated the incident.
* **El Salvador to send over 2,000 soldiers to Haiti, increasing military presence:** Salvadoran President Nayib Bukele [told](https://substack.com/redirect/8c6f9dd3-f00b-4483-8c77-c5fb16638489?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Haitian Prime Minister Alix Didier Fils-Aime in a phone call on Wednesday that he will deploy more than 2,000 troops to Haiti. He claimed the military surge is intended to rescue four missing Salvadoran soldiers and support anti-gang operations in the country, according to El Salvador's foreign ministry. Bukele has already sent hundreds of soldiers to the area. The Haitian prime minister's office confirmed the call.
* Separately, Haiti's government announced it would postpone planned presidential elections until next year. The country has not held national elections since 2016, and its last president was assassinated in 2021. Presidential elections have been repeatedly postponed under transitional administrations.
* **U.S. sanctions Rwanda defense ministry and Rwandan financial institution over the eastern Congo conflict:** The U.S. Treasury Department [announced](https://substack.com/redirect/d065baeb-d2e6-49a6-8eca-7b1d412649de?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) sanctions on Rwanda's defense ministry and on the Zigama Credit and Savings Society on Wednesday. The U.S. accused the defense ministry of directing the previously sanctioned Rwanda Defense Force to deploy thousands of troops to the Democratic Republic of the Congo. And the U.S. accused Zigama, which it said is linked to Rwanda's security services, of facilitating payments to Chinese and other entities for weapons, and of moving gold from rebel-held Congo to Rwanda. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said, "Rwanda must halt its support for M23 and withdraw its troops from eastern DRC." Rwanda denies backing the rebels, formerly AFC-M23. The Congolese government welcomed the sanctions.

This is Drop Site Daily, our free news recap We send it Monday - Friday Iran Vance requests renewed talks in letter to Iran 's security chief: Vice President JD Vance a letter to Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, proposing renewed direct negotiations as the Trump administration considers launching a short, intense military campaign against Iran after next week's U.S. midterm elections, the Wall Street Journal reported. The letter was delivered through Qatari mediators on Sunday. In it, Vance proposed a meeting as early as next week, to be potentially held in Qatar or Turkey. Vance would lead the U.S. delegation, the New York Times . Discussions have so far focused on a negotiating framework rather than specific terms, as Washington demands upfront nuclear concessions while Tehran seeks immediate economic relief. President Donald Trump confirmed on Wednesday that he had approved Vance's outreach, but he characterized it as an effort to facilitate medical supplies. "They need help with medical supplies and various things," Trump told reporters. "He asked me what I thought. I said, 'If you want to do that, that's OK.'" Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi on X: "While our Brave Armed Forces are fully prepared to defend the Homeland, Iran continues to give diplomacy a chance to succeed." He added that Tehran remained "in close and ongoing contact with intermediaries" to explore implementing Iran's seven-day plan "in even less than a week." AP: U.S. warns regional allies to prepare for possible renewed war in Iran: U.S. officials told several Middle East allies to prepare for renewed military action against Iran after the U.S. midterm elections next week, two diplomats briefed on the matter . The diplomatic sources told the AP that the U.S. informed regional allies that the new round of military action could last for several days, but regional officials are preparing for Iranian retaliation that could lead to a longer fight. U.S. officials urged regional allies to take precautionary measures against Iranian retaliatory strikes targeting energy facilities and other crucial infrastructure, according to AP. President Trump has not made a final decision on whether to carry out new strikes against Iran, the diplomats said. Iran claims three oil tankers struck mines near Strait of Hormuz: Three oil tankers after striking naval mines south of the Strait of Hormuz on Wednesday and Thursday, Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) Navy said on Thursday. The IRGC said the vessels had switched off their radar and navigation systems, ignored warnings, and attempted to pass through an "unauthorized" southern route. Separately, the UK Maritime Trade Operations said on Thursday that a ship had been spotted on fire nine nautical miles north of Khasab, Oman. The crew's condition, the extent of the damage, and the environmental impact remain unknown. IRGC spokesperson Hossein Mohebi reiterated that the Strait of Hormuz remains "under the strategic control of the Iranian armed forces and will never be opened until the Islamic Republic's conditions are fully met," in comments quoted by the Fars news agency on Thursday. Iran claims capture of one U.S. spy drone, downing of another over Hormuz: The IRGC on Thursday that it captured an intact U.S. MQM-170 reconnaissance and decoy drone west of the Strait of Hormuz. The IRGC electronic warfare unit allegedly took control of the aircraft's guidance systems and took it down. The IRGC said, without providing evidence, that the U.S. deployed the drone to identify Iranian air defense positions along the Persian Gulf coast and had taken off from an unnamed Gulf country. Separately, the IRGC said that it intercepted and destroyed a U.S. MQ-1 drone over the eastern Strait of Hormuz, the 14th MQ-1 drone it says it has shot down. The U.S. military has not commented on the IRGC's claims. Hegseth fires Pentagon 's top military planner: U.S. War Secretary Pete Hegseth Brett Sylvia, the Pentagon's top military planner. Sylvia served as director of strategy, plans, and policy on the Joint Staff, a key position responsible for coordinating military planning and advising the chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff and the president. A Pentagon official accused Sylvia of leaking classified information related to the wars in Iran and Ukraine, according to CBS News, though the allegations have not been independently substantiated. Sylvia's dismissal is the latest in a series of departures involving nearly two dozen senior military leaders under Hegseth. Palestine Israeli drone strike in central Gaza kills two Palestinians: Two Palestinians were killed and several others wounded on Thursday in an Israeli targeting a vehicle near the entrance to the Maghazi refugee camp in the central Gaza Strip, according to WAFA. Israeli forces demolish homes in the occupied West Bank as Hebron siege enters seventh day: Hebron: Israel's military assault its seventh consecutive day on Thursday, with more than 780 families affected and approximately 5,000 Palestinians forcibly displaced or confined to their homes, particularly in the sealed-off neighborhoods of Al-Jalda and Deir Bahha, WAFA reported. More than 115 Palestinians have been arrested since the operation began. Israeli restrictions have disrupted in-person education for an estimated 80,000 students across the governorate, with 66 schools directly affected. On Thursday, Israeli forces arrested seven Palestinians and injured two others during raids. In Tarqumiya, northwest of Hebron, Israeli bulldozers demolished an inhabited home, leaving seven family members homeless. Salfit: Israeli forces three homes in Deir Ballut and Bruqin. In the Wadi Al-Ahmar area, Israeli settlers stole olives from Palestinian farmland that owners had been prevented from accessing. Settlers fired live ammunition toward a Palestinian farmer who encountered them. Jericho: Israeli forces agricultural structures and bulldozed farmland east of Jericho. Ramallah and Al-Bireh: Israeli settlers Palestinian olive harvesters in Kafr Malik, northeast of Ramallah. Israeli settlers beat U.S. journalist and Russian activists in West Bank: Israeli settlers attacked U.S. journalist Jasper Nathaniel and two Russian activists in the Palestinian village of Umm Al-Khair in Masafer Yatta, in the occupied West Bank, before Israeli authorities arrested two of the victims, according to Russian activist Adele Shoko. Videos by Shoko show several men, some armed, beating Nathaniel and Russian activist Andrey X. "Andrey was severely beaten and lost consciousness several times in front of police," Shoko wrote, adding that he was denied hospital treatment and taken to a police station instead. "Jasper and I were also beaten. Jasper was then pepper-sprayed and arrested." Another video showed Nathaniel shouting, "I just got beat up," as Israeli forces led him away. Health Ministry stresses urgency of increased medical evacuations through Rafah: On Thursday, the Gaza Health Ministry reiterated its call for the opening of the Rafah crossing to allow for patients requiring medical treatment to leave and to increase the number of people allowed to travel on medical evacuations. "The successive and sudden closures of the crossings, and the deliberate slowness in the procedures, have turned the file of medical transfers from a humanitarian rescue path to a fatal obstacle; which caused a serious deterioration in the health conditions of thousands of wounded and sick, and the loss of dozens of them to their lives while waiting to be allowed to travel," the ministry said in a statement. Last week, Drop Site News that the entire functioning of the Rafah crossing was in jeopardy after the UN informed Palestinian officials that, beginning in mid-November, it would stop receiving Palestinians returning from Egypt and coordinating their entry into Gaza, citing the dangers facing returnees and repeated Israeli arrests. In response to inquiries from Drop Site, UN Public Information Officer Daria Carmon responded: "At this time we are reassessing the UN facilitated return operations into Gaza through Rafah crossing. We will make a public pronouncement about our position once the review is completed later this month. The UN remains fully committed to continue supporting medical evacuation missions through Rafah Crossing." Yemen Nearly 1,700 killed and 281,000 displaced in Yemen since August: At least 1,677 people have been killed and 7,395 injured in Yemen since August amid escalating fighting, according to the World Health Organization. Between October 20 and 25 alone, the WHO recorded 559 casualties, averaging approximately 93 killed or injured per day. More than 281,000 people have been by fighting in Yemen since the beginning of August, with over half sheltering in Taiz governorate, according to the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs. Humanitarian access has deteriorated over the past three weeks after damage to a key road connecting Taiz to southern governorates forced aid deliveries onto narrow mountain routes. Three-quarters of displaced Yemenis are sheltering in sites with inadequate water, sanitation, and shelter, while more than 35,000 families lack shelter assistance and over 230,000 people need emergency water and sanitation support. In Marib, only six of 31 mobile medical teams remain operational, and 15 health facilities have shut down entirely. Ansarallah reports 101 airstrikes by Saudi-backed forces across Yemen: Ansarallah 101 airstrikes by the Saudi-led coalition across the country over the past 24 hours, including strikes targeting the Dhubab and Mocha districts near the strategic Bab al-Mandab Strait. Separately, Saudi-backed Yemeni forces said that they carried out two airstrikes on an Ansarallah military camp in the al-Ash'oub area west of Taiz. Meanwhile, air traffic at Aden International Airport resumed following a sixth Ansarallah attack on the facility, which caused casualties and damage. The National Human Rights Authority in Sana'a said on Thursday that a Saudi strike on a paint factory near the city of Taiz caused a large fire and could release toxic gases and contaminate nearby soil and groundwater. It said that the attack was a war crime. HRW: Ansarallah depriving civilians of food, medicine in Taiz: Human Rights Watch on Thursday Ansarallah, also known as the Houthis, of endangering civilians in Taiz city by enforcing a siege on hundreds of thousands of residents in the city. "Renewed efforts by the Houthis to cut off food, water, and medicine to Taizz show their utter disregard for civilian lives,", Yemen and Bahrain researcher at Human Rights Watch, said in a statement. "Throughout the 12-year-long siege of [Taiz], the Houthis have bombed, starved, and denied humanitarian aid to a million residents of the city with scant adherence to international law." An Ansarallah spokesperson told Human Rights Watch that Saudi-backed government forces were blocking roads into the city. But residents, civil society workers, and United Nations officials blamed Ansarallah for the shortages, Human Rights Watch said. Lebanon Hezbollah leader calls Israeli election results "an expression of defeat," rejects disarmament: Israel's election results were "one of the expressions of defeat," Hezbollah Secretary-General Naim Qassem said on Wednesday, pointing to what he described as Israel's internal political, economic, and social crises. "We do not concern ourselves with who governs Israel, but let it be perfectly clear that it cannot continue its occupation and must leave our land," he said, vowing to continue resistance regardless of the election outcome. Qassem insisted there was "no room for discussion" about disarming Hezbollah as long as Israel continues its occupation and attacks on Lebanon, and called for an Israeli withdrawal under the November 2024 ceasefire agreement and UN Security Council Resolution 1701. He also declared the June 26 Lebanon-Israel framework agreement "null and void." Amid concerns that Hezbollah could enter another war in support of Iran, Qassem did not clarify whether the group would intervene if the U.S. or Israel launched new attacks, but said the U.S.-Iran agreement had helped reduce Israeli attacks on Lebanon. U.S. News DoorDash buys Instacart for $17 billion: The food delivery giant Doordash on Thursday that it purchased the grocery delivery app Instacart for $17 billion, the New York Times reported. It is DoorDash's largest acquisition to date. The deal could face antitrust scrutiny and pushback from grocers and gig workers. The deal is expected to close in 2027 or 2028. DoorDash completed 993 million orders in the third quarter, up 28%, while Instacart, once valued at $39 billion by private investors, has a market capitalization of about $14 billion and relationships with more than 2,200 retailers. Dolores Huerta, labor leader and civil rights figure who co-founded United Farm Workers, dies at 96: Labor and civil rights leader Dolores Huerta on Wednesday at her home in Bakersfield, Calif., of cancer, a family spokesman said. Alongside Cesar Chavez she founded the National Farm Workers Association in 1962, and led the 1960s and '70s strikes and boycotts that helped many California grape-growers consolidate worker power. She served as the union's vice president for nearly four decades. Over her working life, police arrested her 22 times. In 1988, she was severely beaten by a San Francisco police officer--a case settled by the city for $825,000. Huerta is widely believed to have coined the phrase "Si se puede." President Barack Obama awarded her the Presidential Medal of Freedom in 2012. In early 2026, she told the New York Times that Chavez raped her in 1966, and that two of her children resulted from sexual encounters with him. She is survived by 13 of her 14 children, 24 grandchildren, 23 great-grandchildren, and seven great-great-grandchildren. Fed holds rates steady: The Federal Reserve its benchmark rate at 3.75% to 4% on Wednesday, with governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack dissenting in favor of a quarter-point increase. The Fed rated economic activity as "strong," up from "solid." Traders see an 85% chance of a rate hike in December, according to CME's FedWatch Tool. Inflation has come in above target and Thursday's PCE report is expected to show a rate of 3.6% for the year through September. Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh said that starting next year, one of the eight annual Federal Open Market Committee meetings will focus solely on monetary policy strategy. It was Cook's first dissent, coming ahead of a White House hearing next week on Trump's bid to remove her over alleged mortgage fraud, which her lawyers call a pretext. Leak exposes records of more than 41,000 DHS employees and contractors, including undercover ICE agents: The transparency nonprofit Distributed Denial of Secrets an archive it calls "Icepick" on Wednesday, which contains the records of more than 41,000 DHS employees and contractors. In a press release, DDoSecrets said the information comes from DHS's Okta login system and was obtained by a group that calls itself the Department of Peace. That group attached a note that said, "They have our information, so it's only fair that we have theirs." The records, last updated on August 19, cover the DHS and seven component agencies, including emails, phone numbers, office addresses, supervisor names, and permission groups referencing undercover agents, and surveillance programs. DHS said it was working to address a potential security breach. Judge rejects Trump administration bid to set aside 20,000 California ballots: Judge David O. Carter , a Bill Clinton appointee, on Wednesday that the Trump administration's demand that California sequester 20,000 ballots "would wreak havoc and disrupt the election that is already underway" and "discount the votes of United States citizens." Carter wrote that "never before in American history has the federal government, on the eve of an election, sought to coerce a state and local government to abandon their own constitutional elections procedures." He noted that the Department of Justice has filed at least 31 suits seeking state voter rolls and has won "precisely zero" of the 26 suits decided so far. He called the DOJ's effort part of "a broad, ongoing pattern of attempted election interference." The DOJ immediately appealed the ruling. DOJ turned a rights-group informant into the government 's own: The rights group Southern Poverty Law Center said one of its informants was flipped by the Trump administration, and became a government informant, according to court papers the SPLC on Wednesday. SPLC lawyers said that the informant "F-9," who worked with the group from 1996 and was paid at least $1.2 million over 16 years, has met DOJ prosecutors more than 20 times since November 2025 under immunity, exchanged about 1,800 texts with FBI and IRS agents, and given at least four "intelligence briefings" to federal authorities as part of the DOJ's ongoing fraud case against the group. One of the informant's PowerPoint presentations bore FBI and IRS seals, as though "he were an actual member of the prosecution team," the SPLC filings said. The group requested that the court order the informant to preserve all documents, and to grant a subpoena for his materials. In April, the DOJ charged the SPLC with defrauding donors, alleging that the group funneled money to informants inside white-supremacist groups. Defense lawyers said that the case began after a coalition of right-leaning groups complained to senior White House advisor Stephen Miller about the SPLC's work. Trump administration issues more than 100 subpoenas for voter records in at least 13 states ahead of midterms: Reuters more than 100 subpoenas issued by the Trump administration, mostly in the past three months, to state and local election officials. The Trump administration sought records on tens of thousands of voters. The federal government targeted Democratic strongholds like Minneapolis, Philadelphia, and Los Angeles, and Republican-leaning Texas, Kansas, and Georgia. Legal experts told Reuters that the federal government could use the records to contest close election results. One expert said that the probes are "setting up" post-election challenges. California elites spend $612 million to defeat billionaire tax: Seventy past and current California billionaires have spent a record-setting $612 million to block a one-time, 5% tax on their wealth, . That spending has pushed support for the tax below 50%, . Company linked to Darline Graham 's husband was sanctioned for arming Russia against Ukraine: Lindsey Graham's central political ambition was to confront and contain Russia. The former South Carolina senator died within hours of returning from Ukraine, where he toured a drone factory as one of his last acts on his earth. His sister Darline Graham now holds his seat and is on the ballot next week. It turns out that her husband works for a company linked to a Chinese firm sanctioned in 2024 for providing sophisticated military tech to Russia. . CNN Senate poll finds Democrats up in Michigan, Kansas, Maine, and Texas: President Trump is heading to South Carolina to stave off Republican catastrophe there, while polls show potentially competitive races in Iowa, Nebraska, Florida, Mississippi, and Arkansas. Four from CNN put Democrats on top in critical races: Michigan Abdul El-Sayed (D): 49% Mike Rogers (R): 42% Kansas Adam Hamilton (D): 49% Roger Marshall (R): 45% Maine Troy Jackson (D): 49% Susan Collins (R): 45% Texas James Talarico (D): 49% Ken Paxton (R): 43% 📥 Have a tip on Capitol Hill? Email DC Correspondent Julian Andreone at Julian@dropsitenews.com Other International News Russian drone strike on Ukraine train station kills at least 14: A Russian jet-powered drone a busy train platform in Dnipro, Ukraine, on Thursday, killing at least 13 people. At least 14 others were injured in the attack, six of whom are in critical condition. Russian strikes also hit Kharkiv, damaging an educational institution, and a strike on the Rivne region killed one man. Fl avio Bolsonaro declares himself Brazil's rightful "leader" after arriving in Miami: Brazil's right-wing presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro, who left Brazil in secret after losing the election to Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, said in a Wednesday letter that he was the rightfully "elected president" of the country. He claimed that the Supreme court and Lula had carried out an "electoral coup" against him. He later amended the letter to say he was Brazil's "leader" and added that he "did not flee Brazil." He thanked Argentina's Javier Milei for helping him travel to the U.S., and thanked Trump for securing visas for him and his family. Pakistani court sentences human rights lawyers to 10 years in prison: A Pakistani anti-terrorism court prominent human rights lawyers Imaan Mazari and her husband, Hadi Ali Chattha, to 10 years in prison on Thursday. Their sentences will run concurrently with additional one-year and two-year sentences for obstructing and assaulting government servants. Mazari and her husband were accused of holding a protest in 2024 that blocked a road, and thereby endangered an international cricket team's security plans. They denied the charges, calling themselves "prisoners of conscience" targeted for their human rights work. Mazari's mother, Shireen Mazari, a former member of Imran Khan's cabinet, said that they were not allowed access to their lawyer or given key legal documents in the case. The couple had earlier been sentenced to 17 years in prison for social media posts. That sentence was suspended by Pakistan's Supreme Court--they were re-arrested for the 2024 protest on the same day. Clashes on Pakistan-Afghan border kill one: Clashes on the border of Afghanistan and Pakistan one person and injured five others, a Pakistani official said on Wednesday, accusing the Afghan Taliban of firing at civilian houses and a market in Pakistan's Waziristan region on Tuesday. He added that Pakistani forces would respond "effectively and heavily" to the attack. Afghan's Taliban government said Pakistan carried out four drone attacks on the district commissioner's office and nearby security facilities in Paktika province, and Afghan defense ministry spokesperson Sedeequllah Nasrat said Afghan forces retaliated against a nearby Pakistani military base, causing several casualties. Pakistan accuses Kabul of harboring militants who stage cross-border attacks, a charge the Afghan government denies. The conflict has killed hundreds of people this year. Drop Site's latest reporting on the clashes is available. South Korean prosecutors again seek death penalty for ex-President Yoon: South Korean prosecutors their effort to impose the death penalty on former President Yoon Suk-yeol at a Seoul High Court hearing on Thursday. Earlier this year, Yoon was convicted of leading an 2024 insurrection against the state. South Korea halted state executions in 1997, but prosecutors said that was "no reason to hesitate" in sending Yoon to his death. In January, prosecutors failed to secure a death penalty at Yoon's trial. He was sentenced to life in prison instead. Iraq PM visits Damascus: Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa on Wednesday. The two reportedly discussed exporting Iraqi oil through Syrian territory, boosting bilateral trade and joint agricultural development, Iraqi News Agency reported. Since the U.S.-led war on Iran began, Iraq has exported oil through Syria. In July, Iraq and Syria signed deals to revive the Haditha-Baniyas pipeline, entrusting a Chevron-led consortium to implement the deal. North Korea fires short-range ballistic missiles into Sea of Japan: North Korea about 10 missiles into the Sea of Japan on Thursday, South Korea's Defense Ministry said. The test firings come just days after South Korea proposed military talks with North Korea over a border dispute. In September, a landmine blast in the Demilitarized Zone separating North Korea and South Korea injured three South Korean soldiers, which joint South Korea-UN blamed on mines North Korea planted over a year ago. North Korea rejected the finding, and told the UN Security Council that South Korea fabricated the incident. El Salvador to send over 2,000 soldiers to Haiti, increasing military presence: Salvadoran President Nayib Bukele Haitian Prime Minister Alix Didier Fils-Aime in a phone call on Wednesday that he will deploy more than 2,000 troops to Haiti. He claimed the military surge is intended to rescue four missing Salvadoran soldiers and support anti-gang operations in the country, according to El Salvador's foreign ministry. Bukele has already sent hundreds of soldiers to the area. The Haitian prime minister's office confirmed the call. Separately, Haiti's government announced it would postpone planned presidential elections until next year. The country has not held national elections since 2016, and its last president was assassinated in 2021. Presidential elections have been repeatedly postponed under transitional administrations. U.S. sanctions Rwanda defense ministry and Rwandan financial institution over the eastern Congo conflict: The U.S. Treasury Department sanctions on Rwanda's defense ministry and on the Zigama Credit and Savings Society on Wednesday. The U.S. accused the defense ministry of directing the previously sanctioned Rwanda Defense Force to deploy thousands of troops to the Democratic Republic of the Congo. And the U.S. accused Zigama, which it said is linked to Rwanda's security services, of facilitating payments to Chinese and other entities for weapons, and of moving gold from rebel-held Congo to Rwanda. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said, "Rwanda must halt its support for M23 and withdraw its troops from eastern DRC." Rwanda denies backing the rebels, formerly AFC-M23. Hi Derek, it’s Dr.
Annie Andrews.

There’s a lot of new eyes on this campaign, so I wanted to take a second
to reintroduce myself.

I’m the Democratic nominee for the U.S. Senate in South Carolina. But
that’s not it.

I’m also a mom of three who does school pick ups and watches Bluey before
bed. I’m a pediatrician of twenty years. In other words, I’m not your
typical politician.

In fact, this is the last thing I ever thought I’d be doing. But I knew
someone had to step up for the people of South Carolina.

Our campaign is people-powered by grassroots donors like
you, Derek. I don't
have a network of wealthy donors or billionaire friends. I don't have
decades of political favors to call in.

What I do have is twenty years of sitting across from families in some of
the scariest moments of their lives, listening to what they actually need,
and trying to help.

That's the experience I'm bringing to this race. Not a perfect political
resume. A real life, spent in service to the people in this state.

[ https://act.joshshapiro.org/go/21812?t=1002&akid=841%2E245147%2E-8AUwS ]I’m running for the U.S. Senate to fight for the families, kids, and
communities that need someone in their corner. So, if you’re ready to win
in November, split a donation between my campaign and Josh Shapiro today.

name: Roy Cooper
subject: Taking a moment to say thanks.
body:
Trump’s not going to give up this seat without a fight. Neither will I.
| [](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1782&source=&t=1&akid=5066%2E124072%2EYwKpwz) | | | |
---
Peter, I just want to say – thank you, thank you, thank you.
You haven’t chipped in to my U.S. Senate campaign yet, but I appreciate that you’d take the time just to read my email.
Experts maintain that North Carolina is our best chance to flip a Senate seat blue this cycle, and momentum is on our side. In a state that hasn’t gone blue for a federal election since 2008, this wouldn’t be possible without grassroots supporters like you.
Now, the GOP is clearly panicking – but it’s not all good news:
* Both President Trump and Vice President Vance held rallies in North Carolina last week to put their thumbs on the scale for my MAGA opponent Michael Whatley – **and yesterday, Vance came back for his _fourth_ midterm rally with Whatley.**
* A super PAC with direct ties to Trump announced it’s launching new million-dollar ads attacking me for this final stretch.
* Donald Trump promised he’d join my MAGA opponent on the trail in NC one more time.
**Trump is undefeated in North Carolina, but so am I.** He’s not going to give up this seat without a fight, so we can’t let the positive polls and predictions lull us into complacency.
With only five days left to take on the MAGA machine and win, I need your help to continue building the biggest voter mobilization effort in state history. [**_So if you understand the stakes, I’m asking you to make your first donation to my grassroots campaign today – $5 or any amount will do. Will you please chip in to help me reach our critical end-of-month goal, win in North Carolina and flip the Senate blue?_**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1782&amount=5&t=8&akid=5066%2E124072%2EYwKpwz)

Roy Cooper

Democrat Roy Cooper is running for U.S. Senate to help take back the Majority for Democrats. North Carolina is Democrats’ best chance to flip a seat from red to blue — the path to stopping Republicans in Washington starts here.

National Republicans will target North Carolina as a key battleground and invest heavily in defeating us.

Cooper is a former state legislator, Attorney General, and most recently Governor of North Carolina. North Carolina will be the most competitive Senate election of 2026, and Cooper enters the race as the most formidable candidate of either party.
