_**First Hartford takes control of our neighborhoods. Then it tells Greenwich what to do with our taxes and schools. And somehow, our representatives still get to say they voted NO.**_
[](https://substack.com/redirect/62ef5521-c397-4b95-817a-ecf52d00a14f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
## I Called It Before the Debate. I Raised It at the Debate. Now Look What's Happening.
[Pledge your support](https://substack..Oc4m4MQx3fmmhjM3XXhQzQVU4qn8zB1DE-yQwfyKEjo?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=222653869)
[Share](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=1454853&post_id=222653869&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&utm_campaign=email-share&action=share&triggerShare=true&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MjIyNjUzODY5LCJpYXQiOjE3OTMyODc2MDIsImV4cCI6MTc5NTg3OTYwMiwiaXNzIjoicHViLTE0NTQ4NTMiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.Yt7uTl7FJLXr6cbUcCOu5frPg54MC9wGNtcaxaSkg7Y)
There is a political tradition in Hartford that Greenwich residents should understand.
I call it the **Hall Pass and the Full Moon.**
**The Hall Pass:** When a controversial bill already has enough votes to pass, a legislator can vote NO, go home, and tell constituents they opposed it. But what did they actually do to stop it?
**The Full Moon:** When Hartford turns its backside on Greenwich, takes away local decision-making power, and leaves our residents dealing with the consequences.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/269daf3b-1adc-4a22-8ccd-e9635fbfef56?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
It's a little political humor. But the consequences aren't funny.
And I've been warning about both throughout this campaign.
## The Hall Pass: A NO Vote Doesn't Tell the Whole Story
Let's look at the legislative record.
On May 27, 2025, Greenwich State Representative Steve Meskers voted YES on House Amendment B to HB 5002, a controversial housing bill.
Later that evening, he voted NO on the amended bill.
The bill passed the House anyway, 84-67.
Those are recorded votes, not speculation.
That bill was subsequently vetoed by Governor Lamont. But the housing debate did not end there. [My father and I wrote this as a father son piece back then.](https://substack.com/redirect/8976de94-85ab-485a-846e-1e9afcc4e29d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
In November 2025, Hartford enacted a different housing measure, HB 8002, which became Public Act 25-1. [We covered that too ](https://substack.com/redirect/df3e16a4-2c2f-4396-a71b-809cccc6855d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)as the father -son duo as we care about this state and built this Substack to over 23,000 people.
My criticism is not that every NO vote is meaningless. My criticism is that **a final NO vote is only part of the record.**
Did your representative challenge the bill? Debate its consequences? Offer amendments? Fight for sewer capacity, parking, local infrastructure, and municipal authority?
Or did the opposition end with a vote after the outcome was effectively decided?
I've called this a political _hall pass_. That's my characterization of a legislative practice--not a claim that anyone privately arranged a deal.
**A hall pass may get a politician off the hook. It doesn 't get Greenwich off the hook. That is where we stand in the 150th with your current representative - Just another seat at the table but no voice for Greenwich.**
## The Full Moon: Your Neighbor Sells. Hartford Changes the Rules.
Picture this.
You've lived in Greenwich for 20 or 30 years. You bought your home, raised your children, invested in your property, and chose your neighborhood for a reason.
Then your neighbor sells.
What gets built next door?
Should the answer come from Greenwich's Planning and Zoning Commission, applying local standards, or from state laws that limit what local officials can require?
Public Act 25-1 changes Connecticut's housing planning and zoning framework, including rules governing certain developments and minimum off-street parking requirements.
Not every home sale permits a large apartment building. Existing zoning and applicable legal requirements still matter. But the broader question is real: **How much authority should Greenwich retain over its own neighborhoods?**
What about traffic? Sewer capacity? Drainage? Schools? Parking?
Hartford may write the rules. Greenwich residents live with the results.
That's what I mean by the Full Moon.
**Hartford turns its backside on local concerns, and Greenwich gets the view.**
## And Now Hartford Is Looking at Your Taxes and Schools
On October 26, 2026, the CT Mirror reported that the Connecticut Citizens' Assembly on Property Taxes recommended proposals including highway tolls, a surcharge on high incomes, incentives for school regionalization, and changes to special education financing.
These are recommendations, not enacted laws. The assembly also proposed measures intended to reduce municipal burdens, including greater state support for special education.
But these recommendations raise questions that I believe Greenwich should confront now, not after legislation is drafted.
Who decides how our schools are organized?
Will local taxpayers receive genuine property tax relief, or will one set of taxes simply replace another?
Will Greenwich retain control of education and development decisions?
And will state lawmakers be willing to challenge proposals from their own leadership?
I warned that Hartford's expansion into local zoning could be followed by more debates over local fiscal and educational control.
**Now those debates are on the table.**
That is what I meant when I said I called it.
I did not predict every recommendation. I predicted the larger conflict over who controls Greenwich's future.
## Greenwich Is Not Stamford
Stamford is a city. Its density, development needs, transportation network, and municipal priorities are different.
Greenwich has different neighborhoods, infrastructure, and planning needs.
Housing affordability is a legitimate concern. So is the need to provide opportunities for younger residents, working families, and seniors.
But housing policy must account for the infrastructure necessary to support growth.
We cannot simply look at how many housing units a sewer system can accommodate in dry weather while ignoring what happens during a heavy rainstorm.
We already have concerns about sewage entering Long Island Sound and beach closures.
Development decisions and infrastructure planning belong in the same conversation.
**One size does not fit all.**
## I'd Rather Make Noise at the Kids' Table Than Sit Quietly at the Grown-Ups' Table
I've said throughout this campaign that I may be part of the minority in Hartford.
I understand that.
But I've also raised an important question: Have you ever heard how much noise kids can make at the kids' table?
Sometimes they make so much noise that the grown-ups have to stop talking and pay attention.
That's the kind of representation I'm talking about.
As an attorney, I've negotiated with people who had more leverage than I did. In construction, I know that problems don't disappear because someone refuses to acknowledge them.
You challenge the assumptions. You ask the uncomfortable questions. You demand answers. You put alternatives on the table.
And you make sure that the people making decisions cannot say nobody warned them.
**I would rather be heard from the minority table than sit quietly at the majority table.**
## No More Hall Passes. No More Full Moons.
My priorities remain simple:
**A -- Affordability:** Address outrageous utility costs, eliminate the Public Benefits Charge from electricity bills, and pursue a temporary gas and diesel tax holiday.
**B -- Beaches:** Address sewage pollution, infrastructure failures, and beach closures affecting Long Island Sound.
**C -- Local Control:** Protect Greenwich's voice in zoning, development, infrastructure, and education decisions.
**I 'm not going to Hartford to ask for a hall pass. **
I'm going to Hartford to ask questions, challenge bad bills, offer alternatives, and make sure Greenwich is heard. I may have to go up there with a hard hat and safety glasses - but that's what PPE is all about and a good pair of boots
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/ae015a87-3606-4add-9443-8948fba85589?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
And when Hartford gives us the Full Moon, I won't pretend the sun is shining.
**Greenwich deserves more than a representative who can say he voted NO. Greenwich deserves a representative who makes sure its concerns are heard before the vote.**
I'm Jonathan Goldstein, and I'm asking for the opportunity to represent Greenwich in Hartford.
**Not Red. Not Blue. Just Greenwich.**
**Jonathan Goldstein | Vote 4B -- Row B**

Then it tells Greenwich what to do with our taxes and schools. And somehow, our representatives still get to say they voted NO. I Called It Before the Debate. I Raised It at the Debate. Now Look What's Happening. There is a political tradition in Hartford that Greenwich residents should understand. I call it the Hall Pass and the Full Moon. The Hall Pass: When a controversial bill already has enough votes to pass, a legislator can vote NO, go home, and tell constituents they opposed it. But what did they actually do to stop it? The Full Moon: When Hartford turns its backside on Greenwich, takes away local decision-making power, and leaves our residents dealing with the consequences. | | ---|---|--- It's a little political humor. But the consequences aren't funny. And I've been warning about both throughout this campaign. The Hall Pass: A NO Vote Doesn't Tell the Whole Story Let's look at the legislative record. On May 27, 2025, Greenwich State Representative Steve Meskers voted YES on House Amendment B to HB 5002, a controversial housing bill. Later that evening, he voted NO on the amended bill. The bill passed the House anyway, 84-67. Those are recorded votes, not speculation. That bill was subsequently vetoed by Governor Lamont. But the housing debate did not end there. In November 2025, Hartford enacted a different housing measure, HB 8002, which became Public Act 25-1. the father -son duo as we care about this state and built this Substack to over 23,000 people. My criticism is not that every NO vote is meaningless. My criticism is that a final NO vote is only part of the record. Did your representative challenge the bill? Debate its consequences? Offer amendments? Fight for sewer capacity, parking, local infrastructure, and municipal authority? Or did the opposition end with a vote after the outcome was effectively decided? I've called this a political hall pass. That's my characterization of a legislative practice--not a claim that anyone privately arranged a deal. A hall pass may get a politician off the hook. It doesn 't get Greenwich off the hook. That is where we stand in the 150th with your current representative - Just another seat at the table but no voice for Greenwich. The Full Moon: Your Neighbor Sells. Hartford Changes the Rules. Picture this. You've lived in Greenwich for 20 or 30 years. You bought your home, raised your children, invested in your property, and chose your neighborhood for a reason. Then your neighbor sells. What gets built next door? Should the answer come from Greenwich's Planning and Zoning Commission, applying local standards, or from state laws that limit what local officials can require? Public Act 25-1 changes Connecticut's housing planning and zoning framework, including rules governing certain developments and minimum off-street parking requirements. Not every home sale permits a large apartment building. Existing zoning and applicable legal requirements still matter. But the broader question is real: How much authority should Greenwich retain over its own neighborhoods? What about traffic? Sewer capacity? Drainage? Schools? Parking? Hartford may write the rules. Greenwich residents live with the results. That's what I mean by the Full Moon. Hartford turns its backside on local concerns, and Greenwich gets the view. And Now Hartford Is Looking at Your Taxes and Schools On October 26, 2026, the CT Mirror reported that the Connecticut Citizens' Assembly on Property Taxes recommended proposals including highway tolls, a surcharge on high incomes, incentives for school regionalization, and changes to special education financing. These are recommendations, not enacted laws. The assembly also proposed measures intended to reduce municipal burdens, including greater state support for special education. But these recommendations raise questions that I believe Greenwich should confront now, not after legislation is drafted. Who decides how our schools are organized? Will local taxpayers receive genuine property tax relief, or will one set of taxes simply replace another? Will Greenwich retain control of education and development decisions? And will state lawmakers be willing to challenge proposals from their own leadership? I warned that Hartford's expansion into local zoning could be followed by more debates over local fiscal and educational control. Now those debates are on the table. That is what I meant when I said I called it. I did not predict every recommendation. I predicted the larger conflict over who controls Greenwich's future. Greenwich Is Not Stamford Stamford is a city. Its density, development needs, transportation network, and municipal priorities are different. Greenwich has different neighborhoods, infrastructure, and planning needs. Housing affordability is a legitimate concern. So is the need to provide opportunities for younger residents, working families, and seniors. But housing policy must account for the infrastructure necessary to support growth. We cannot simply look at how many housing units a sewer system can accommodate in dry weather while ignoring what happens during a heavy rainstorm. We already have concerns about sewage entering Long Island Sound and beach closures. Development decisions and infrastructure planning belong in the same conversation. One size does not fit all. I'd Rather Make Noise at the Kids' Table Than Sit Quietly at the Grown-Ups' Table I've said throughout this campaign that I may be part of the minority in Hartford. I understand that. But I've also raised an important question: Have you ever heard how much noise kids can make at the kids' table? Sometimes they make so much noise that the grown-ups have to stop talking and pay attention. That's the kind of representation I'm talking about. As an attorney, I've negotiated with people who had more leverage than I did. In construction, I know that problems don't disappear because someone refuses to acknowledge them. You challenge the assumptions. You ask the uncomfortable questions. You demand answers. You put alternatives on the table. And you make sure that the people making decisions cannot say nobody warned them. I would rather be heard from the minority table than sit quietly at the majority table. No More Hall Passes. No More Full Moons. My priorities remain simple: A -- Affordability: Address outrageous utility costs, eliminate the Public Benefits Charge from electricity bills, and pursue a temporary gas and diesel tax holiday. B -- Beaches: Address sewage pollution, infrastructure failures, and beach closures affecting Long Island Sound. C -- Local Control: Protect Greenwich's voice in zoning, development, infrastructure, and education decisions. I 'm not going to Hartford to ask for a hall pass. I'm going to Hartford to ask questions, challenge bad bills, offer alternatives, and make sure Greenwich is heard. I may have to go up there with a hard hat and safety glasses - but that's what PPE is all about and a good pair of boots | | ---|---|--- And when Hartford gives us the Full Moon, I won't pretend the sun is shining. Greenwich deserves more than a representative who can say he voted NO. Greenwich deserves a representative who makes sure its concerns are heard before the vote. I'm Jonathan Goldstein, and I'm asking for the opportunity to represent Greenwich in Hartford. Not Red. Not Blue. Just Greenwich. Time and again, she started her answer by saying she agreed with her opponent. On the Iran war, she said “I agree that the president did not have a good plan.” She’s been in the Senate since 1997 and is asking for a sixth term, something no senator from Maine has ever won. Her opponent Troy Jackson is a fifth generation logger from Allagash and a former President of the Maine Senate. He isn’t backed by corporate PACs or billionaire donors. | | | | The very first question at that debate was how to bring down heating costs in Maine. The war has pushed heating oil and gas prices up across the state, right as winter sets in. Agreeing it was a bad plan doesn’t lower anyone’s oil bill. A New York Times analysis of her record found her votes against Trump have rarely stopped anything. name: Adam Ukman, The Dads Initiative
subject: What We Learned about Connecting with Dads this Year
body:
Some of our favorite moments from this year, and a giveaway for one lucky family.

| | | | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/4ebf2177ef6d/the-dads-initiatives-second-show-cart-talk-7232753?e=7e921d898f)
---
| | | | Hi Peter,
I’m Adam, and I run The Dads Initiative at ParentsTogether. We make entertaining shows, conduct research, and drive conversations for dads trying to show up well for their families, even when nobody gave them the playbook.
As we near the end of the year, I wanted to share a few things that stuck with me in 2026:
1. **Dads really love to talk about being dads.** On Cart Talk, we put dads in a golf cart and they open up about their own fathers, the pressure to provide, and what they’d do differently. If you haven’t seen it, this episode with author [Tom](https://us.list-manage.com/QQBXF6lgIZg?e=7e921d898f&c2id=e37e4accfbad4ed1f05c4cddb6e361bf)[ ](https://us.list-manage.com/1ICtvdB28sX?e=7e921d898f&c2id=e37e4accfbad4ed1f05c4cddb6e361bf)[Coyne](https://us.list-manage.com/Z2ou3IpE0nL?e=7e921d898f&c2id=e37e4accfbad4ed1f05c4cddb6e361bf) is a good place to start.

2. **Small habits matter.** On [Reset Mode](https://us.list-manage.com/he3o1C6Q0sD?e=7e921d898f&c2id=e37e4accfbad4ed1f05c4cddb6e361bf), creator Sidney Raskind talks about modeling a love of reading for his kid. Kids learn more from what we do than from what we say.

3. **Dads have something to say about the world our kids deserve.** After the Cornell 7 news, hundreds of dads signed our Open Letter committing to do better as men and fathers. [You can still read and sign it](https://us.list-manage.com/lp7n2Nia5iz?e=7e921d898f&c2id=e37e4accfbad4ed1f05c4cddb6e361bf).

---
| | **Enter our Giveaway** To celebrate the year, we’ve partnered with child furniture brand **dadada** to give one family a [toddler tower](https://us.list-manage.com/SpBTMO0KNYD?e=7e921d898f&c2id=e37e4accfbad4ed1f05c4cddb6e361bf). As a toddler dad myself, I can tell you it’s a game changer. To enter, just [comment on this post](https://us.list-manage.com/vPYU4THt6x8?e=7e921d898f&c2id=e37e4accfbad4ed1f05c4cddb6e361bf) and follow [@ResetModeShow](https://us.list-manage.com/67vFXQaM1jA?e=7e921d898f&c2id=e37e4accfbad4ed1f05c4cddb6e361bf) and [@Dadadababyusa](https://us.list-manage.com/18TXFncAIRa?e=7e921d898f&c2id=e37e4accfbad4ed1f05c4cddb6e361bf) on Instagram by November 15.
---
| [Comment on this post to enter the giveaway](https://us.list-manage.com/1D0ibck5rL7?e=7e921d898f&c2id=e37e4accfbad4ed1f05c4cddb6e361bf)
---
| | **What’s Next
** In 2027 we’re launching new shows with creators dads already trust, and building something bigger around Father’s Day. Before then, I’d love to know: what’s a conversation about being a dad you wish more men were having? Just hit reply. I read these.
---
| | Wishing you and your family a good Thanksgiving and a restful holiday season.
AdamFounder, The Dads Initiative
P.S. Don’t forget to [enter](https://us.list-manage.com/IPp9Atj4Z6a?e=7e921d898f&c2id=e37e4accfbad4ed1f05c4cddb6e361bf) the toddler tower giveaway before November 15!

On Cart Talk, we put dads in a golf cart and they open up about their own fathers, the pressure to provide, and what they’d do differently. If you haven’t seen it, this episode with author is a good place to start. 2. Small habits matter. On , creator Sidney Raskind talks about modeling a love of reading for his kid. Kids learn more from what we do than from what we say. 3. Dads have something to say about the world our kids deserve. After the Cornell 7 news, hundreds of dads signed our Open Letter committing to do better as men and fathers. . | | Enter our Giveaway To celebrate the year, we’ve partnered with child furniture brand dadada to give one family a . As a toddler dad myself, I can tell you it’s a game changer. To enter, just and follow and on Instagram by November 15. | | | What’s Next In 2027 we’re launching new shows with creators dads already trust, and building something bigger around Father’s Day. Before then, I’d love to know: what’s a conversation about being a dad you wish more men were having? Just hit reply. I've seen the hurt that this district has gone through over the past few years because of leaders like Ben Cline and Donald Trump. The Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee just announced that VA-06 is officially a district in play!= = When I got into this race, I heard a lot of people say, "Bless your heart, young lady." And I get it. Twelve months ago, flipping this ruby-red seat may have seemed impossible. But thanks to folks like you, we've built a movement that puts the impossible within reach. I've seen the hurt that this district has gone through over the past few years because of leaders like Ben Cline and Donald Trump. They are responsible for the rising costs for farmers, veterans losing their benefits, and families in the VA-06 going hungry because of SNAP cuts. I got into this race because I knew we could win. People here are sick of the inaction and hyper-partisan politics infecting our district. VA-06 deserves a leader who will deliver results, not empty promises. That's why the DCCC named us as a district in play, and it's why we have momentum on our side going into Election Day. Together, we've built a movement for change up and down 81. And we're ready to win on November 3. Here's the deal: this is the last week of the campaign. It's now or never. | | It’s time to make our voices heard, our values count, and our votes matter! Washington may make the headlines, but moms shape the future. We’re raising the next generation, protecting our families, and working hard every day to keep America strong. Now it’s time to take that same determination to the ballot box. From parental rights and our children’s futures to girls’ sports, border security, and the freedoms we hold dear, the decisions made by our elected leaders affect every family. We can’t afford to sit this one out.

Talk to your friends, sisters, neighbors, and fellow moms. Encourage two other women to make their voices heard, too. We don’t have to agree on everything to recognize that our participation matters. When moms show up, our communities benefit from having more voices engaged in shaping our future. Mommas, America needs you! Let’s lead by example, stand firm in our values, and make sure our voices are part of the decisions that will shape the next generation.With purpose and determination, let’s make our voices count!

body:
We stand by our reporting.

We stand by our reporting.

View in Web Browser
[https://link.email.freethinkerdaily.com/click/e9772510/UaHR0cHM6Ly9vZGIubnVjbGV1c2VtYWlsLmNvbS9hbXBsaWZ5L3YvdmRxbUVwR0NuMw/SZW1haWxfZnJlZXRoaW5rZXJkYWlseV9jb20yNjEwMjk/LbmNsckdQdTVEbw/qP2hpZHM9bmNqa1l1dktsdFczdjBsc10/gauNzKQ/s3vbd602a9c

[Statement: Minnesota charged me with two felonies. I never settle.
Stand with James.]
[https://link.email.freethinkerdaily.

Dear Patriot,

Minnesota charged both myself and fellow journalist Cam Higby with two
felony counts in retaliation for our bombshell investigative report on
voter vouching laws that we did back in August.

WE STAND BY OUR REPORTING.

I recorded a statement on these charges, and I WANT YOU TO WATCH IT
AND STAND WITH ME
[https://link.email.freethinkerdaily.

[Watch: James O'Keefe statement on Minnesota felony charges. Watch
and stand with James.]
[https://link.email.freethinkerdaily.

The charges are an attempt to criminalize investigative journalism.
The charges are an attempt to distract from what our reporting exposed
as insecure elections in Minnesota. Now, this has become a landmark
1st Amendment case where EVERYONE'S RIGHT TO SPEAK TRUTH TO POWER HAS
JUST BEEN PUT ON THE LINE
[https://link.email.freethinkerdaily.

Hennepin County Attorney Mary Moriarty led a press conference
regarding these charges.

“Today we are charging two individuals, James O'Keefe and Cameron
Higby, with felony counts of unlawful voting and identity theft.”
— MORIARTY

She also said that Cam and I could do some local jail time for our
investigative reporting.

We received a charging document that lists two felony counts.

COUNT I
Identity Theft
Knowingly misrepresented his identity in applying for a voting ballot

COUNT II
Unlawful Voting
Knowingly misrepresented his identity in applying for a voting ballot

TWO COUNTS WITH THE EXACT SAME JUSTIFICATION BENEATH EACH COUNT.

In our report, we clearly stopped and walked out of the polling places
to avoid even touching a voting ballot.

Moriarty even said it herself. She admitted that my and Higby's intent
was to act as investigative reporters.

“A group of people were attempting to cast doubt on the state's
vouching system. I think it's pretty clear they did not intend to
vote.”
— MORIARTY

They admit we didn't vote. They charged us anyway. WATCH MY STATEMENT
AND STAND WITH ME.
[https://link.email.freethinkerdaily.

Moriarty also said there is no such thing as undercover journalism
when looking into election loopholes.

“If you identify as a journalist, there is no such thing as
undercover investigation in the polling place. You have to identify
yourself as a journalist in the polling place, which they did not.”
— MORIARTY

MORIARTY IS WRONG AS A MATTER OF CONSTITUTIONAL LAW.

The 1st Amendment allows reporters to show up on Election Day and ask
questions at polling booths.

But don't take my word for it. In 2012, former Attorney General of the
United States Eric Holder went under oath in Washington, D.C.
discussing an almost identical investigation asking if the polling
official has Eric Holder's ballot at a precinct on primary day there.

“What I drew from that video was that [O'Keefe] was very careful not
to say that he was Eric Holder, not to actually get a ballot. He
didn't do the kinds of things that would have subjected him to
criminal prosecution.”
— ERIC HOLDER

In today's press conference, Moriarty points out this distinction,
too.

“So, there's a difference between intent to vote and intent to apply
for a ballot. The application of a ballot is a multi-step process. I
can't anticipate what [O'Keefe and Higby's] defense is. I'm sure we'll
hear from them.”
— MORIARTY

OUR DEFENSE IS THE SHIELD OF THE 1ST AMENDMENT TO HOLD GOVERNMENT
ACCOUNTABLE TO THE PEOPLE.

We didn't apply for a ballot; we were there talking to election
clerks, posing hypotheticals, and getting answers so that Americans
could know what was happening in the elections.

Many people in the United States did not even know about vouching for
eight, and this investigative report educated them.

By the way, we conducted training and specifically told each
journalist NEVER TO SIGN AN AFFIDAVIT, NEVER TO PROCURE A BALLOT,
NEVER TO EVEN TOUCH A BALLOT.

We even did exercises training the journalists to say “the name
is” rather than “my name is.” We were very intentional about
what we were there to do, namely was to inform the public.

Moriarty admitted that we stopped short of signing any oath or
carrying out any fraud.

“Both men stopped short of signing the oath we all sign before
receiving our ballot.”
— MORIARTY

The reporters in the room questioned Moriarty on what exactly we're
being prosecuted for.

“Does that give them a way to say that we didn't commit a crime
because we didn't take it all the way? ... Can you explain why you
think it's still a crime?”
— A REPORTER AT THE PRESS CONFERENCE

So again, what exactly are we being prosecuted for? What is this
really about?

MAKE NO MISTAKE, THIS IS ABOUT PROSECUTING THE PRESS, AND THIS ISN'T
THE FIRST TIME SOMETHING LIKE THIS HAS HAPPENED TO ME.

STAND WITH JAMES →
[https://link.email.freethinkerdaily.

In New Orleans, LA, they falsely accused me of a felony and later
admitted there was no felony. The U.S. attorneys involved in that case
were eventually disbarred.

The federal prosecutor was so furious about this case that he
literally threw my book at me.

“You're a nasty, little, cowardly spud. You are scum! I recused from
your case!”
— PROSECUTOR JIM LETTEN

Then there was the case when the FBI came knocking at my house. Agents
stormed into my home and unlocked my phone to get access to my Signal
in order to intimidate me and to intimidate the sources that come to
me.

It was such a landmark First Amendment case that the American Civil
Liberties Union (ACLU) filed amicus, and the Reporters Committee for
Freedom of the Press came to my defense.

I have been to the Ninth Circuit Court of Appeals, challenging the
constitutionality of Oregon's recording laws. Got a reversal there.

I went up to the 1st Circuit Court of Appeals in Massachusetts there.
We won a partial victory.

In another civil case, Shirley Teter v. O'Keefe, I won at directed
verdict. For that case, there were six pro-bono lawyers representing
the plaintiff, who stated, “We're not paid by the Hillary Clinton
campaign or by the Democratic Party or anything like that.” The
federal judge pointed out the unsolicited statement only raised
further questions, and ordered them to pay my legal fees.

I have been sued so many times and have had so many criminal threats
made against me that even the media that hates me is forced to
acknowledge that I have established legal 1st Amendment precedent
throughout the nation.

We also overturned a jury verdict against me in the D.C. Circuit Court
of Appeals last month before a panel of judges, which were appointed
by Democrats. We convinced the panel to side with the 1st Amendment,
creating a new standard for undercover journalism across the board.

It's now called the “O'KEEFE PRINCIPLE.” On publication injury
when undercover journalism is involved.

I've won these fights before. STAND WITH ME AND HELP ME WIN THIS ONE.
[https://link.email.freethinkerdaily.

The politics of fear and weaponized lawfare don't seem to work against
me. It never has. Actually, it has always backfired against the people
who come after me.

Why is that? It's because what's at issue here is not actually
political; it's fundamental.

This is about whether citizens still have a right to ask questions of
their government servants, and such a fundamental right will always
prevail if you do not cower at their threats.

AND THE THING ABOUT ME IS — I NEVER SETTLE.

Most people find lawsuits stressful. The process becomes a form of
punishment, but not to me. I actually love this process.

I enjoy this process.

I'm going to have fun with this process.

Because it allows me to expose injustice at the highest levels.

THERE IS NOTHING AS SWEET AS JUSTICE, AND THERE IS NOTHING AS
MOTIVATING AS INJUSTICE.

And in this case, they have put your right to speak on the line.
EVERYTHING WE BELIEVE IN AS AMERICANS HAS BEEN PUT ON THE LINE.
[https://link.email.freethinkerdaily.

But it does seem to indicate the direction of where our country is
going.

I recognize that we're well past the point of being completely divided
in this country, but this case isn't about what divides us; it's about
what unites us. What unites us is so much stronger than what divides
us. Because the right to question authority and educate people matters
to people on all sides.

Ironically, Moriarty put out a statement on social media and
restricted the comments section on her official X government account,
which violates the 1st Amendment.

And now, I'm summoned to appear before the Hennepin County judge on
Monday, Nov. 16th, just four days after our Citizen Journalism Gala,
where we'll host many people who don't all agree with each other on
public policy. And yet, each of them all stands united behind the 1st
Amendment.

[https://link.email.freethinkerdaily.

SUMMONED TO APPEAR
MONDAY, NOV. 16
Hennepin County, Minnesota
TWO FELONY COUNTS • I NEVER SETTLE

That's why I'm calling on all Americans, and not just independent
journalists, but especially those in the mainstream or legacy media
institutions, TO STAND WITH US FOR THE RIGHT TO FREEDOM OF SPEECH
[https://link.email.freethinkerdaily.

And to send a message to the prosecutors in Minnesota that politics of
fear will not prevail in the United States of America.

PLEASE STAND WITH ME TODAY WITH WHATEVER YOU CAN GIVE.
[https://link.email.freethinkerdaily.

$35

$50

$100
[https://link.email.freethinkerdaily.

[https://link.email.freethinkerdaily.

OTHER
[https://link.email.freethinkerdaily.

I STAND WITH JAMES →
[https://link.email.freethinkerdaily.

Thank you for everything you do.

In Truth,

[James O'Keefe signature]
JAMES O'KEEFE
Founder, O'Keefe Media Group

did not intend to vote.” They charged us with two felonies anyway,
and I'm due in a Hennepin County courtroom on Nov. 16. WATCH MY
STATEMENT AND STAND WITH ME.

| | | Peter, President Trump is coming to Kansas on _Saturday_ for yet another rally with my opponent. This tells us two things: **1)** Washington insiders are paying close attention to this race because they know we can win; and**2)** They’re about to pour _even more_ resources into defeating us. That’s why this is so alarming: I just reviewed the latest numbers, and Roger Marshall and his GOP super PAC allies are spending nearly $30 million to drown us out in the final stretch. They’re blanketing the airwaves with attack ads against me in every corner of the state. This comes at the worst possible moment – Kansans are already casting their ballots and if even more dark-money comes in for Marshall, it could deter the voters we critically need to flip this Senate seat. **That’s why my team set a nonnegotiable rapid response goal of $250,000 — but I’m worried we won’t reach it unless folks step up today.** [**Can I count on you to chip in $25 or $50 right now between our campaign and****Equal Opportunity Now**** to help us hit our final end-of-month goal and fight back?**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142453846/656977971/1996485280?amount=25&refcode=261029_hamilton_trump&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDUvMS83MzE2OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI0NDMxMWJlMi1iNGQzLWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDIyNDgyNGQ0ZGIiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=OlOHa54eQ6Um-or2HO85TEdCWrxRQgbBUfzFI74uTtI=)

In just the last several weeks of this race, we turned a formerly “Safe Republican” seat into a toss-up. We’re tied with Sen. Marshall in the polls, but we can’t pull ahead if his super PACs start upping their million-dollar advertising buys filled with lies in the final days before Election Day. Here’s the hard truth: _The President coming back to Kansas is just the beginning_. Marshall and his corporate PAC allies will do everything in their power to stop our momentum. **I’m running for Senate to be a champion for hardworking Kansans — to listen to and work for Kansans every single day in the Senate. Our momentum is surging, but we can’t compete if we let Marshall’s money drown us out. > _-> You don't want a Senate run by Chuck Schumer.
> -> You don't want Elizabeth Warren to chair the Senate Banking Committee.
> -> And you don't want Bernie Sanders setting environmental policy that kills jobs in South Carolina._
That's the radical Democrat agenda, _and it's what Annie Andrews would be voting for._

She's raised over $25 million - nearly $4 million in the last couple of weeks - from liberal donors who don't share South Carolina's values. **She built her campaign attacking Lindsey, and now her whole mission is to defeat his sister.**

clean_body: I just left South Carolina. This race is neck and neck, and Darline needs us now. | Fellow Patriot, On Monday, I was in South Carolina, on the campaign trail with Darline Graham. I want to tell you what I saw, because this race is closer than anyone in Washington wants to admit. It is neck and neck. Election Day is less than a week away, and Darline's seat could swing either way. Here's what I told the folks there: -> You don't want a Senate run by Chuck Schumer. -> You don't want Elizabeth Warren to chair the Senate Banking Committee. -> And you don't want Bernie Sanders setting environmental policy that kills jobs in South Carolina. That's the radical Democrat agenda, and it's what Annie Andrews would be voting for. She's raised over $25 million - nearly $4 million in the last couple of weeks - from liberal donors who don't share South Carolina's values. She built her campaign attacking Lindsey, and now her whole mission is to defeat his sister. Darline stands for common sense: low taxes, good jobs, and backing the police. She won't vote to put violent criminals back on the street or to let boys compete in girls' sports. She has thirty years of experience working for the people of her state, and she has a backbone. What Darline doesn't have is Hollywood money. Schumer needs JUST FOUR SEATS to take the majority, and he's betting South Carolina hands him one because Darline is being outspent after running two elections back-to-back. Fellow Patriot, races this close are decided in the final days by who can stay on the air, keep volunteers knocking doors, and get voters to the polls. They tried this playbook on me in Texas. National Democrats dumped millions to attack me because they thought the bigger bank account would win. Now I'm making a personal plea: show up for Darline. | | | | | | We have less than a week. Let's not sit this one out. | | Friend,

Yesterday, California lost a generational leader. Dolores Heurta, co-founder of the United Farm Workers, passed away at 96.

Dolores proved that working people can overcome monied special interests when we work together. For seventy years, she showed up again and again when the odds told her she was not likely to win. And time and time again, she united workers to demand the dignity that every human being deserves, and won.

Before she organized California's farmworkers, she was a schoolteacher in Stockton. After seeing her students come to class hungry, she recognized that the best way to support her students was to organize their parents and help them win better working conditions and fair wages.

Her legacy lives on in the lives of countless California farmworkers who enjoy better wages, disability insurance, and workplace rights thanks to her tireless advocacy and organizing chops.

Every organizer in America stands on the shoulders of her work. I know I do.

**_[In lieu of flowers or gifts, Dolores asked that contributions be made to the Dolores Huerta Foundation, which is training the next generation of organizers in the Central Valley.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142455042/656981746/1070461035?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDQ0NDUiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiMDkyNTQxZTAtYjdkMy1mMTExLWJmNWItMDAyMjQ4MjRkNGRiIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=77LKZkaTEMj4i0Q5XsADFcAX2s6zeU44mz-4ETCd3Ns=&emci=c0f0e4b4-b4d3-f111-bf5b-00224824d4db&emdi=092541e0-b7d3-f111-bf5b-00224824d4db&ceid=22554739)_**

Her wisdom, her work, her spirit will live in the people she guided and the movements she inspired, always.

Rest in power, Dolores.

In solidarity,

Lateefah

If you haven’t signed up yet, here are links for each of the virtual events — and remember, you don’t need any training or experience! → → → → I hope to see you shortly!—Sara \------- Forwarded message ------From: Sara Jacobs <info@sarajacobsforca.com> Date: Wed, Oct 28, 2026 Subject: I’ll be on 4 virtual phone banks tomorrow. Join me? Hi friends — we’re coming down to the wire with just six days left to go until Election Day, and it’s all hands on deck. From Arizona to Florida to Michigan to Georgia, I’ve been criss-crossing the country to support my colleagues facing tough races, and my hopefully-soon-to-be-colleagues fighting to flip red seats. I’m so excited to be helping as many Democrats as I can in these final days! Tomorrow, Thursday 10/29, I’ll be joining four (yes, 4!) virtual phone banks to kick off voter outreach in targeted battleground districts, and I’d love for you to join me. This is a great chance to channel any of that pesky midterm anxiety into action that will help us get the results we all want — plus, calling voters can be a lot of fun! Click the links below to sign up for a phone bank (or two, or even all four), and let’s get ready to win: All you’ll need to participate in these phone banks is a phone, a laptop or tablet, and a comfortable place to sit! No experience necessary — training will be provided during the event. We’re on the brink of huge victories, but we need to see it through to the finish, so I hope you’ll join me in taking action to support these Democrats who really need more help. ### Senate Update: Bringing Down Costs while Fighting a Lawless and Corrupt Administration
This fall, we face challenges on a number of fronts: families across the country continue to be squeezed by rising prices, the Trump Administration is escalating its attacks on our elections, and unchecked advances in artificial intelligence pose growing risks to our safety, security, and workforce. At the same time, President Trump's illegal and senseless war in Iran continues to cost American lives and drive up prices here at home.

The Trump Administration also continues to engage in an all-out assault on immigrant communities across the United States with their [mass deportation agenda](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15634.63198736.8375648.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.instagram.com%2freel%2fDd_ipWuBG04%2f%3fobrf%3dMjBjdDJ5bHk4dzgy&redir_log=302074255146436) - including by targeting people who have lived and worked here legally for years under Temporary Protected Status (TPS). I recently hosted a [spotlight forum](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15634.63198736.8375648.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.vanhollen.senate.gov%2fnews%2fvideos%2fwatch%2fvan-hollen-to-host-spotlight-forum-on-the-trump-administrations-attacks-on-tps&redir_log=83322682725912) before Congress and the American people highlighting the critical role TPS holders play in communities across the country.

We heard from community leaders and employers, including Carlos Raba, Chef and Owner of Clavel in Baltimore, about families facing separation, businesses losing employees, and the tragic consequences of ICE's [dehumanization](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15634.63198736.8375648.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fbsky.app%2fprofile%2fvanhollen.senate.gov%2fpost%2f3mwrmh4hlas2b&redir_log=443292495681447) of former TPS holders who are being forced back to unsafe countries. These are our [neighbors, friends, and coworkers](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15634.63198736.8375648.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fbsky.app%2fprofile%2fvanhollen.senate.gov%2fpost%2f3mvsaq4pogs25&redir_log=180300551776445) who have contributed so much to our communities.

In fact, a report from Forward US published earlier this year showed that TPS holders contribute about $29 billion every year to the US economy and pay $7.8 billion in combined federal payroll, state, and local taxes. Given their long-established roots, stripping away employment rights and forcing people from their homes will deliver severe economic shocks across the nation.

I will keep pushing to pass my [SECURE Act](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15634.63198736.8375648.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.youtube.com%2fwatch%3fv%3dm87eS833TU8&redir_log=838293019947282) to provide qualified TPS holders and Deferred Enforced Departure recipients with a pathway to lawful permanent residency and the certainty these families deserve. I am fighting back against these abuses while I work to continue delivering results for communities across Maryland. Here's the latest:
---
### Fighting to Make Life More Affordable
President Trump promised American workers a "golden age," yet he has delivered another Gilded Age only for billionaires and big corporations, while everyday Americans continue to struggle to make ends meet.

As of August, the average Maryland household had paid more than $3,700 in additional costs for everyday goods and services under President Trump. His [reckless tariff taxes](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15634.63198736.8375648.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.instagram.com%2freel%2fDce6nZhNjKN%2f%3fpsln%3dMXZmeDZkaW05YXcwOA%253D%253D&redir_log=830307826646472) and senseless war in Iran have pushed prices even higher.

Families felt that squeeze as students returned to school. The cost of a typical basket of school supplies - including notebooks, lunch boxes, and index cards - increased nearly 8 percent compared to last year, while the cost of a typical school lunch rose 11 percent. And after Trump and Congressional Republicans [cut SNAP](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15634.63198736.8375648.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fbsky.app%2fprofile%2fvanhollen.senate.gov%2fpost%2f3ms22ottwv22a&redir_log=528530152985442) to finance tax breaks for billionaires and wealthy corporations, more families are being forced to stretch already-tight budgets to put food on the table. Hungry kids can't learn. This is cruelty as a policy choice.

Meanwhile, Trump's own Administration has reported that the [share of economic growth](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15634.63198736.8375648.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fbsky.app%2fprofile%2fvanhollen.senate.gov%2fpost%2f3mxrt7y34m22b&redir_log=264189729607438) going to workers is now the lowest ever recorded. In the years immediately following World War II, roughly 65 percent of economic growth went into workers' pocketbooks. Today, that figure stands at just 52.8 percent. As corporate profits skyrocket, working people are being stiffed.

I am fighting to pass responsible funding bills that lower costs, protect essential services, and invest in Maryland communities - not another blank check for Trump's illegal war or more giveaways to those at the very top. We need to shake up this rigged system and ensure working people get their fair share. I will continue fighting to end Trump's sweeping tariff taxes, lower costs for Maryland families, and build an economy that works for everyone.
### Pumping the Brakes on Dangerous Frontier AI
We are hearing [extremely clear warnings](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15634.63198736.8375648.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.youtube.com%2fwatch%3fv%3dckaz9T4WGpI&redir_log=177667402805294) from the people building frontier artificial intelligence models about the risks that unregulated development poses today. We don't need to take every word at face value to grasp the broader point: the people developing this technology are concerned about the loss of human control.

Those risks became even more urgent with OpenAI's release of its latest model, GPT-6 Astra. OpenAI has acknowledged that its ability to monitor the model's internal operations has decreased, that its safety systems may miss dangerous behavior, and that the company may be unable to detect whether Astra is deliberately concealing its capabilities during safety testing. Those concerns come after multiple incidents in which OpenAI's models broke out of their "containment" during evaluations and caused security failures.

That's why I'm pushing OpenAI CEO Sam Altman for [answers](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15634.63198736.8375648.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fbsky.app%2fprofile%2fvanhollen.senate.gov%2fpost%2f3mwodut5njs2j&redir_log=623731579397449) about the company's decision to release Astra despite these warnings. I also urged OpenAI to provide researchers from the National Institute of Standards and Technology, the National Security Agency, and the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency with full and transparent access to the technical information they need to assess the risks to our digital systems and critical infrastructure. If OpenAI or any AI developer cannot guarantee the safety of its models or effectively monitor their behavior, those models should be removed from public use.

We need to pump the brakes until clear rules are in place to prevent this technology from doing grave harm. That includes mandatory safeguards and a comprehensive testing regime. If any AI developer fails to contain their technology during development or testing, they should be held accountable under our existing laws while Congress works to develop new commonsense guardrails.

Instead, President Trump dismissed concerns about AI safety as a "hoax." He has said that he is the only guardrail that's needed while focusing his efforts on renaming AI to "Super Intelligence." After starting his presidency by delivering for the Silicon Valley investors and tech oligarchs who helped fund his return to the White House (remember, they were seated right behind him when he was sworn in) by eliminating safety rules and working to block both federal and state oversight, the Trump Administration has done little to protect public safety from this growing threat.

Earlier this year, when the Trump Administration tried to force Anthropic to include dangerous capabilities in their contract, like the ability for AI to control autonomous weapons or to perform mass surveillance in the United States, I demanded the Administration end their pressure campaign - an alarming abuse of governmental power. Instead, the Administration doubled down and retaliated against Anthropic by designating them as a supply chain risk. A federal judge has since ruled in one case that the Administration's retaliatory actions were unlawful, but we must continue pushing back. Humans must always be in control, and no technology should enable mass surveillance in our free country.

Because this is a digital technology, [advanced AI development](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15634.63198736.8375648.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fbsky.app%2fprofile%2fvanhollen.senate.gov%2fpost%2f3mwdygovb3225&redir_log=434444610495440) across the world may impact the American people. The United States currently has the most advanced models, but Chinese AI companies are also pushing the technology. When Trump welcomed China's President Xi to Washington, I led sixteen of my Senate colleagues in [calling on him](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15634.63198736.8375648.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.vanhollen.senate.gov%2fnews%2fpress-releases%2fvan-hollen-more-than-15-senate-democrats-push-trump-to-negotiate-ai-guardrails-with-xi&redir_log=380326826838972) to discuss basic safety guardrails on the international development of advanced AI. President Trump delivered nothing but a tour of his ballroom for President Xi.

Congress needs to act now. We must confront the political system that enabled the unregulated AI race while delivering what must be done today: strong federal guardrails on AI development to ensure public safety and security.
### Stopping Trump's Illegal and Senseless War in Iran, Ending U.S. Complicity in Gaza, and Demanding Accountability in the West Bank
President Trump's illegal war in Iran continues to [kill Americans](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15634.63198736.8375648.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fbsky.app%2fprofile%2fvanhollen.senate.gov%2fpost%2f3mwgsf7qll22y&redir_log=691036480846445) and civilians, drain our resources, and [drive up prices](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15634.63198736.8375648.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fbsky.app%2fprofile%2fvanhollen.senate.gov%2fpost%2f3mwc77oghgk2c&redir_log=419101978438443) here at home.

Estimates from the Pentagon show that the war has already cost American taxpayers $47 billion, while the Congressional Budget Office (CBO) estimates this war will cost another $2 billion to $3 billion for every additional month it continues. CBO also estimates that the United States has used between one-half and two-thirds of its inventory of certain missile defense interceptors since June 2025 - stockpiles needed in the event of a real national security threat that could take five years to rebuild.

American families are paying for this war every day. Every two minutes, consumers pay another $1 million in higher fuel costs because of Trump's war. Across Maryland, drivers have spent an estimated $1 billion more at the gas pump since the war began - an average of $642 per family. President Trump calls those higher prices "peanuts" and a "very small price to pay." Families struggling to afford gas, groceries, and electricity know otherwise.

This is what happens when you delude yourself into believing that one more week of airstrikes or one more month of a blockade will produce a quick victory. As I warned in July, this kind of logic is how forever wars begin. When you are digging yourself into a hole, stop digging. But Trump keeps digging. He is now reportedly sending up to another 10,000 troops to fight this illegal war of choice, which he says he plans to renew next month.

Instead of working to end the war, protect our troops, save civilian lives across the region, and lower costs, the Trump Administration announced that it plans to send $2.8 billion in bombs - paid for by American taxpayers - to a government still led by someone wanted for war crimes, and even as Prime Minister Netanyahu continues dropping bombs in Gaza despite the so-called "ceasefire."

Netanyahu has said outright that in Gaza they are "destroying more and more houses so the Palestinians will have nowhere to return." I will work to block this transfer of American taxpayer-financed bombs. I made clear that in the aftermath of the horrific Hamas attacks of October 7th, Israel was justified in going after Hamas, but not in imposing brutal collective punishment on all the people of Gaza.

Meanwhile, the final outcome of this week's Israeli election remains uncertain. Coalition negotiations could take weeks, and Netanyahu will remain a caretaker Prime Minister until a new government is formed. Regardless of the outcome, the United States must judge any Israeli government and leader by the same standards and whether their actions comport with our interests and values. We must enforce our laws and ensure that American taxpayer dollars are not used to support the occupation or violations of Palestinian's human rights, regardless of who is in power in Israel.

That's why we are also demanding answers about the unacceptable situation on the West Bank, where violent Israeli settlers terrorize Palestinians with impunity and seek to force them off their lands. Moreover, in just over four years, nine Americans have been killed in the West Bank, yet none of their families have received accountability or justice from either the Israeli or United States Governments. In addition to these deaths, Americans are routinely wrongfully imprisoned by the Netanyahu government, and Palestinians [face injustices daily](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15634.63198736.8375648.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fbsky.app%2fprofile%2fvanhollen.senate.gov%2fpost%2f3mxzelbvbyc27&redir_log=434499118186448) under the Israeli occupation of the West Bank.

That is why Senators Kaine, Sanders, and I led 23 of our Senate colleagues in [forcing a vote on](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15634.63198736.8375648.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fbsky.app%2fprofile%2fvanhollen.senate.gov%2fpost%2f3mworjjnbj22b&redir_log=034115028567447) a resolution requiring the State Department to report to Congress on these killings, rampant violent settler attacks, and the dire human rights violations in the West Bank, including the detention of American citizens and Palestinian children.

[I spoke on the floor](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15634.63198736.8375648.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.youtube.com%2flive%2fBuAOnzMvF2o&redir_log=077261870821275) and urged my colleagues to support [this resolution](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15634.63198736.8375648.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.vanhollen.senate.gov%2fnews%2fpress-releases%2fvan-hollen-kaine-sanders-lead-20-senators-in-introducing-privileged-resolution-seeking-answers-on-west-bank-violence&redir_log=513556038731189) because the families of those killed and detained deserve answers. The American people deserve answers. And we must ensure that recipients of U.S. taxpayer dollars are acting in accordance with our laws and our values.

While I was pleased that 47 Senators supported this effort - more support than we've ever had in this fight - it's clear the United States must do more.

I will keep fighting to end U.S. complicity in Gaza, demand accountability for [Americans killed](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15634.63198736.8375648.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.youtube.com%2fshorts%2fHIprOi31YcQ&redir_log=258594298735287) in the West Bank, stand up for human rights for all, and stop President Trump's illegal war in Iran.
### Delivering for Maryland
Despite the dysfunction and chaos generated by the Trump Administration, I remain focused on delivering real results for communities across Maryland.

In Baltimore, Senator Alsobrooks and I recently highlighted a $300,000 investment we secured for [Global Refuge](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15634.63198736.8375648.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.vanhollen.senate.gov%2fnews%2fpress-releases%2fvan-hollen-alsobrooks-highlight-300000-in-federal-funding-to-support-opportunities-for-baltimores-refugee-immigrant-communities&redir_log=431565701721269) to expand their workforce development and career counseling services for refugees and immigrants. This federal funding will help program participants obtain the skills and training needed to secure jobs, achieve rapid self-sufficiency so they can contribute even more to their communities, and create opportunities for economic growth.

Just one week before this event, the Trump Administration had announced it would be illegally rescinding over $800 million in federal funds approved by Congress for programs that have supported many Marylanders, including Global Refuge. I will continue to fight back against the Trump Administration's unlawful acts and work hard to ensure that these vital programs are appropriately funded.

While in Baltimore, I also joined Congressman Mfume and Mayor Scott at the Baltimore City Office of Equity and Civil Rights' 33rd Annual Civil Rights Breakfast to honor Maryland's trailblazing civil rights leaders - past and present - and to discuss efforts to fight back against this Administration's attempts to dismantle their work. In Baltimore County, Congressman Olszewski and I joined local leaders to celebrate a $2 million federal investment that will support the construction of a new Baltimore County Public Library branch. The new Essex Branch will give the library more room for programs and community use, while allowing it to offer services that cannot be adequately accommodated in the current branch. Every Marylander should have access to all the books and resources that libraries have to offer, regardless of their ZIP code or their income.

And this week in Howard County, I joined County Executive Calvin Ball and Enterprise Community Development - a national nonprofit focused on expanding access to affordable housing, founded and based in Columbia - to mark the grand opening of The Vision at Parkway. Together with former Congressman Sarbanes, we secured an $850,000 federal investment for the project. The project also received $13 million in federal tax credits and other HUD loans. The opening of The Vision at Parkway will expand housing options in Columbia and provide more Marylanders with an affordable place to call home.

We're also bringing Maryland leaders and community partners together in Washington to advance our shared priorities. The Maryland congressional delegation recently met with [Mayor Scott](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15634.63198736.8375648.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.vanhollen.senate.gov%2fnews%2fpress-releases%2fmaryland-congressional-delegation-and-baltimore-mayor-brandon-scott-meet-to-discuss-baltimore-city-priorities&redir_log=108567542641149) at the Capitol to discuss our work to expand affordable housing, improve Baltimore's transportation and infrastructure, continue to strengthen public safety, and protect access to health care. As the Trump Administration targets essential programs that Baltimore residents rely on, Federal Team Maryland will continue working alongside our state and local partners to defend those resources and deliver new investments in the City's future.

The Maryland congressional delegation also met recently with [Port of Baltimore](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15634.63198736.8375648.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.youtube.com%2flive%2f6fAZNi99C4c&redir_log=630874990457264) leadership and stakeholders to discuss the Port's infrastructure needs, upcoming modernization projects, workforce, and long-term growth. With more than 270,000 Maryland jobs connected to the Port and $70 billion in annual economic impact for our state, its continued success is a priority for all of us. Together, we're working to build on past investments and secure the resources needed to strengthen the Port and expand economic opportunity across Maryland.
### Thank You
The decisions being made in Washington have real consequences for Marylanders, from the prices families pay to the use of taxpayer dollars at home and abroad. I will continue bringing Marylanders' priorities into every fight ahead.

Thank you for staying engaged and for all you do to strengthen our communities and our democracy!

Don't forget to vote!

Onwards,
Chris Van Hollen
