Dream In the go-big-or-go-home collective consciousness of Texas, no
ambition is deemed too reckless, no daydream too wild. Save perhaps one.
It is the idea, fantastical to many as it is irresistible to others, that
the Democrats will win a statewide race in Texas for the first time in 32
years. According to the latest New York Times/Siena University poll of the
race for U.S. Senate, James Talarico, a 37-year-old state legislator seen
by national Democrats as one of the breakout stars of this cycle, is ahead
of his Republican rival, Ken Paxton, the state’s scandal-plagued attorney
general, by six points. The poll was conducted from Sept. 21 to Sept. 30.
A survey from mid-September, the ReconMR/Siena Research Institute poll,
also showed the Democratic gubernatorial candidate, Gina Hinojosa, four
points ahead of the three-term G.O.P. incumbent, Greg Abbott, the most
dominant political figure in Texas. Cue the fluttering heartbeats. Cue, as
well, the eye-rolls. Given how thoroughly Republicans have dominated the
state, and how the hopes of Democrats have repeatedly crashed, some Texas
pollsters remain skeptical. “At some point, you do get conditioned by all
that’s happened in the past,” said James Henson, the director of the
University of Texas at Austin’s Texas Politics Project. “I mean, you look
at the trends and you have to admit that something’s going on. But you
still don’t want to believe your lying eyes, because you’ve been burned
for so long.” Mr. Henson was referring to the perennial spectacle of
much-ballyhooed Texas Democratic aspirants face-planting against the Lone
Star State’s red wall. First came Tony Sanchez Jr., the swaggering and
self-funding Laredo oilman whom Gov. Rick Perry dispatched in 2002 by an
18-point margin. Next was the state senator Wendy Davis, who attracted
worldwide attention for her filibuster in the Texas Legislature against an
anti-abortion measure but whom Mr. Abbott demolished by 20 points in 2014.
Finally, the El Paso congressman Beto O’Rourke came up 2.6 points short of
defeating Senator Ted Cruz in 2018 but then suffered a 10-point loss to
Mr. Abbott four years later. Even with the awareness of such humiliations,
Democrats find themselves maintaining that 2026 could, at long last, be
the year. President Trump’s deep unpopularity and the prospect of a blue
wave could, they insist, extend into the state he won by nearly 14 points
in 2024. According to a September survey conducted by Texas Southern
University, Mr. Trump is seven points underwater in Texas. Mr. Talarico
has run an energetic and well-financed campaign, while Mr. Paxton has
staged far fewer public events and has had to rely on outside groups to
fund an attack-ad blitzkrieg against his Democratic opponent. Mr. Abbott,
meanwhile, has outspent Ms. Hinojosa by a 10-to-one ratio, yet has been
unable to build an insurmountable lead. “People have vastly underestimated
Gina,” said Ms. Davis, now a political consultant and a senior adviser to
Planned Parenthood Texas Votes, an advocacy organization. “Dollar for
dollar, she’s running the best statewide campaign we’ve ever seen.” Such
optimism stands in defiance of the political axiom that Texas is where
idealistic Democrats go to be mugged by reality. The party’s demise there
is not a product of ill fortune, Mr. Henson said. “Governor Abbott has
built an impressive election machine that has benefited state-level
Republicans again and again for a decade and a half,” he said. “And the
Democratic machinery here is almost nonexistent.” A ‘Hollowing-Out’ I have
written about the politics of my native state at regular intervals for
more than three decades. After watching the Democrats’ century-long rule
in Texas come to a decisive end with Gov. Ann Richards’s loss to George W.
Bush in 1994, I saw the party descend into atrophy in which failure begot
more failure. “The 30-year drought has done a lot of things,” said Luke
Warford, the chairman of the Travis County Democratic Party and the
founder of the Agave Democratic Infrastructure Fund. “It’s kept donors on
the sidelines, which makes a lot of potentially good candidates not run
because there’s no belief they can win. And it also makes a lot of really
talented staff leave to find better-paying work in true battleground
states.” The Democratic Party has no counterpart to Mr. Abbott, and hasn’t
since 1993, when Senator Lloyd Bentsen moved to Washington to join
President Bill Clinton’s cabinet. Its weaknesses are even more glaring
farther down the hierarchy. In recent elections, as many as one-third of
state races have gone uncontested by Democrats. One-fifth of the party’s
county chairs and two-thirds of its precinct chairs have been left
unfilled. Until last year, the state party had a negative operating
budget. As the veteran Democratic consultant Matt Angle observed, “There’s
been a hollowing-out of the party.” Still, those of us who recall the
satisfied sense of invincibility among Texas Democrats after roughly a
century of one-party rule have detected similar signs of overconfidence
among the state’s ruling party. The party’s rightward tilt, increasingly
forceful with each legislative session, reached its apotheosis in March,
with Mr. Paxton’s primary victory over the more moderate Republican
four-term incumbent, Senator John Cornyn. Mr. Paxton, a close ally of Mr.
Trump’s, was impeached by the Republican-controlled State House (and later
acquitted by the State Senate) in 2023 over allegations that included
bribery. He was also accused by his wife of adultery. Mr. Trump endorsed
him anyway, all but guaranteeing his landslide primary triumph over Mr.
Cornyn but in the process testing the allegiance of center-right Texans.
In similar fashion, the Texas G.O.P. is in danger of losing many Latino
voters who voted for Mr. Trump in 2024 after years of siding with
Democrats. “We adopted a lazy way of campaigning that bit us on the ass,
and we’ve learned from that,” Mr. O’Rourke said. “Now it’s the Republicans
who’ve gotten really lazy and complacent and comfortable.” Signs of
Republican Overreach Simply spending one week driving through the vastness
of Texas, as I did in September, is all it takes to appreciate an underdog
party’s uphill battle. The state’s 32 million residents are spread across
20 media markets, many of them distinct ecosystems, from the urban colossi
of Houston and the Dallas-Fort Worth metroplex to the oil patch of the
Texas Panhandle to the Latino-dominated borderlands of the Rio Grande
Valley. “When national donors are deciding where to invest, they look at a
place like Iowa, where $5 million can fully fund a race,” said Katherine
Fischer, the director of the Texas Majority PAC, which was established by
the liberal philanthropist Soros family. “That’s why Texas is always at
the bottom of their list. It’s just so damned big.” Reaching so many
markets presents a daunting challenge for an upstart candidate like Ms.
Hinojosa, a state representative from the border city of Brownsville.
“There’s still 20 percent of the electorate that doesn’t know who I am,”
she said in an interview in mid-September. To date, Ms. Hinojosa’s
campaign has said that it has raised about $20 million. For his part, Mr.
Talarico spent about $30 million earlier this year to introduce himself
statewide as a man of Christian faith and a member of the Texas House with
a record of supporting bipartisan legislation. Since that time, however,
Mr. Paxton and his associates have invested more than $100 million in an
effort to redefine his opponent as “radical” and “weird,” with ads that
quote from remarks Mr. Talarico made several years ago (and later
renounced) suggesting that “God is nonbinary” and that there are six
biological sexes. Mr. Paxton and his allies have at times questioned Mr.
Talarico’s manhood and even his Christianity, an effort to jolt the
sensibilities of a state prone to mythologizing godly and masculine
archetypes. “How they’re negatively defining Talarico is kind of a
bank-shot way of saying that he’s not a true Texas conservative,” Mr.
Henson said. Whether money can overwhelm conditions on the ground is the
riddle looming over the Texas races. In the border city of Laredo, which
Mr. Trump won in 2024 — the first time a Republican had done so in over a
century — signs of buyer’s remorse are evident. Arrests by Immigration and
Customs Enforcement agents in Laredo were higher in July than in any other
American city. Mr. Trump’s erratic trade policies have further created
instability at the city’s port of entry. While acknowledging the economic
concerns that many border residents share, Adrian Zapata, a business
executive in the health industry who voted for Mr. Trump in 2024, said in
an interview that the negative ads against Mr. Talarico were resonating
with some of his family members. “They see Talarico as an ultraliberal,”
he said. “They’re done with the ‘they/them.’ They’re going to vote for
Paxton just because of that.” As for Mr. Zapata, “I’m not ready to vote
for Talarico,” he said. “But I don’t like Paxton. He’s never done anything
for South Texas, and his personal and business dealings have hurt him a
lot with folks down here.” There is a similarly muddled electoral picture
in the cattle country of deep West Texas adjacent to Big Bend National
Park. Mr. Trump and Mr. Abbott have aggressively championed a border wall
and artificial intelligence data centers, both of which threaten to
disrupt the region’s pastoral ethos. A coalition of more than 200
landowners has sued the federal government over the border wall, while
other residents have circulated a petition to protest the construction of
a new data center near Fort Stockton. George Johnson, a cattle feed
operator in Alpine, waved off such concerns, saying: “Folks worrying about
data centers were also worried when the internet got started. It’s
Talarico who scares me to death, him and all that socialist talk.” Others
in this largely conservative region harbor the view that Republicans have
failed to make good on their promises. Thaddeus Cleveland, the Republican
sheriff of Terrell County, said that both he and his county had voted for
Mr. Trump in 2024, but added, “Everything he campaigned on, we’re seeing
the opposite of, like going to war.” Sheriff Cleveland predicted that the
negative campaign ads by the Republicans would not factor as significantly
into the votes of his neighbors as “the price of groceries and gas, which
are compounded here because we’re so far from everywhere else.” But it is
in purple Tarrant County, dominated by Fort Worth, where the party could
pay the price for having potentially overestimated its mandate from the
voters. Conservative leaders have cut funds for nonprofits that aid
at-risk children, subjected school library books to right-wing litmus
tests and eliminated free bus rides to polling stations in poor
neighborhoods. “The far-right leaders here have implemented Project 2025
on a county level,” said Alisa Simmons, a Democrat and county commissioner
who is running to unseat the conservative county judge, Tim O’Hare. In an
early sign this year that area Republicans may be out of step with Tarrant
County’s constituents, a Democratic aviation machinist and union leader,
Taylor Rehmet, defeated Leigh Wambsganss, a well-funded Republican
Christian activist who led the conservative takeover of several metroplex
school boards. He won by 14 points in a January special election for a
State Senate seat covering a region that Mr. Trump won by 17 points in
2024. A ‘Gradualist’ Theory Which party prevails in Texas is a complicated
riddle. Historically a low-turnout state — it ranked second to last in the
2024 election, ahead of only Arkansas — Texas held a primary in March that
saw nearly one in four voters showing up to the polls, a modern record for
midterm participation, with Democrats slightly outpacing Republicans. A
few factors could conspire to thwart a blue wave in Texas. As of 2020,
straight-ticket voting is no longer possible in the state, which could
impact the mostly Democratic urban counties where that practice has
frequently been used by voters in past elections. Texas is one of only
eight states that lack universal online registration, while voting by mail
is also highly restricted. In January, Mr. Abbott turned over the state’s
list of approximately 18.7 million registered voters to the Trump
administration, and 1.2 million of them have subsequently been put on the
“suspense list” because their addresses have not been verified. The recent
shuttering of nearly one-third of Tarrant County’s polling sites by its
Republican-controlled county commission is particularly worrisome for
Democrats. “The reason we’ve lost these statewide races in the past is
because we’ve never gotten enough out of Tarrant County to overcome the
margins in rural Texas,” Ms. Davis said of the turnout. “If we don’t get
it to 53 or 54 percent this November, it’s game over. James and Gina can’t
win.” But the state’s Republicans have reasons of their own to be fretful.
Partly because of the recruitment efforts of the Texas Majority PAC and
Blueprint Texas, a down-ballot candidate support organization co-founded
by Ms. Davis earlier this year, the Democrats are fielding a full slate in
all 150 state races for the first time in a half-century. Though many of
these aspirants face long odds, their presence on the ballot could
energize the Democrats in predominantly conservative regions who have not
bothered to turn out in the past. “If we win on Nov. 3, most of those
names running down-ballot in really tough areas like East Texas and the
Hill Country and the Panhandle will be responsible,” Mr. O’Rourke said.
Mr. Henson added that while he remained skeptical about Democratic
enthusiasm being sufficient to carry the day for Mr. Talarico, he also
doubted that a last-minute avalanche of negative ads would prove decisive
for Mr. Paxton. “At a certain point, there’s diminishing impact once you
get past an absurd level of spending,” he said. Rather than project a
winner in November, Mr. Henson said he felt more comfortable embracing a
“gradualist” theory, one in which Texas does not become blue overnight,
but instead competitive. “Even if Talarico loses by a Beto-like margin,”
he said, “the next cycle is a presidential election, where Trump likely
won’t be popular and Democratic turnout will be higher. So there are
reasons for Texas Democrats to be optimistic.”'

| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/96845b55-d813-47d5-b0fd-9ea31b486c7e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Friends,
Just a few days ago, I held a public town hall in Oakley, Kansas -- a rural town of approximately 2,000 people.
Oakley is where -- 607 days ago -- Sen. Roger Marshall **walked out of the town hall he was holding.** He ended the event early after calling the crowd one of the rudest audiences he'd ever had.
After that, he said town halls had become "nonproductive" and "dangerous." He hasn't held one since.
**Friends, Sen. Marshall is just plain wrong. Talking to Kansans isn 't dangerous or nonproductive. In fact, Kansans deserve a senator who stays and listens to them. We don't always have to agree with each other -- and in fact, the people at that town hall and I **_**didn 't**_**agree on everything. But I stayed, and I** _**listened**_**.**
I opened my heart to the farmers worried about the cost of diesel and fertilizer. To the parents trying to figure out how they'll pay for healthcare. To the neighbors looking out for families struggling to put food on the table.
And then, we had an honest conversation about how I'll fight for them in Washington.
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/96845b55-d813-47d5-b0fd-9ea31b486c7e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The people in the crowd gave up part of their weekend to come to their town hall, and they brought their questions with them. And friends, nothing about that crowd was dangerous, and talking to them was the most productive thing I could be doing. How else would I know what issues are concerning them? How else would I know what problems they need help solving?
Sen. Marshall seems to have forgotten this, but a leader's job is to _fight for the people they were elected to represent ... and you can't represent people who never see you._
When he called talking to Kansans dangerous and nonproductive, he made it crystal clear he has no intention of putting his constituents over his party or his politics. He has no intention of listening to them, thinking about how to solve their problems or courageously fighting to implement those solutions.
Instead, he's turned his back on the people he was elected to represent -- and it shows. If he were willing to listen to Kansans, he might not have voted multiple times to keep us in the war that's driving up diesel and fertilizer prices. He might not have backed the tariffs that are costing Kansas families hundreds of dollars every month. He might not have rubber-stamped slashing the healthcare assistance that thousands of Kansans rely on.
He might be willing to stand up and say "no more" to the corrupt and chaotic policies coming out of Washington.
**But he** _**isn 't**_**willing to listen to Kansans. That 's why we MUST WIN this race. **
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/96845b55-d813-47d5-b0fd-9ea31b486c7e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
**Kansans deserve an independent-minded leader who is focused on being a true champion for** _**them**_** -- not for corporate PACs or party bosses. But with just five days to go until Election Day, Roger Marshall's allies are flooding the airwaves with attack ads to turn voters against me. We have to fight back -- which is why my team and I have set an ambitious $3 million end-of-month goal so we can get our ads into every living room in Kansas, make sure every voter knows what's at stake in this election and FLIP this seat.**
**[Please, time is running out. Will you chip in whatever you can to help us reach our goal, fight back against Marshall's attacks and get every supporter out to the polls?](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/96845b55-d813-47d5-b0fd-9ea31b486c7e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[Donate](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/96845b55-d813-47d5-b0fd-9ea31b486c7e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
The people of Kansas are ready for a leader who will listen. With your help, we can give them one.
Thank you,
Adam Hamilton

The Senate confirms every federal judge and every Supreme Court justice. Whoever holds the Senate majority decides who sits on the courts that will rule on our gun laws for decades.
That majority runs through four races: Jon Ossoff in Georgia. Roy Cooper in North Carolina. Sherrod Brown in Ohio. James Talarico in Texas. All four are GIFFORDS-endorsed, and all four are close.
GIFFORDS PAC is putting everything we have into reaching the undecided voters who will decide them. We have four days left.

| | | Fellow Conservative, In the U.S. Senate, there is no separate background check. No security clearance process. **The election IS the clearance.** That means, if Abdul El-Sayed wins in Michigan, Chuck Schumer could put him on the Intelligence Committee, with access to the intelligence that keeps our troops and covert operators alive.Think about that for a moment. **_[Our nation's secrets could be in the hands of a man with connections to the Muslim Brotherhood, whose father-in-law is a leader of a group named in America's largest terror-financing case, and who campaigned with someone who said America deserved 9/11.](https://trk.email.tedcruz._xAYKKv-npZL3hiknr_Gw)_** **That's a risk we cannot take.** I'm in Michigan right now doing everything I can to stop Abdul El-Sayed from winning. Right now, there are two glimpses of hope. The first is Republican Mike Rogers. Mike served in the Army and in the FBI. He chaired the House Intelligence Committee. He knows exactly what's at stake when it comes to protecting America's secrets. I've been campaigning alongside him. He's within an arm's reach of pulling off a historic victory. **The second is YOU.** I have hope that if you have read this far, you'll go one step further and rush in a donation right now to help Mike win. This isn't just another tough fight. Our national security is on the line. America's future is at stake. I know folks like you will take this plea seriously and rush in a donation before it's too late. This race is close. Every last dollar will make or break the outcome. **[Please donate now to help Mike Rogers win and keep El-Sayed out of the Senate.](https://trk.email.tedcruz.)** Thank you,

Maine Democrats, operating under the auspices of the George Soros-funded Maine People's Alliance, stormed into Lewiston City Hall during early in-person voting in a brazen violation of Maine's laws against electioneering in and around voting places.
The Maine Wire's Graham Pollard narrates this stunning video showing what can only be described as a militant attempt to scare normal voters away from the polls and illegally influence the votes of Lewiston residents present at City Hall that day.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..EfnmVTA6UrkeH4HCn1_TGMd_yNbn_lfZ6qL2qI14O3A?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=222685293)
The illegal acts occurred on Thursday, October 22, 2026, as a group of roughly 20 activists entered the hallway outside the early voting room at Lewiston City Hall. Photographs from the scene show Democratic State Rep. and Lewiston City Councilor Scott Harriman among the participants.
The direct action was organized in response to Maine Wire Reporter Jon Fetherston capturing photographic evidence that raised questions about whether Somali translators were violating other Maine laws when they coached and assisted apparently illiterate Somalis on how to same-day register and fill out their ballots.
City Clerk Kathy Montejo, after consulting the Attorney General's office, has been treating the early voting period as equivalent to Election Day for purposes of electioneering restrictions. GOP candidate Bret Martel told MWTV that prior complaints had already required him to remove a plain paper name tag and campaign magnets from his truck to avoid any appearance of prohibited activity. Yet no similar disciplinary action was meted out against the bolshevik blitzkrieg.
[Share The Robinson Report](https://substack..NlrGHd33qoDywH2kxaOEMbZyMKkKBNov0AKaETOUcPg?)
Maine law is unambiguous on the illegal nature of the conduct captured in the security video.
Title 21-A, section 682 of the Maine Revised Statutes prohibits influencing or attempting to influence a voter's decision regarding candidates or ballot questions "on public property within 250 feet of the entrance to the voting place as well as within the voting place itself." Protecting Colorado’s children shouldn’t be a partisan issue

[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

Here's a summary of today's top stories:

🏔️ HERE IN COLORADO...The DOE asked the full D.C. Circuit to
overturn a ruling narrowing its authority to keep coal plants online
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.
freezing three Colorado cases including one over Craig Station Unit 1,
still running 10 months past its scheduled retirement; nearly 842,000

$1,000 federal contribution, though parents must still formally claim
the account.

🗣️ COMMENTARY SPOTLIGHT... Alejandro Bermúdez urges backing
Propositions 133, 134 and 135
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.
as child-protection measures, rebutting claims they’d punish

“Cynical Publius” argues the U.S. is undergoing a CIA/USAID-style
“color revolution.”
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

This is your Mountain Minute for Thursday, October 29, 2026.

– Team RMV

TODAY'S TOP STORIES

BERMÚDEZ: PROTECTING COLORADO’S CHILDREN SHOULDN’T BE A PARTISAN
ISSUE
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

BY ALEJANDRO BERMUDEZ, ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

_On November 3, Colorado voters have a remarkable opportunity to do
something that should transcend political affiliations: protect
children from sexual predators, defend fairness in girls’ sports,
and prevent minors from undergoing irreversible sex-change surgeries._

_Propositions 133, 134, and 135 are straightforward, common-sense
measures. Yet opponents have managed to manufacture alarming scenarios
that deserve closer scrutiny._

_Proposition 133, the Children Are Not for Sale Act, would impose life
imprisonment without parole for child sex trafficking and expand the
law to cover those knowingly buying sexual activity with minors._

READ MORE
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

CRAIG COAL PLANT: 3 COLORADO CASES FREEZE WHILE DOE SEEKS A REHEARING
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

BY SHAINA COLE, ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

_The Department of Energy is fighting to preserve its authority to
force coal plants to stay open after a federal court narrowed that
power, leaving three Colorado cases over the Craig plant in limbo._

*
A FEDERAL EMERGENCY POWER UNDER CHALLENGE: A D.C. Circuit panel ruled
in September that DOE’s authority to keep plants running under the
Federal Power Act is “rare and authorized only when states, their
utilities” and grid operators can’t respond, and DOE’s Oct. 26
rehearing petition argues the court wrongly invented a
deference-to-states requirement not found in the statute.

*
EVEN PLANT OWNERS ARE PUSHING BACK: Tri-State and Platte River, two of
Craig Unit 1’s own owners, formally asked DOE to rescind the order,
arguing it amounts to an uncompensated taking of their property under
the Fifth Amendment, while Colorado’s own Public Utilities
Commission had already found in August 2025 that the unit “is not
required for reliability or resource adequacy purposes.”

*
COLORADO’S CASE REMAINS ON HOLD: AG Phil Weiser’s challenge, along
with suits from environmental groups and the plant’s owners, has
been frozen since June pending resolution of the Michigan case that
triggered the narrower reading of DOE’s emergency authority, with no
timeline yet for when Colorado’s litigation resumes.

COLORADO CIVIL RIGHTS AGENCY DISMISSED 93% OF COMPLAINTS LAST YEAR
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

BY SHAINA COLE | STATE | OCTOBER 27

_The Colorado Civil Rights Division reached a determination on 974
discrimination complaints in FY24-25 and dismissed 902 of them, or
93%. In the other 72 it found probable cause to believe discrimination
occurred, 44 fully and 28 in part. That works out to 7.4%._
__

DOWNS: WHY I’M BACKING DR. SHIMON BLAU IN DENVER’S HOUSE RACE
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

BY JOHN DOWNS | COMMENTARY | OCTOBER 27

_Dr. Shimon Blau is running as an independent in Colorado’s First
Congressional District, the seat currently held by Diana DeGette. He
is running against Melat Kiros, a Democrat and a member of the
Democratic Socialists of America (DSA)._

__

MILLIONS TO DEFEAT PROPS 134, 135: WHO FUNDS THE FUNDERS?
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

BY KELLY NOTARFRANCESCO | STATE | OCTOBER 26

_Over two decades ago, in a nondescript conference room at the
Colorado Education Association’s building across the street from
Colorado’s Capitol, a highly effective and influential political
network was born. Today, the secret network has expanded and is still
influencing Colorado’s political landscape._

🧐 DID YOU KNOW?

In January 1913, Adolf Hitler, Joseph Stalin, Leon Trotsky, Josip Broz
Tito, and Sigmund Freud all lived within a few square miles of each
other in Vienna. They all frequented the same dense cluster of coffee
houses, entirely unaware they would collectively shape and fracture
the 20th century.

to any system under which men can live as human beings."_ – Ludwig

Friend, it’s Pete Buttigieg, and I’m reaching out on behalf of
my friend Rob Sand, who is running for governor of Iowa in one of the most
closely watched statewide races anywhere in the country this year.

Rob holds a narrow lead in the polls. But Iowans know better than most
that a poll is a snapshot, not a result. With just 5 days to go, this race
will be decided by who puts in the work between now and November 3rd.

[ https://act.robsand.com/go/12067?t=1017&amount=25&akid=1629%2E412644%2EMeTEsf ]In a moment, I’ll explain why I believe Rob is the right person to lead

please chip in $25, or whatever you can, to help him in the final week of
this race.

[ https://act.robsand.com/go/12067?t=1019&amount=35&akid=1629%2E412644%2EMeTEsf ]Other Amount

Iowans deserve a governor who puts the needs of working families first,
and Rob has spent his career doing exactly that.

He grew up in Decorah and served as an assistant attorney general before
Iowans elected him state auditor, twice. In that job, he uncovered $29
million in misspent public money, more than any state auditor in Iowa
history. That record tells you something about how he would govern. He
sees protecting taxpayer dollars as part of the job, no matter which party
is in charge.

Rob has also shown he’s willing to buck his own party when he thinks it’s
wrong. His campaign puts it well: not redder or bluer, but better and
truer. That kind of independence is a big part of what makes him the right
person for this moment. It’s also why he committed to holding 100 town
halls across the state to hear directly from Iowans.

Zach Lahn is offering something very different: another four years of
failed policies, single-party rule, and a government with no transparency
or accountability.

Partisan insiders have taken notice. The Republican Governors Association
has already given Lahn more than $15 million to prop him up, and he’s
spending $1 million every week on ads attacking Rob. They see Rob and his
grassroots team as a threat to a decade of one-party control in Iowa.

No grassroots campaign can match a $1 million-a-week ad budget on its own.
But it doesn’t have to. What Rob needs is a team strong enough to keep
reaching voters in every corner of Iowa and cut through the noise of those
attacks. That depends on people like you.

clean_body: A combat veteran on Trump’s $47 billion illegal war. | | Peter, Trump had the gall to stand on a Texas stage this week and brag that the Iran war will end "whenever I want it to end." So he finally admits it 's a war? Because Pete Hegseth is still denying benefits to the families of soldiers killed and wounded in this conflict by refusing to call it one. Kings and despots can singlehandedly decide when wars end. Presidents answer to the Constitution. Ours puts war powers in the hands of Congress, and Congress never authorized a single day of this catastrophe. Donald Trump is wrong. The Pentagon's own estimate now puts this war at $47 billion, with $29 billion just replacing the munitions Trump bragged were "virtually unlimited." Let me put $47 billion in Texas terms. That money could have paid every public school teacher in Texas for almost two full school years. It could have funded children's health insurance in this state for decades. It could have matched the entire national fund Congress just created to rescue America's dying rural hospitals, and Texas has lost more of those hospitals than any state in the country. Instead it bought burned aircrafts, bombed barracks, and a cover-up of our war casualties. The average American family has already paid about $2,000 for this war through energy bills and interest rates alone. If our representatives truly believe this is a just and necessary war, then they owe it to the American people to debate it fully in Congress, and take a vote on the record, as our founding fathers intended. A congressman holds the power to demand war powers votes, subpoena the costs, and defend the Constitution he swore to uphold. If Keith Self wants to put our uniformed personnel in harm’s way for a bunch of lies from President Trump, then let him say it with his whole chest and put his vote on the record. Instead, he’s voted against enforcing congressional war powers SIX TIMES since the start of this war. H.R. 40 failed by a single vote. And H.R. 75 ended in a dead tie. Self has proven he will never lift a finger against this illegal war, so the voters of this district must remove the decision from his hands. Five days from now, this district can fire a congressman who keeps cheering this war while we lose more servicemembers and the bill keeps climbing. I served my country for 20 years in uniform. I know what war costs in dollars, and I know what it costs in folded flags. Ending this disaster is a solemn and urgent duty that I take seriously. Case File No DRT-ED-ORBIT · Special File · The Lights Overhead
SpaceX Has Asked Permission to Launch Up to One Million Satellites. Not for Internet. For AI Computing in Orbit.
In January, SpaceX filed with the FCC for a constellation of up to a million solar-powered satellites designed to work as an “orbital data center.” At the time, fewer than 10,000 Starlink satellites were in orbit. If even part of this plan happens, it will need hardware that can survive one of the harshest environments there is.
Threat level 3/5 — Guarded
| | | | | | | | |
---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---
|
---
Since the first Starlink trains appeared, people have reported strange lines of lights crossing the night sky. Most were satellites, freshly launched and still bunched together. That was the internet business. What SpaceX is proposing now is something different: moving part of the AI boom off the planet entirely.
The evidence board
| | What the Filing Says
---|---
| EVIDENCE
---
**Exhibit A — the request.** On January 30, 2026, SpaceX asked the FCC for permission to “deploy a system of up to one million satellites” operating in narrow orbital shells.
| EVIDENCE
---
**Exhibit B — the purpose.** The filing describes a solar-powered “orbital data center” providing computing capacity for AI workloads.
| EVIDENCE
---
**Exhibit C — the scale.** At the time of the filing, an unofficial tracker counted more than 9,600 Starlink satellites in orbit. A million would be roughly a hundred times that.
| OUR THEORY
---
Space offers constant sunlight and no neighbors complaining about power bills. But it also bombards electronics with radiation that can corrupt data and destroy ordinary chips. Whoever supplies hardware that survives up there could be paid on every satellite launched.
Connected file
| | Why AI Is Looking Up
---|---
On the ground, AI’s power needs are becoming a political problem. A Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory report estimated data centers could use 6.7% to 12% of U.S. electricity by 2028, up from about 4.4% in 2023.
One research team says a little-known energy technology could let AI companies power data centers without touching the public grid.

body:
Our very last fundraising deadline before Election Day is almost here, and I need you with me to finish this last stretch strong.
# [](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/892?refcode=em20261029-6902-footer&t=1&akid=6902%2E420207%2EcHjTfE)
Hi Peter, it’s Pramila.
When the stakes are highest, I turn to the people I know I can trust: this grassroots movement.
That’s why I’m not sending this email to everyone. I’m sending it to the people who have been standing with our movement and believe in the future we’re building together. In the final days of this election cycle, I need you with me.
I’ve been on the road nearly every weekend, rallying and knocking doors with courageous progressive candidates on the ballot, many of whom have faced down _millions_ of dollars in outside spending and kept fighting anyway.
**And on November 3, we have the chance to grow our progressive movement in Congress and across the country.** That means more fighters who will help us pass Medicare for All, protect our immigrant neighbors, stand up to corporate power, and finally put working people first. This moment truly matters because control of the House and Senate could come down to a handful of votes, in a handful of races.
With early voting already underway and ballots coming in as we speak, every moment counts. But to be honest with you, _our fundraising isn’t where we need it to be._
This is our very last fundraising deadline before polls close on Election Day, and every dollar we raise before midnight on October 31 will go right to work getting out the vote through these final days. [**Will you please pitch in $3 today to help us reach our $75,000 fundraising goal and finish this last stretch strong?**](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/47393?c0=pj-em-20261029-1.ZFsO4q&refcode=em20261029-6902&amount=3&t=3&akid=6902%2E420207%2EcHjTfE)
**[Contribute $3](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/47393?c0=pj-em-20261029-1.ZFsO4q&amount=3&refcode=em20261029-6902&t=22&akid=6902%2E420207%2EcHjTfE)**
Thank you so much for being a part of this movement. Let's bring home these wins!
— PJ

Hi there, it's Michele Tafoya!

If I were to take a guess, there's a 50/50 chance you may recognize me from a stadium's big screen.
If that's not the case, I get it... Let me at least tell you briefly about who I am and what I'm about anyway!

I should clarify first, no, I didn't make my career running for touchdowns or kicking game-winning field goals.

I worked as a sideline reporter in professional football for nearly three decades. Working in the sport for that long was a dream come true, and I wouldn't have wanted it any other way.
[Believe me, I know plenty of people who called me crazy for walking away from a career I loved. But life is short, and I was not willing to sit on the sidelines while everything I care about was on the line.](https://links.iterable.com/s/c/Lsifcyb7Y_o5rRLKgN08Yfb-LSUlzFYHtw-ry1um_eK5096C1cLpmfIF8suErz_0b6hsQyDZ95SAo5_orYCpJ_rqdzVlQz6PSp6scKYsLZA9IC5LIPt7pCyMhssQICr_QZpNn290NI9AUbm7rItbymh0QeBdAafPpkFJdPtyZ_jff2ncCu78ayEZU1v3lngWrqDK3tWd1QmDwfdHMyXMrP9jQCIFsZ9Z4bbl83wXvF-R-CUyD0wjdmNyaptIyHrrMDgNqvktNnVzmMqV3YN3kJZzkHDaZjdjywaRIKY96-AqzV3UuAzLGSOLWFYEYEXEE0hJF-q9BZvCMm7fWdMngQHaGLOlQ4C8uxaqXaC37elRwNHgglzB75nyBtAj4QHfxwPoF-i-adkf9UkUlxEAZMZrn6-I6Yj-tlomEL9gduAbK5_ThHj7jLpGW4hY5RSIDWhamOq1J5DWwGwtCE80il0kS9TUzOSQh4WyaMYUnLUWk7Hny6dT5a41iNDZlMZIPvw_7mBfOl-YwE4i8HUHiaQdD42FEDexsprVvKVVSZ1N7qICefczCfJ6VzxqIPZdaxzoxzMJBABH8DiWblYOq0722tAE-gRM0whIPgjQA0AOVNXnwkfh2AaEDY5J6WvAqtAmlU08aDgEOCd7VQnrNCPrLC5rZ_Vor8L_acek0gG1ZGbgf4-XBuQniaq1MK_Gfl5eABiSVAaviHYAALmW7pIDPwC5xpVUrCltoQGtqBV40r6fIqB71c3X7WTvLKDDd_E5E3qLW8gAelNSO_RI1Pulv3a-WF999bgpdop7Kk9KJHm34v6VlTDYnCmS-6F_w-VW3OH-p3Emq7_hs-um1Sp73K41Z911lGSBT6jOzfZDyeb3ykkqz3FQHdIu_eSKexaEnk99bb4JzBAbYQv2kq9MNFCUPhqokno/zV0OK9z59prRDDE5RCja83uxL5DNwvht/26)
I told myself before I officially launched my race for U.S. Senate that we had to be all in or not do it at all.

I burned the boats, Friend, and there's absolutely no looking back.
I will not be canceled. I will not apologize for values that are wholesome and good. And if my voice gives someone else the courage to use theirs, that is exactly why I did it.

I want my daughter and every young American to know one thing:
You earn your place. You think for yourself. And you never let anyone put you in a box. That's the Minnesota I'm fighting for.
Parents who speak up are called transphobes.Girls who lose opportunities are told to be quiet.And women's groups are nowhere to be found.
This is not complicated.
Girls' sports are for girls, and boys' sports are for boys.

The radical Left has done everything in its power to infiltrate some of the most vulnerable minds in our society. I launched this run because just like you, I'm sick of the indoctrination and want to bring back sanity to our country.

It's going to be FAR from easy. Minnesota hasn't had a Republican Senator in nearly two decades! However, it's ripe for a flip....with the disastrous leadership of Governor Walz and the Democratic Party in the state, people are fed up.

It's going to take a grassroots army of patriots, just like you, to propel this movement of ours to victory and shock the world.

clean_body: We’re halfway through our tour. Chip in to keep us moving until Election Day. | | | = = Hey, friend, it’s Adam, coming to you from the road. In the final stretch, I’ve been busy talking to folks all across Kansas. Everywhere I go, people are tired of the chaos and corruption in Washington — and ready for change. But here’s the tough truth. While I’m out campaigning, Roger Marshall and his allies in D.C. are busy too — pulling out all the stops to crush our momentum at the eleventh hour with attack ads and outright lies about me. We’re so close to the finish line — but while I’m on the road, we also need to make sure our ads stay on air until the last ballots are cast AND fully fund our get-out-the-vote efforts.= | | = Everywhere our campaign bus stops, the energy is amazing. From Hays and Olathe to Holton and Greensburg, I hear the same thing: Our state and our country deserve better. It’s time for a new kind of leadership, grounded in decency and a commitment to fight for real people, not special interests or party bosses. But our incredible momentum has put a target on our backs. The president and VP have both visited Kansas personally to prop up Roger Marshall’s failing campaign, and the Senate GOP’s top super PAC is spending $14 million to defeat us. I know we can still fight back and win, but only if we keep up our energy in these final days. That’s why hitting our final end-of-month deadline is so important. It’ll give us the resources to reach the last undecided voters, fight back against attacks and make sure our voters get to the polls. There could not be a more important time to give, friend. I’m counting on this grassroots team to show up one final time.= If you've saved payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: | | | = | | = | | = | | = Thank you for doing your part to get us across the finish line! — Adam | Adam Hamilton is a husband, father, pastor and fifth-generation Kansan. Now, he’s running for U.S. Senate as an independent-minded Democrat. Just like you, he’s tired of the chaos and corruption in Washington that is harming our farmers, raising costs at the checkout line and making critical health care services unattainable. He hears your concerns and is ready to get to work for you. Early polling shows Adam neck-and-neck in this race, and with your help, we can win big this November. = | | = | | = | This email was sent to dpwillis67@gmail.com Rather donate by check or by mail? It’s Chris.

It's been an incredible journey since we launched our campaign 18 months
ago — and tonight represents one of the biggest moments in our fight to
keep New Hampshire blue.

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20261029_5.kZDzdB&refcode=em20261029-5&t=1003&akid=9872%2E582294%2EOc-lT7 ]If you’re already on board and ready to help us get our message in
front of the Granite Staters who need to hear it, can I count on you to
rush a $5 contribution to our campaign in the next 30
minutes?

Our final chance to expand our TV advertising buys is rapidly slipping
away.

This is our final chance to get our message out to the voters in time.
Because over 90% of New Hampshire voters cast their ballots on Election
Day, we have to close out this race strong, and we can’t afford to lose
momentum right now when the stakes are highest.

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20261029_5.kZDzdB&refcode=em20261029-5&t=1004&akid=9872%2E582294%2EOc-lT7 ]Tonight is our chance to show what we’ve built together — a movement of
people who believe in a freer, fairer future for the Granite State and the
country. We set a goal to raise $500,000 to continue our campaign as
planned. Can you chip in $5 to help us hit our goal before
midnight tonight?

The GOP and the MAGA billionaires are determined to elect John Sununu and
flip this seat red. That’s why they are spending over $65 million to try
and buy this seat – and they’re counting on us falling short tonight.

With Election Day in just FIVE DAYS, every single hour matters. And every
dollar has to stretch even further in these final moments.

That’s why I’m reaching out one last time to ask for your support. Not
because it’s a nice-to-have, but because hitting this $500,000 goal
tonight is the only way we’ll be able to win this race.

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20261029_5.kZDzdB&refcode=em20261029-5&t=1005&akid=9872%2E582294%2EOc-lT7 ]Please, will you chip in
$5 or anything you can before MIDNIGHT to help us reach our
$500,000 fundraising goal and keep us on track to win on November 3rd?

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20261029_5.kZDzdB&amount=5&refcode=em20261029-5&t=1024&akid=9872%2E582294%2EOc-lT7 ]Donate $5 »

Thank you,

Chris Pappas

clean_body: I will not waste your time.| | | | | Peter, it’s John James. We're less than 7 days away from Election Day. Before I say anything else—as someone who has logged 750 combat hours in Iraq—I know every second counts, and there’s not a moment in the day we should be wasting. I promise I will not waste your time. I just want to tell you a little about myself; it’s about time we got well-acquainted. I was born and raised in Michigan, and throughout high school, I felt a deep-rooted call to service. I decided I wouldn’t just read about service in the magazines, I would live it. Graduating from West Point was just the beginning of my eight years in the United States Army. During Operation Iraqi Freedom, I led Apache Helicopter Platoons, and I feel like I spent more time in the air than I did on the ground. Some nights, I didn’t know if I’d make it through the next day, and every mission I flew, I went into the unknown. Throughout my service, I had the honor of receiving a Combat Action Badge and two Air Medals. I wouldn’t trade my time in the service for anything, but I’ll be honest, it was good coming home, and I can rest easy knowing I did my country proud. After coming back stateside, I swapped my fatigues for a suit. I took over the family business, creating jobs here in Michigan and earning a master’s in supply chain management from Penn State and an MBA from the University of Michigan. I was never one to rest, and after making so many life-or-death decisions in Iraq, I knew every second mattered; I wanted to make the most of my time for my family and me. I never for a second considered running for office, and the last thing I’d consider myself is a politician... I saw the Democrats destroying our country, and I knew my service to this great nation wasn’t over yet. Everybody told me running for office isn’t easy, but my heart was telling me it was the right thing to do. I won my election, with the help of President Trump, and started delivering results for my new constituents. Then, in 2023, when the Establishment tried to move on from Trump and being MAGA was seen as risky or politically inconvenient, I was among the first in Michigan to endorse President Trump for 2024. Loyalty isn’t a talking point to me; it’s the only way I know how to operate. My dedication to this country, my loyalty towards my constituents, and my desire to see the greatest nation on earth excel are part of the reasons why I’m now emailing you, but they’re not my #1 reason why... These three kids are the reason why I’m sending this message to you, as a TRUMP-ENDORSED Republican and father running to be the next Governor of Michigan. Having my own family taught me more lessons than I could list, and it was the one thing being in the U.S. Army didn’t prepare me for. But it also awoke in me a desire to do EVERYTHING and ANYTHING I can to ensure my kids have bright futures. My family means everything to me, and Michigan is our home; that’s why I will fight like my life depends on it to save this state and win this November. I’m under no illusions; I know this election will be one of the toughest challenges I’ve faced in my entire life, but after everything I’ve done in my service, it’s nothing I can’t handle. Unfortunately, the one thing I can’t directly control is spending, and the Democrats will do everything in their power to stop my campaign from making it to the ballot box this November. Nothing can stop us from saving this country if we stand together. Today, I’m asking you to make a small-dollar gift of $10, $25, $50 or ANYTHING you can spare to fuel my campaign’s fight as we approach our upcoming election for Governor on November 3rd. Thank you for taking the time to read my message. I hope to hear from you in the days to come. He met with one of our team members at 8 pm last night to give us a check before leaving for a family trip early this morning. body:
They're running hard to get our tax dollars. What are we doing?

| | | | | |
---
|
---
| | | | |
---
| |

This race will be decided by turnout. And right now, the other side is mobilized like never before. They want the state income tax and control of Congress to fund their salaries and social programs.
They’re looking at our checking accounts and imagining what they could do with that money. All they want is for you to pay your “fair share”. My opponent has even proposed higher taxes on Social Security.
This is real.
Looking at national numbers, Fox News just reclassified our race from “Solid Republican” to “Likely Republican,” and it means we must buck the trend and work harder this year. I’m crisscrossing the district, speaking, sign-waving, going door-to-door and making phone calls so we can finish strong and win this. But this seat won’t stay in Republican hands without your help.
---
|
---
| |
The unions and the die-hard Democrats are “all in” this election. They are running a multi-million dollar turnout campaign, and they know exactly what they want if they win: to lock in Washington's first-ever income tax, passed by Democrats this year, and expand it until every Washingtonian is paying one.

MAGA is shocked we're competitive. A Black farmer from rural Louisiana isn't supposed to threaten their Senate seat. But here we are. | | | [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142470315/657031928/1254121610?refcode=261010_jamie_magashock&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjIvMS8xMjAwMzEiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiZTZhOTgzYjEtZDZkMy1mMTExLWJmNWItMDAyMjQ4MjRkNGRiIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=mWnbFLzDT3bkGnrXpSzNoF5UKD0L9dH94gJMEJoMHjs=)

Let me be honest with you about something.
I'm not supposed to be in this race.
The grandson of a sharecropper? Not supposed to be a viable Senate candidate in Louisiana.
A Black farmer from rural Tensas Parish? Not supposed to compete statewide in the Deep South.
Someone without billionaire backers or a Rolodex full of Washington insiders? Not supposed to have a shot at flipping a Senate seat.
But here we are.
**And MAGA is absolutely shocked.**
They thought Louisiana was locked up. They thought they could focus on defending seats in swing states while the South stayed safely red. They thought a race like ours — a real populist challenge to their grip on power — wasn't possible here.
They were wrong.
Look at what's happening: Democrats flipping Trump districts across the South. MAGA candidates tearing each other apart in primaries. Republican retirements at levels not seen since the Great Depression. Trump's approval cratering over his failed Iran war.
This is a once-in-a-lifetime opening. The kind of moment that doesn't come around often in Louisiana politics.
**_And I believe — deep in my bones — that this is the campaign to meet this moment._**
Not because I'm the most polished politician. Not because I've been planning a Senate run my whole career. But because I understand what working Louisianans need because I've lived their struggles.
I know what it's like to watch costs rise while your income stays flat. I know what it's like to compete against corporations that rig the system against family operations. I know what it's like to worry about whether there will be anything left for the next generation.
That's the authentic economic populism that can win here. Not the fake MAGA version that delivers nothing but culture wars — the real thing that actually fights for working people.
And if we capitalize on this moment — if we show the political world that Louisiana is genuinely winnable — everything changes.
Not just for this race. For the entire map. For what's possible in the South.
But only if we have the resources to compete. And that counts on good folks like you stepping up.

I'm so excited to share that I've earned Governor Wes Moore's endorsement.
From Maryland to communities across the country, Governor Moore has been a powerful advocate for working families and a voice for a new generation of leadership.
As Maryland's first Black governor, he's one of the trailblazers who inspired me to step up and take on leadership roles in politics.
I'm honored to have his support, and I look forward to standing alongside him in the fight for common sense, accountability, and a better future for working families.
Now, I'm ready to bring that fight to Kentucky. Together, we can challenge the status quo, put people ahead of special interests, and prove that our communities deserve leaders who work for them, not just the elite.
My last end-of-month deadline before the election is 2 days away, and if we're going to reach every last voter, I really need to reach this final goal. Can you chip in whatever you can spare to support me in this last stretch?

I'm thankful to everyone who has stuck with me. Let's win this!

body:
Across Alaska, elections are conducted by dedicated local government clerks, yet many communities are struggling to fill these essential positions. | | | | [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142471313/657034943/2003048360?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxNi8xLzEwMjc1NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI0MTc5YjBlYi1kOGQzLWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDIyNDgyNGQ0ZGIiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=rWXNvqZE6LNuhxQDPxR-kY7jkh8lMcJKGYuygkzIPh0=&emci=35e40f48-63ce-f111-bf5b-00224829f869&emdi=4179b0eb-d8d3-f111-bf5b-00224824d4db&ceid=9512399)
---
| | | Dear Friend, Even though the last day to vote is Tuesday, **many of us, mostly in urban Alaska, have already voted in record numbers. It's not that easy in smaller towns and villages.** There, casting a ballot relies on a lot of players woven together: poll workers, post offices, local government clerks and tribal administrators, and many, many volunteers. **That is civic infrastructure, and in too many Alaska communities, it is stretched thin.** Our updated [Alaska Civic Infrastructure Assessment](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142471314/657034944/-1225593654?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxNi8xLzEwMjc1NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI0MTc5YjBlYi1kOGQzLWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDIyNDgyNGQ0ZGIiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=rWXNvqZE6LNuhxQDPxR-kY7jkh8lMcJKGYuygkzIPh0=&emci=35e40f48-63ce-f111-bf5b-00224829f869&emdi=4179b0eb-d8d3-f111-bf5b-00224824d4db&ceid=9512399) looks at the full system that lets Alaskans vote and shows where shortages exist and found that:
* **27** cities have not reported holding a local election in 2025–2026.
* **67** communities are USPS Postmaster Relief Sites, a sign of limited postal service that can affect absentee ballots.
* **24** local government clerk positions are vacant statewide.

**That last gap is where our work begins.** Democracy doesn't run itself, and in rural Alaska, clerks carry an added role, supporting state and federal elections as well as local ones. Working with communities and organizations statewide, we're telling clerks' stories and building recognition for a job most Alaskans have never thought about. Our video, [No Clerk, No Election](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142471315/657034945/-803653937?v=6bPVFnIcss8&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxNi8xLzEwMjc1NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI0MTc5YjBlYi1kOGQzLWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDIyNDgyNGQ0ZGIiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=rWXNvqZE6LNuhxQDPxR-kY7jkh8lMcJKGYuygkzIPh0=&emci=35e40f48-63ce-f111-bf5b-00224829f869&emdi=4179b0eb-d8d3-f111-bf5b-00224824d4db&ceid=9512399), shows what's at stake when that position sits empty. **We don't do this alone. We work alongside other nonpartisan 501(c)(3) organizations through the Alaska Voter Hub to identify problems and respond in real time**. And thanks to donors like you, strong support and partnerships with the Rasmuson Foundation, RurAL CAP Foundation, the Alaska Association of Municipal Clerks, and the Alaska Municipal League, this work is reaching communities across Alaska. Whatever concerns you most, from post offices to polling stations, there is a lot to do. **We invite your continued support by making a donation [here](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142471316/657034946/-412970717?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxNi8xLzEwMjc1NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI0MTc5YjBlYi1kOGQzLWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDIyNDgyNGQ0ZGIiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=rWXNvqZE6LNuhxQDPxR-kY7jkh8lMcJKGYuygkzIPh0=&emci=35e40f48-63ce-f111-bf5b-00224829f869&emdi=4179b0eb-d8d3-f111-bf5b-00224824d4db&ceid=9512399). ** **We're also happy to bring this information to you live, wherever you are** (after the election, of course!). Marty Rutherford, Veronica Slajer, Heather Flynn, and I have taken our "dog and pony" show on the road, sharing the [assessment](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142471317/657034947/-1225593654?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxNi8xLzEwMjc1NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI0MTc5YjBlYi1kOGQzLWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDIyNDgyNGQ0ZGIiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=rWXNvqZE6LNuhxQDPxR-kY7jkh8lMcJKGYuygkzIPh0=&emci=35e40f48-63ce-f111-bf5b-00224829f869&emdi=4179b0eb-d8d3-f111-bf5b-00224824d4db&ceid=9512399) and our clerk work with groups around the state. **We'd love to visit your board, club, or community group next, in person or online**. Just drop us a line at [info@BuildAlaska.org](mailto:info@BuildAlaska.org). Thank you for your commitment to supporting our work. Jane Angvik

And thanks to donors like you, strong support and partnerships with the Rasmuson Foundation, RurAL CAP Foundation, the Alaska Association of Municipal Clerks, and the Alaska Municipal League, this work is reaching communities across Alaska. Whatever concerns you most, from post offices to polling stations, there is a lot to do. We invite your continued support by making a donation . I grew up on Star Trek: The Next Generation. I still remember being introduced to it in 1987 when Encounter at Farpoint first aired. My **Unc** was a Star Trek fan from the original series, and he told me there was a new Star Trek coming out and that I needed to watch it. I did, and I was immediately hooked.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..W7Yrixlrd5UtR5EHleR0Iwuo76pGjzZDGZjvnxDWgR8?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=196267588)
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..W7Yrixlrd5UtR5EHleR0Iwuo76pGjzZDGZjvnxDWgR8?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=196267588)
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/48094ff0-37b5-426e-ad72-a4ff1b4b716a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Captain Jean-Luc "The GOAT" Picard
I recorded every episode on VHS. I would sit there stopping and starting the tape so I could cut out the commercials, and I honestly do not think I missed more than a couple episodes during the entire run of the series. My dad kept those tapes for a long time, until my late 30's, until eventually we realized you could just buy the whole series on DVD, download it, or stream it like a normal person. But that process, looking back, was part of the obsession. It was part of the ritual. It was part of loving something before everything was available instantly.
Star Trek is deep in my heart. A lot of people may not know this about me, but I am a big nerd. Science, philosophy, sci-fi, all of it. I did not just watch Star Trek. One of my favorite classes in college was Philosophy and Star Trek, taught by Dr. Kathy Ferguson, who later became my thesis mentor. I wanted to write about Kantian philosophy in Star Trek. Her class was brilliant because she took Hegel, Mill, Kant, and so many others, then showed how those ideas played out inside Star Trek episodes.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/b48d9384-b5b0-4d64-9b80-223dcee2d81b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Dr. Ferguson
So when I came across this picture of the ten best Captain Picard quotes from The Next Generation, I kept thinking about it. Not because this is some deep academic breakdown, but because these quotes really did impact me and thousands others. They shaped my personality, my goals, my morals, my ideology, and the way I think about leadership, politics, truth, compromise, failure, and power.
Picard had this code. No compromise, but also enough judgment to know when the rule itself had to be questioned. He believed in sacrifice over self-indulgence. He carried this stoicism that was not always healthy, and in many ways, Picard was a sad lonely man. But for some reason, I admired that too. Maybe because he showed that leadership is not about being happy all the time. Sometimes it is about carrying the weight and still doing the right thing.
**Here are 10 great Captain Picard Quotes and what they mean to me.**

* * *
### 10\. "Let's see what's out there. Engage."
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/be66ad49-60e2-4822-a994-c954bc518e98?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
I am a creature of habit. I love comfort. There is nothing better than sleeping in my own bed, taking a shower in my own bathroom, and living inside the small rituals that make life feel stable. I have never been the traveling hippie type. I know people who can go anywhere, sleep anywhere, camp anywhere, move from place to place, and feel perfectly fine. I know people from the military who can do that without thinking twice. That is not me.
But at the same time, I cannot stay in one place forever. There is too much out there. I need to explore. That is why I moved to Hawaii. That is why I moved to China. That is why I lived in Taiwan. That is why I have been to more than 40 countries and learned foreign languages, because every culture and every language adds another layer to how you understand the world. The more time you spend outside your own bubble, the more depth you get.
And to be perfectly honest, that can be a lonely place. Not everybody has those experiences, and not everybody understands what it does to you. But trust me, the people who do understand find each other.
* * *
### 9\. "There can be no justice so long as laws are absolute. Even life itself is an exercise in exceptions."
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/8cacd5fb-45ec-4f22-ad78-e0ef0a74da8d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
I do not even remember the episode this quote came from, but as soon as I read it again, I thought, yeah, this is rebel Matt.
I do not believe laws are absolute. I never have. I am the guy who sees a no right turn on red sign and, if it is clear and nobody is being hurt, I am probably taking the turn. That may sound small, but that is the point. There are rules we follow because they protect people, and there are rules we follow because somebody wrote them down and nobody has questioned them since.
This one hit me because of recent Supreme Court rulings. Laws should be examined. Laws should be challenged. Laws should be changed. And yes, sometimes existing laws need to be broken, because shit, sometimes we have evolved. Sometimes a law was right for one moment, one context, one version of society, and then it becomes the opposite of what we wanted to achieve.
It means justice means change and change means there are no absolutes.

[Share The Angry Democrat](https://substack..3stUnQ5aZzNEjVz6VGMdNWj8gJbEJQXyTewwv_w_O1s?)
* * *
### 8\. "There are times, sir, when men of good conscience cannot blindly follow orders."
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/e88bed69-87bb-4449-ae42-1c546244c055?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Senator Mark Kelly
This one immediately made me think of Senator Mark Kelly and his statement about troops following orders under President Trump. There are two sides to this, and both are very valid. On one hand, you cannot have a military where everyone just disobeys orders because they personally do not like them. That creates chaos, and there have to be consequences for that.
But at the same time, you cannot have troops blindly following orders if those orders turn them into tools of something immoral, homicidal, genocidal, or unlawful. I am not saying that is what Trump is doing. I **AM** saying there has to be a line.
And this does not only apply to the military. It applies to your boss. It applies to your political party. It applies to your friends. It applies to yourself. At some point, you have to be able to say, no, I am not doing that. The more clearly you draw that line before the moment comes, the more likely you are to actually hold it when it matters. No matter the consequences.

[Share The Angry Democrat](https://substack..3stUnQ5aZzNEjVz6VGMdNWj8gJbEJQXyTewwv_w_O1s?)
### 7\. "Let's make sure history never forgets the name... Enterprise."
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/b5ed44c4-a7fd-4605-b26b-8cb89265a689?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
NCC 1701 D
Here lies my ego.
I do not know why I am on this earth, and I do not think most people really know either. But I know this. I do not want to die and be forgotten. I do not want to have no impact. I do not want to live a life, fade away, and have nobody remember me two generations from now.
If we are not trying to do something big, then what the hell are we doing? Go big or go home. I know that is not for everybody, and yes, I probably judge people for it more than I should. But I believe we are supposed to ruffle feathers. We are supposed to make waves in still water. I do not want to leave this earth without contributing something positive, something real, something that mattered.
* * *
### 6\. "You cannot explain away a wantonly immoral act because you think that it is connected to some higher purpose."
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/5eafce5f-1722-47d8-a1c9-ef499d385c79?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
This one is very relevant because of what we see in politics all the time. Money starts flowing, outside groups start spending on behalf of a candidate, and suddenly everyone wants to pretend the principle changes depending on who benefits. I want to be very clear because people love to twist shit. This is not about one specific candidate. This is about the system. It is about whether we actually believe money in politics is corrupting, or whether we only believe that when the money is helping someone we do not like.
When people say, "Well, you need money to run a race," they are not wrong. You do. But that does not erase the principle. You can still say you are against corporate money in politics. You can still say Super PACs are corrosive. You can still say the system is fucked, even if the system helps someone you like.
You do not get to explain away an immoral act because you think it is connected to some higher purpose, like winning office. Maybe you think your side deserves the exception. Maybe you think the ends justify the means. But does that make it right?
* * *
### 5\. "The first duty of every Starfleet officer is to the truth, whether it's scientific truth or historical truth or personal truth. It's the guiding principle on which Starfleet is based."
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/0bba6fab-b7d6-4b52-9a37-30b0e4b455de?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Star Fleet Academy, San Francisco
When I ran for office in 2022, I dealt with personal truth quite a bit. In 2024, I broke out of the consultant-driven version of campaigning and tried to run a campaign that was actually mine. My ideas. My instincts. My voice. My purpose.
Now I feel like I am on a different mission, which is trying to find truth in a broader sense. What do we actually want out of the United States? What do we want out of democracy? How much truth do people really want?
But truth is not just one thing. There is scientific truth, historical truth, political truth, and personal truth. The guiding principle should be figuring out what truth you are actually operating from. If you do not know that, then you are just reacting. You are not thinking. You are not leading. You are just being pushed around by whatever pressure hits you next.
* * *
### 4\. "With the first link, the chain is forged. The first speech censored, the first thought forbidden, the first freedom denied, chains us all irrevocably."
[](https://substack.com/redirect/78793b11-2a34-4f1a-a387-079f750ec74d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
This might be my favorite quote in all of Star Trek. It may be tied with another one, but this one is personal. This is not just about politics. This is about who you are and the decisions we make and what we allow.
I think about this every time someone in politics says, well, it is just a little compromise. Just take the money. Just look the other way. Just soften the statement. Just make the deal. Just vote for this one thing. Just go along this one time.
But with the first link, the chain is forged.
People do not think one small compromise changes how they legislate, how they represent people, or how they can be manipulated in the future. But it does. That first link matters because once it is attached to you, somebody can pull it. And once somebody can pull it, you are not as free as you were before.
I also think about this with our data, our privacy, AI, online manipulation, corporate control, and every app being designed like a slot machine. We keep acting like the first step does not matter. But it does.
It is like addiction. The danger is not just thinking about heroin. The danger is the first time you do it. That is when the path starts.
So how much compromise do you take? How much do you endure? How many times do you look the other way before you realize the chain is already around your neck?

[Share The Angry Democrat](https://substack..3stUnQ5aZzNEjVz6VGMdNWj8gJbEJQXyTewwv_w_O1s?)
* * *
### 3\. "It is possible to commit no mistakes and still lose. That is not a weakness; that is life."
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/7a660c65-788f-4b70-92c1-d83cd8a4da75?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
This is tied for my favorite Picard quote because I think about it all the time. I think about it for myself, but I also think about it for other people. I know people who started businesses and failed. I know people who started businesses, succeeded, and then failed later. I know people who did everything they were supposed to do and still ended up struggling.
And the truth is, some people do reckless things. Some people gamble, cheat, lie, or self-destruct. But most of the people I know who failed were not those people. They were people who tried hard, made decisions, worked their asses off, and still lost. The decisions did not work out, but that does not mean the decisions were stupid. It means life is brutal sometimes.
That is why I believe in a social safety net. Not because everyone who struggles is inadequate. But, sometimes people just lose. And when they do, a decent society does not treat them like garbage for it.
* * *
### 2\. "There. Are. Four. Lights."
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/1b47a214-c77b-46bf-b48b-9001505cec1f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
This is the power quote of power quotes.
If you do not know Star Trek, it may not make sense. But Captain Jean-Luc Picard was captured by the Cardassians, and they tried to break him. They wanted him to say there were five lights when there were only four. It was not really about the lights. It was about breaking his mind, his hope, his spirit, and his ability to trust what he knew was true.
And he did not break.
He said, "There! Are! Four! Lights!"
That means he refused to capitulate. He refused to give in to torture. He refused to say something false just to stop the pain. I honestly think everyone should watch that episode at least once a year, just to remember that whatever you are going through, however hard it gets, do not break.
But I also think this quote hits differently now because of what we consume every day. It is not just about torture in some distant sci-fi prison cell. It is about what people tell us is true, what media tells us is true, what algorithms push in front of us, and what we know in our gut is wrong.
We live in a time where manipulation is everywhere. Some of it comes from inside our own country. Some of it comes from outside of it. Now we have deepfakes, AI-generated bullshit, edited videos, fake screenshots, propaganda farms, and endless online narratives all trying to make people doubt what they saw, what they know, and what they believe.
That is what makes this lesson so important. People can look at the same video, the same event, the same set of facts, and walk away with completely different interpretations. Some of that is human nature, but some of it is intentional. The goal is to wear you down. The goal is to make you so confused, so tired, and so overwhelmed that you eventually give in and say whatever version of reality makes the pressure stop.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/1e0f7757-0d68-4f55-b2d5-6c36cb3cfa25?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
And that is where the strength comes in. Being grounded in truth, whether that is factual truth, personal truth, or moral truth, is not always popular. It is not always comfortable. Sometimes the easier path is to capitulate. Sometimes the more rewarding path, financially, socially, or politically, is to just say '**there are five lights '** and move on with your life.
But that is the whole point. The strength is seeing the situation clearly, knowing what is true, and refusing to let manipulation pull you away from it. It is not stubbornness for the sake of stubbornness. It is the discipline to say, no, I know what I saw. I know what happened. I know what is true.
**There! Are! Four! Lights!**

[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..W7Yrixlrd5UtR5EHleR0Iwuo76pGjzZDGZjvnxDWgR8?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=196267588)
* * *
### 1\. "Seize the time, Meribor. Live now. Make now always the most precious time. Now will never come again."
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/19c8a1d0-40d7-4583-bf8b-40b2353efef7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
This is probably the most Buddhist thing you could ever hear from Star Trek. Everybody talks about living in the now, but most people do not do it. We live in the future. We live in the past. We predict. We project. We worry. We replay old mistakes. We make decisions today based on imaginary futures that may never happen.
But the truth is, we do not know. We do not know what is coming. We do not know how long we have. We do not know which moment is going to matter until it is gone.
So why not make now the time? Why not live in the now and let it move over you like waves? Do not try to control every second of it. Do not plan so obsessively that you forget to actually experience your life. I think a lot of people would be happier if they stopped trying to manage every possible future and started being present in the one moment they actually have.
* * *
That is what these quotes mean to me. Some political. Some personal. Some probably obvious. Some maybe not that deep. But they are mine. Star Trek shaped me. Picard shaped me. Philosophy shaped me. And whether I am talking about campaigns, corruption, truth, law, compromise, or just trying not to break, I can still hear these lines in the back of my head.
That is what old Star Trek gives you. It gives you a moral question without handing you a clean answer,. That was the beauty of it. It was never on the nose. It was not just an action show. It was not empty entertainment in space uniforms. It was asking real questions about society, power, identity, duty, faith, work, love, marriage, race, gender, sexuality, and what it actually means to be decent when there is no perfect choice in front of you. Or how doing the right thing might actually make you a villain.
That is why I always encourage people to go back and watch the old episodes. Star Trek would put these questions in front of you, let the characters wrestle with them, and then refuse to insult you by pretending there was always one obvious answer. The crew still had to act. Picard still had to make a decision.
And that is the part I miss. That image of Picard staring out the window of his ready room, quietly carrying the choice he just made, is more powerful than most shows yelling their entire moral argument at you from some superiority high horse. It leaves you wondering whether he made the right call, or whether there was ever a right call to begin with.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/0fe0c9f3-f87b-4607-9884-40b63e8cb60e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
That was the beauty of Star Trek. It forced you to wrestle with ethical questions without treating you like a child. It was humbling. It reminded us that you can think hard, act in good faith, do everything right, and still lose.
That is not weakness. That is life.

**What could two proposed property-tax changes mean for Florida households and the communities they depend on?**
Amendment 3, on the 2026 ballot, proposes two changes. First, it would increase the homestead exemption on non-school property taxes for qualifying primary residences to $150,000 in 2027 and $250,000 in 2028, with inflation adjustments in subsequent years.
Second, it would lower the annual assessment-growth cap for non-homestead properties from 10% to 5%. That cap limits how much a property's assessed value may increase each year; it does not limit the tax bill itself.
The amendment would also change constitutional rules governing how counties and municipalities may use property-tax revenue, restricting spending to specified public purposes, with provisions for certain other expenditures.
Qualifying homeowners could save on property taxes, while local governments could collect less revenue. The effects on household finances, local budgets and public services will depend on how the changes play out in each community.
Florida's Revenue Estimating Conference projects a cumulative $45.84 billion reduction in local property-tax revenue statewide over five fiscal years, as reported by Florida TaxWatch. This is a forecast, not proof that services will be cut.
What might this mean for you? Check your county property appraiser's records to see whether your property has a recorded homestead exemption.
**And beyond your own tax bill, what might change in your community?** That is what we examine next.
