---|---|---
Fernando Cerimedo, a former adviser to Bolivian President Rodrigo Paz, sits at his hearing in the Nadia Beller shooting, in Santa Cruz, Bolivia, August 21, 2026. REUTERS/Ipa Ibanez
The day after Bolivian Attorney General Roger Mariaca was arrested in late September on drug-trafficking charges, presidential spokesperson Jose Luis Galvez called a press conference to thank U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio for his support. Then he delivered a warning.
"This has only just begun," said Galvez.
Since then Bolivian authorities have moved to [silence](https://substack.com/redirect/73e93e63-8430-42e4-8307-b7611a57d997?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a leftist news outlet, [jailed](https://substack.com/redirect/7afc3319-a15d-4f52-94c5-ad71228f0dff?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) an opposition lawmaker on terrorism charges, and announced an [investigation](https://substack.com/redirect/10d8bafb-86e5-4581-964c-41fd0c1be354?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) into former President Evo Morales.
Before his arrest Mariaca had been investigating Fernando Cerimedo, the MAGA-affiliated Argentine political operative after allegedly hiring a hitman to kill his pregnant ex-girlfriend, Nadia Beller. Cerimedo, who was a [top aide](https://substack.com/redirect/0036f145-9cdc-4e14-8733-7ff75f2ed322?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of President Rodrigo Paz, was also being investigated for drug trafficking.
Beller told Drop Site she expects to be arrested by Bolivian authorities as soon as Friday. She said government sources had warned her that she would be charged with failure to report Cerimedo's drug trafficking and election interference. She said the Ministry of Government planned to "build a case against me to persecute me and intimidate me, and in this way exonerate [Cerimedo], dismiss all charges against him and absolve him of all responsibility."
Mariaca's ouster sidelines a figure who had become a political problem for the Paz government, and serves as an example of how the selective prosecution of individuals accused of links to organized crime works to advance U.S. interests in the region.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/55dc56bd-ba60-42b3-9267-8209c4d7b360?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Bolivian activist Nadia Beller wears a bulletproof vest as Bolivian police escort her to testify as a witness, in Santa Cruz, Bolivia, September 23, 2026. REUTERS/Ipa Ibanez.
On September 28, two days before Mariaca's arrest, the United States [sanctioned](https://substack.com/redirect/8d41c5e5-69d1-403a-8c33-a5952ad54a80?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) him and revoked his visa for "involvement in significant corruption," including allegedly "soliciting and accepting bribes to facilitate narcotrafficking," helping "violent criminals evade justice," and "undermining" Bolivia's democratic institutions.
"I think it is important that if crimes have been committed they must be investigated and sanctioned, but his arrest, as it has happened, ignores all legal procedures and guarantees of due process," Canela Crespo, a Bolivian lawyer and political analyst, told Drop Site.
Galvez later told CNN in an October 6 interview that the timing of Mariaca's arrest was merely a "coincidence" and that the investigation had been ongoing since the March arrest of Uruguayan drug trafficker Sebastian Marset.
The charges against Mariaca center on his association with Marset, whom the former attorney general is accused of protecting through high-level bribes and leaked intelligence. On the night of his arrest, an ambulance attempting to leave Mariaca's residence was stopped with approximately $300,000, in both the local currency and U.S. dollars, and prosecutors claim they have financial intelligence linking him to drug trafficking networks.
Prior to his arrest, Mariaca vehemently denied U.S. allegations regarding ties to drug trafficking and claimed they were driven by political interests linked to his ongoing investigations.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/72a62efe-3bd0-43fe-9bb4-b674eb2e602a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Fernando Cerimedo (center left) is shown with Donald Trump Jr. (center right) and Brad Parscale (right), former campaign manager for President Donald Trump, in an undated photo posted to Nadia Beller's Facebook page in September.
Beller, who has spoken out publicly about her former partner's political activities throughout the region, told Drop Site that she believed the Trump administration was involved in the decision to arrest Mariaca due to his investigation into Cerimedo, who had ties to U.S. political figures such as Brad Parscale and Donald Trump Jr. In September, shortly before the Mariaca's arrest, she posted a photo of Cerimedo, Trump Jr., and Parscale to her Facebook page.
Bolivian Vice President Edmand Lara Montaño--who has publicly broken with Paz--leaked audio that allegedly captures Cerimedo negotiating payments for aircraft linked to drug trafficking operations.
Beller alleges that the Paz government acted over concerns that Mariaca's investigation could potentially reach the highest levels, including government ministers and even Paz's wife, Maria Elena Urquidi.
Following Cerimedo's arrest, Lara's legal team accused Urquidi of involvement in drug trafficking offenses, but prosecutors eventually opted to exclude her from their investigation.
Beller accused Bolivian government authorities of deliberately stalling and derailing the investigation into the assasination plot after her scheduled testimony as a protected witness was abruptly suspended.
"They want to protect their allies, there is no other explanation," Beller told Drop Site.
Crespo said the arrest of Mariaca is not only linked to an effort to impede investigations into Cerimedo's alleged criminal activities but to gain control over the country's prosecutor's office.
"U.S. interference and the actions of the Rodrigo Paz government seek first to deconstruct the judicial system as it is and to put their own pawns," said Crespo. "What you have to ask is what power structure is being disassembled, and above all, what power structure intends to be installed in its place."
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/5684306f-e805-4e07-afcb-0ae841772e1d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Bolivian Attorney General Roger Mariaca is shown in an undated file photo. Mariaca was arrested September 30, two days after the United States revoked their visas and accused Mariaca of corruption and aiding drug traffickers. REUTERS.
Mariaca, appointed in 2024 during the tenure of former president Luis Arce, had investigated politicians across the political spectrum, including supporters of Evo Morales, Paz's political rivals.
Kathryn Ledebur, director of the Andean Information Network and an expert on Bolivian politics, told Drop Site that Mariaca had become a "problem" for the Paz government.
"He had been useful for a certain amount of time, but his arrest and prosecution of Fernando Cerimedo was very uncomfortable," said Ledebur.
Bolivia's Plurinational Legislative Assembly moved quickly to select Mariaca's replacement, naming Jose Armando Urioste as acting attorney general. Urioste is behind the push to prosecute Morales and former Vice President Álvaro Garcia Linera over the deaths of three European citizens at the hands of police in 2009.
Mariaca's investigation into Cerimedo, who worked closely with the president, threatened to further destabilize an already weakened government that had been rocked by corruption allegations and intense protests in June and July over Paz's neoliberal economic policies.
Ledebur told Drop Site that in addition to worries about what Mariaca's investigation could reveal about high-level connections to drug trafficking, the Paz government was also motivated by their desire to secure stability ahead of a politically volatile time in Bolivia.
"They've illegally extended a state of emergency that limits freedoms guaranteed by the constitution, and we're at a point in time where they'd need to push through some major legislation that could significantly affect land tenure rights, indigenous rights, and all sorts of guarantees that were provided in the 2009 constitution," said Ledebur.
Social unrest in Bolivia tends to pick up in late October, after the planting season, when highly organized indigenous communities can turn their attention to their social demands, Ledebur explained.
The ouster of Mariaca and the derailment of his investigation into sensitive topics gives the Paz government room to operate as it attempts to push through unpopular reforms.
"I think what we're seeing is they're cleaning house to have a judiciary that responds to their interests and their needs, and to make sure that when gross human rights violations occur, when these violations of due process and the Constitution continue, that there is nothing in the judicial branch that would impede those actions or slow down this process that they seem to have planned in advance," Ledebur told Drop Site.
## Selective Prosecutions
Following Mariaca's arrest, U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Deputy Secretary of State Christopher Landau issued statements of support. A total of 15 countries that form part of President Donald Trump's Shield of the Americas initiative also [issued](https://substack.com/redirect/c1f93d77-b3ec-4bfe-9cd3-ed86cbb2cad9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a joint statement affirming their solidarity with Bolivia following the arrest of Mariaca.
The U.S.-led Shield of the Americas was launched in March, 2026 to coordinate counternarcotics activities in the region and has quickly evolved into a political alliance of countries allied with the U.S. agenda.
Since Trump's return to office, U.S. policy in the region has been largely dictated by the stated U.S. interest in combating "narco-terrorism." The kidnapping of Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro was justified as a "law enforcement operation" in connection to a drug-trafficking indictment.
Yet the Trump administration has also sought closer ties to regional leaders who face credible allegations of ties to drug trafficking. As part of his efforts to help secure a win for the right-wing National Party in Honduras, Trump pardoned former President Juan Orlando Hernandez after he was convicted by a New York court of trafficking drugs into the U.S. And Ecuador's President Daniel Noboa, whose family shipping business has been used by Balkan drug traffickers to [transport cocaine](https://substack.com/redirect/634c66db-0e62-4b82-88a3-ee0df5c4f9b7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), has emerged as one of Washington's closest allies. Noboa has used the fight against organized crime to justify a state of exception in his country and used this narrative to pursue his political opponents, including former presidential candidate Luisa Gonzalez, who was recently jailed.
Crespo said the Paz government's embrace of Washington's drug trafficking narrative also serves similar ends.
"In the Bolivian case, very clearly, very evidently, it points to the leadership of Evo Morales, but not only his, but also that of social leaders, indigenous peasant leaders, and the political persecution against those of these leaders is based on this narrative of the presence of drug trafficking," Crespo told Drop Site.
Benjamin Fogel, deputy director of the Alameda Institute, told Drop Site that the U.S. strategy of using the fight against drug trafficking to advance U.S. interests in Latin America has deep historical roots.
"This has been the pattern since [the Nixon administration] in Latin America: selective prosecution, selective use of threats, and selective application of ever-expanding laws to stop the threat of drug trafficking has been a means to manipulate, intimidate, and in effect, intimidate various governments and protect interest of the United States and its allies," Fogel told Drop Site.
Since his election earlier this year, Colombia's Abelardo de la Espriella, who once [served as lawyer](https://substack.com/redirect/ab91a759-dd9a-4884-9565-c216636106ea?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) for notorious Colombian paramilitary leaders and drug traffickers, has sought to strengthen his country's ties to Washington and invited U.S. troops into the country to directly participate in operations, a move that Fogel says would run afoul of the Colombian constitution.
Fogel points out that the U.S. strategy of selective application of counter-narcotics strategy has significant limitations, especially in the case of countries with greater state capacity like Mexico and Brazil.
In the case of Mexico, where President Claudia Sheinbaum has refused to accept U.S. operations, former Chihuahua Attorney General Cesar Jauregui has been charged with treason for illegally permitting CIA agents to participate in an operation.
Most recently, the U.S. extended a visa to former Brazilian presidential candidate Jair Bolsonaro to allow his entry into the country after he fled fleeing Brazil to avoid a money-laundering investigation.
"This is security slop. None of these policies are actually coherent," said Fogel.
_Joseph Bouchard and Camila Lourdes Galarza contributed to this report._

Your support is what keeps this journalism independent and free. . | | ---|---|--- Fernando Cerimedo, a former adviser to Bolivian President Rodrigo Paz, sits at his hearing in the Nadia Beller shooting, in Santa Cruz, Bolivia, August 21, 2026. REUTERS/Ipa Ibanez The day after Bolivian Attorney General Roger Mariaca was arrested in late September on drug-trafficking charges, presidential spokesperson Jose Luis Galvez called a press conference to thank U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio for his support. Then he delivered a warning. "This has only just begun," said Galvez. Since then Bolivian authorities have moved to a leftist news outlet, an opposition lawmaker on terrorism charges, and announced an into former President Evo Morales. Before his arrest Mariaca had been investigating Fernando Cerimedo, the MAGA-affiliated Argentine political operative after allegedly hiring a hitman to kill his pregnant ex-girlfriend, Nadia Beller. Cerimedo, who was a of President Rodrigo Paz, was also being investigated for drug trafficking. Beller told Drop Site she expects to be arrested by Bolivian authorities as soon as Friday. She said government sources had warned her that she would be charged with failure to report Cerimedo's drug trafficking and election interference. She said the Ministry of Government planned to "build a case against me to persecute me and intimidate me, and in this way exonerate [Cerimedo], dismiss all charges against him and absolve him of all responsibility." Mariaca's ouster sidelines a figure who had become a political problem for the Paz government, and serves as an example of how the selective prosecution of individuals accused of links to organized crime works to advance U.S. interests in the region. | | ---|---|--- Bolivian activist Nadia Beller wears a bulletproof vest as Bolivian police escort her to testify as a witness, in Santa Cruz, Bolivia, September 23, 2026. REUTERS/Ipa Ibanez. On September 28, two days before Mariaca's arrest, the United States him and revoked his visa for "involvement in significant corruption," including allegedly "soliciting and accepting bribes to facilitate narcotrafficking," helping "violent criminals evade justice," and "undermining" Bolivia's democratic institutions. "I think it is important that if crimes have been committed they must be investigated and sanctioned, but his arrest, as it has happened, ignores all legal procedures and guarantees of due process," Canela Crespo, a Bolivian lawyer and political analyst, told Drop Site. Galvez later told CNN in an October 6 interview that the timing of Mariaca's arrest was merely a "coincidence" and that the investigation had been ongoing since the March arrest of Uruguayan drug trafficker Sebastian Marset. The charges against Mariaca center on his association with Marset, whom the former attorney general is accused of protecting through high-level bribes and leaked intelligence. On the night of his arrest, an ambulance attempting to leave Mariaca's residence was stopped with approximately $300,000, in both the local currency and U.S. dollars, and prosecutors claim they have financial intelligence linking him to drug trafficking networks. Prior to his arrest, Mariaca vehemently denied U.S. allegations regarding ties to drug trafficking and claimed they were driven by political interests linked to his ongoing investigations. | | ---|---|--- Fernando Cerimedo (center left) is shown with Donald Trump Jr. (center right) and Brad Parscale (right), former campaign manager for President Donald Trump, in an undated photo posted to Nadia Beller's Facebook page in September. Beller, who has spoken out publicly about her former partner's political activities throughout the region, told Drop Site that she believed the Trump administration was involved in the decision to arrest Mariaca due to his investigation into Cerimedo, who had ties to U.S. political figures such as Brad Parscale and Donald Trump Jr. In September, shortly before the Mariaca's arrest, she posted a photo of Cerimedo, Trump Jr., and Parscale to her Facebook page. Bolivian Vice President Edmand Lara Montaño--who has publicly broken with Paz--leaked audio that allegedly captures Cerimedo negotiating payments for aircraft linked to drug trafficking operations. Beller alleges that the Paz government acted over concerns that Mariaca's investigation could potentially reach the highest levels, including government ministers and even Paz's wife, Maria Elena Urquidi. Following Cerimedo's arrest, Lara's legal team accused Urquidi of involvement in drug trafficking offenses, but prosecutors eventually opted to exclude her from their investigation. Beller accused Bolivian government authorities of deliberately stalling and derailing the investigation into the assasination plot after her scheduled testimony as a protected witness was abruptly suspended. "They want to protect their allies, there is no other explanation," Beller told Drop Site. Crespo said the arrest of Mariaca is not only linked to an effort to impede investigations into Cerimedo's alleged criminal activities but to gain control over the country's prosecutor's office. "U.S. interference and the actions of the Rodrigo Paz government seek first to deconstruct the judicial system as it is and to put their own pawns," said Crespo. "What you have to ask is what power structure is being disassembled, and above all, what power structure intends to be installed in its place." | | ---|---|--- Bolivian Attorney General Roger Mariaca is shown in an undated file photo. Mariaca was arrested September 30, two days after the United States revoked their visas and accused Mariaca of corruption and aiding drug traffickers. REUTERS. Mariaca, appointed in 2024 during the tenure of former president Luis Arce, had investigated politicians across the political spectrum, including supporters of Evo Morales, Paz's political rivals. Kathryn Ledebur, director of the Andean Information Network and an expert on Bolivian politics, told Drop Site that Mariaca had become a "problem" for the Paz government. "He had been useful for a certain amount of time, but his arrest and prosecution of Fernando Cerimedo was very uncomfortable," said Ledebur. Bolivia's Plurinational Legislative Assembly moved quickly to select Mariaca's replacement, naming Jose Armando Urioste as acting attorney general. Urioste is behind the push to prosecute Morales and former Vice President Álvaro Garcia Linera over the deaths of three European citizens at the hands of police in 2009. Mariaca's investigation into Cerimedo, who worked closely with the president, threatened to further destabilize an already weakened government that had been rocked by corruption allegations and intense protests in June and July over Paz's neoliberal economic policies. Ledebur told Drop Site that in addition to worries about what Mariaca's investigation could reveal about high-level connections to drug trafficking, the Paz government was also motivated by their desire to secure stability ahead of a politically volatile time in Bolivia. "They've illegally extended a state of emergency that limits freedoms guaranteed by the constitution, and we're at a point in time where they'd need to push through some major legislation that could significantly affect land tenure rights, indigenous rights, and all sorts of guarantees that were provided in the 2009 constitution," said Ledebur. Social unrest in Bolivia tends to pick up in late October, after the planting season, when highly organized indigenous communities can turn their attention to their social demands, Ledebur explained. The ouster of Mariaca and the derailment of his investigation into sensitive topics gives the Paz government room to operate as it attempts to push through unpopular reforms. "I think what we're seeing is they're cleaning house to have a judiciary that responds to their interests and their needs, and to make sure that when gross human rights violations occur, when these violations of due process and the Constitution continue, that there is nothing in the judicial branch that would impede those actions or slow down this process that they seem to have planned in advance," Ledebur told Drop Site. Selective Prosecutions Following Mariaca's arrest, U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Deputy Secretary of State Christopher Landau issued statements of support. A total of 15 countries that form part of President Donald Trump's Shield of the Americas initiative also a joint statement affirming their solidarity with Bolivia following the arrest of Mariaca. The U.S.-led Shield of the Americas was launched in March, 2026 to coordinate counternarcotics activities in the region and has quickly evolved into a political alliance of countries allied with the U.S. agenda. Since Trump's return to office, U.S. policy in the region has been largely dictated by the stated U.S. interest in combating "narco-terrorism." The kidnapping of Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro was justified as a "law enforcement operation" in connection to a drug-trafficking indictment. Yet the Trump administration has also sought closer ties to regional leaders who face credible allegations of ties to drug trafficking. As part of his efforts to help secure a win for the right-wing National Party in Honduras, Trump pardoned former President Juan Orlando Hernandez after he was convicted by a New York court of trafficking drugs into the U.S. And Ecuador's President Daniel Noboa, whose family shipping business has been used by Balkan drug traffickers to , has emerged as one of Washington's closest allies. Noboa has used the fight against organized crime to justify a state of exception in his country and used this narrative to pursue his political opponents, including former presidential candidate Luisa Gonzalez, who was recently jailed. Crespo said the Paz government's embrace of Washington's drug trafficking narrative also serves similar ends. "In the Bolivian case, very clearly, very evidently, it points to the leadership of Evo Morales, but not only his, but also that of social leaders, indigenous peasant leaders, and the political persecution against those of these leaders is based on this narrative of the presence of drug trafficking," Crespo told Drop Site. Benjamin Fogel, deputy director of the Alameda Institute, told Drop Site that the U.S. strategy of using the fight against drug trafficking to advance U.S. interests in Latin America has deep historical roots. "This has been the pattern since [the Nixon administration] in Latin America: selective prosecution, selective use of threats, and selective application of ever-expanding laws to stop the threat of drug trafficking has been a means to manipulate, intimidate, and in effect, intimidate various governments and protect interest of the United States and its allies," Fogel told Drop Site. Since his election earlier this year, Colombia's Abelardo de la Espriella, who once for notorious Colombian paramilitary leaders and drug traffickers, has sought to strengthen his country's ties to Washington and invited U.S. troops into the country to directly participate in operations, a move that Fogel says would run afoul of the Colombian constitution. Fogel points out that the U.S. strategy of selective application of counter-narcotics strategy has significant limitations, especially in the case of countries with greater state capacity like Mexico and Brazil. In the case of Mexico, where President Claudia Sheinbaum has refused to accept U.S. operations, former Chihuahua Attorney General Cesar Jauregui has been charged with treason for illegally permitting CIA agents to participate in an operation. Most recently, the U.S. extended a visa to former Brazilian presidential candidate Jair Bolsonaro to allow his entry into the country after he fled fleeing Brazil to avoid a money-laundering investigation. "This is security slop. None of these policies are actually coherent," said Fogel. In classic Mitch McConnell fashion, Andy Barr was _once_ _again_ a no-show to our debate this week.
I can't say I'm surprised. After his last performance, I wouldn't show up either.
He couldn't answer a question without bringing up his puppet master, Donald Trump, or the special groups funding his campaign.
Whether discussing local data centers or the disastrous conflict with Iran, all Barr did was put his unpopular policies on full display and remind voters of his allegiance to a deeply broken status quo.
So this time, he just didn't come.
Here's what that tells me: Andy Barr knows he can't win this race on the issues. His only leverage is that his rich donors keep funneling millions into his campaign to attack me on the airwaves.
I'm running on my message alone, and my grassroots supporters like you are what fuels this whole fight. If you're with me, I need you to step up before the last ballots are cast in just a few days. Will you chip in just $25?

Thank you. I do it all for you!
_**Charles Booker**_

name: Jim Jordan
subject: I’ve NEVER emailed you like this before…
body:
But at this final moment, you’re truly my last hope.
| **_A PERSONAL LETTER FROM THE DESK OF JIM JORDAN_**
---
Peter,
---
I know you get spammed with desperate fundraising messages at the end of the month, so I’ve never written to you about monthly deadlines before.
---
Instead, I always put in the work and do my best to ensure we hit our benchmarks well before any potential fundraising cutoff.
---
And here’s what most fundraising messages never tell you...
---
_Truth be told, under normal circumstances, you can just fix a fundraising shortfall in one month by raising more the following month!_
---
But the last deadline of an election is different. Because once the polls close on election night, there’s no going back. There is no “next month” to make up the difference. The results are FINAL. You either win or you lose.
---
**So, since this Saturday, October 31st, is the real,_final_ deadline of the midterms – _and we’re running out of time to raise the funds we need_ – I had no choice but to make an exception.**
---
I’ll be honest and up front with you: __We need AT LEAST another $25,000 in our accounts before the close-of-books.__
---
That’s not some random number I just made up on the spot. That’s a real goal, set by our team, to ensure my leadership account has the vital funds needed to WIN the biggest toss-up congressional races in the nation.
---
And at this FINAL moment that will decide the fate of the President’s Majority, _YOU_ are the FINAL place left for me to turn, Peter!
---
_I’m dead serious. At this point I’m out of options – I don’t have any wealthy donors I can call up, and I refuse to resort to spam or fake matches to try to get grassroots donations._
---
**My only hope of raising the remaining funds we need before this last deadline is to personally write this honest appeal directly to grassroots conservatives like _YOU_. **
---
Of course, I’d never ask you to do something I wouldn’t do myself.
---
**That’s why I’ve put my money where my mouth is by transferring a total of _$6.62 MILLION_ _away from my own accounts_ to help WIN the battleground races that will decide the midterms.**
---
**At this FINAL deadline, can I count on YOU to stand with me and match my commitment to saving the President’s Majority?**
---
The __amount__ you give isn’t what’s important. Instead, what matters is the __sheer__ __number__ of patriots who answer my call and have our back when we need it most!
---
[**So please, make a grassroots contribution of any amount you can afford to help us raise the $25,000 we need to SAVE our Majority before the FINAL deadline of the midterm elections.**](http://links.itsourgreatamerica.com/u/click?_t=442fb7cf105f4725a8bda0b6bcffc1bd&_m=79c897d23a7f4d1d842b13e510d0229b&_e=YaZ26IghK8D-cQ51SNLrJdPs_Y93Nn2dXfp-7DZ7f1uDjpcqAiBuBwNZaziw0yrrsZG8dSV9bOkZj4onGmTV5PG6HNAKqCYLqHPNAqfc4oZpGmTpJ6li9vvtzlwy3aogDwRWNU6WZg1cEimjsnzVxrWgJ-8uYDbdXRbxaiJ1x5d7pvkWKnaKFIhVq2_Q14y3qE8VwBk0JV-jmziSus0rWuxQgUSeI4uGnwKZzEuttDuZitA6811DKc48YJWoIvBETg1_zc_y3UTLfp3mT-6l2W9YFNm32Ug4ZUw1hpah1gkPxsl2UBiH9Doxb-zFxIoSYlyYdWQOkX00vpnVvLTJwJVCpI6LOjiXO5UvnKS9OKj8cnrXYpQD849qbxA218rESojWcB00orZPlCrr_j0oh9fqmdngSSOgpRbBvtgTPALnz-H59wl-1f7T5Rz34X1SvLeBLz9QqnhI-x_gChG9-GGxXFIKLM9zPwBPC8PqnnH3ZylQVL1zXUJ0dhPk_UgN9o0pejWkARqCj1NhwssusNBxEn158T_UP-Ast5bcFOgOcQ6mtuZ0Xnt_pj4jnXrYZfuowrvv4r6Ms6nA50r1MZClhWmgZp8fcurVBMyjOAqkQj5JJy8W8tqmvQuoFJui95J2DBQ9d8oUpuN4n_CZhgY57qodgr13du4R56n-O27h1qRP4CELfbRQqzt3CdIVnhAgJ_6G_U9SF00_f6o_pQCrwaRbVarmH9N5kG-QPx8%3D)

clean_body: But at this final moment, you’re truly my last hope. | A PERSONAL LETTER FROM THE DESK OF JIM JORDAN Peter, I know you get spammed with desperate fundraising messages at the end of the month, so I’ve never written to you about monthly deadlines before. Instead, I always put in the work and do my best to ensure we hit our benchmarks well before any potential fundraising cutoff. And here’s what most fundraising messages never tell you... Truth be told, under normal circumstances, you can just fix a fundraising shortfall in one month by raising more the following month! But the last deadline of an election is different. Because once the polls close on election night, there’s no going back. There is no “next month” to make up the difference. The results are FINAL. You either win or you lose. So, since this Saturday, October 31st, is the real,final deadline of the midterms – and we’re running out of time to raise the funds we need – I had no choice but to make an exception. I’ll be honest and up front with you: We need AT LEAST another $25,000 in our accounts before the close-of-books. That’s not some random number I just made up on the spot. That’s a real goal, set by our team, to ensure my leadership account has the vital funds needed to WIN the biggest toss-up congressional races in the nation. And at this FINAL moment that will decide the fate of the President’s Majority, YOU are the FINAL place left for me to turn, Peter! I’m dead serious. At this point I’m out of options – I don’t have any wealthy donors I can call up, and I refuse to resort to spam or fake matches to try to get grassroots donations. My only hope of raising the remaining funds we need before this last deadline is to personally write this honest appeal directly to grassroots conservatives like YOU. Of course, I’d never ask you to do something I wouldn’t do myself. That’s why I’ve put my money where my mouth is by transferring a total of $6.62 MILLION away from my own accounts to help WIN the battleground races that will decide the midterms. At this FINAL deadline, can I count on YOU to stand with me and match my commitment to saving the President’s Majority? The amount you give isn’t what’s important. Instead, what matters is the sheer number of patriots who answer my call and have our back when we need it most! Thank you, Jim Jordan Paid for by Team Jordan a joint fundraising committee authorized by and composed between Jim Jordan for Congress, Buckeye Liberty Fund, and American Liberty Foundation PAC. On November 3, voters will decide what kind of America our kids and grandkids inherit. Here is what's on the line: Freedom vs. Socialism Free Speech vs. Political Violence Secure Borders vs. Mass Immigration Fair Elections vs. Fraud Education vs. Woke Indoctrination. Hi there,
**Not sure where your donation can make the biggest difference?**
With just five days until Election Day, there are hundreds of critical races competing for resources—we’re sure you’re hearing from many of them! You could spend hours trying to figure out where your money will have the most impact.
**Or, you can let Swing Left do the work.**
**We sent you an update earlier this week with our _final_ Immediate Impact Fund update, and with Election Day getting closer by the hour, we wanted to bring it back to the top of your inbox. **
The political team at Swing Left has spent months tracking these races closely and is using all the knowledge they’ve gained, plus the latest information directly from campaigns, to determine the 20 races where your donation is needed most—and where it stands to make the largest difference:
[](https://act.swingleft.org/go/27?c0=immediate-impact-2026.DM5m6O&utm_source=ak&%3Butm_medium=em&%3Butm_campaign=iif-2026&%3Butm_content=20261029-2&%3Brefcode=ak_em_iif-2026_20261029-2&t=1&akid=3339%2E1562180%2E79rHQc)

When you give to the Immediate Impact Fund, your donation is split across the races where grassroots money can make the biggest difference right now: especially close races, underfunded campaigns, and candidates facing a flood of Republican outside spending. Instead of trying to figure out on your own which races need help most, you can trust that your dollars are going where they’ll count.
Your donation will also power the Swing Left community’s work to turn out voters across the country, through door knocking, phone banking, and every other way we can reach the voters who will decide these races.
We’re not just trying to scrape by with a slim majority. We want to win as many races as possible, by as large a margin as possible, so Democrats have a durable majority in both chambers of Congress strong enough to actually govern.
With this in mind: [**Will you make a donation of $25 right now to help power these critical campaigns across the finish line?**](https://act.swingleft.org/go/27?c0=immediate-impact-2026.DM5m6O&amount=25&%3Butm_source=ak&%3Butm_medium=em&%3Butm_campaign=iif-2026&%3Butm_content=20261029-2&%3Brefcode=ak_em_iif-2026_20261029-2&t=3&akid=3339%2E1562180%2E79rHQc)
Thank you for being a part of this work,
The Swing Left Team
P.S. _If you missed it, read our message from earlier this week to learn more about the races we’re fighting for in these final days, and how your support right now could make the difference._

**We’re also not just looking to eke out a slim majority. We’re looking to win as many races for Democrats as possible, by as large a margin as possible, for an uncontested, durable majority in both chambers of Congress.**

Last night I took the stage with President Obama in Atlanta, where thousands joined us to rally and organize in opposition to the Trump administration and my opponent, Mike Collins.
Folks, it is truly crunch time. Voting is underway in Georgia, and we have no time to waste to reach voters across the state and get out the vote.
I can't do it alone.
If you're ready to play a crucial role in defeating MAGA and helping me win this U.S. Senate race, please use this link to chip in to my reelection campaign today: **[https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ossoff-fr-substack-2026](https://substack.com/redirect/1e26ae67-7fdf-404a-b917-fcf1925bad7d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
Only by regaining Congressional power can we stop the chaos and corruption of the Trump administration and restore checks and balances in Washington.
And from the energy I felt on stage, it's clear Georgians are ready to do our part.
Winning again won't be easy.
Georgia remains one of the most pivotal and most competitive battleground states in the country.
MAGA has spent *tens of millions* to try to defeat me, just like they did six years ago.
But we've been here before. We've done this before. And we won.
Let's do it again.
**[If you 're outraged by what's happening to this country -- and you're ready to fight for the future of our Republic -- donate to my reelection campaign today. Every single donation right now sends a powerful message that people like you have my back.](https://substack.com/redirect/1e26ae67-7fdf-404a-b917-fcf1925bad7d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[DONATE NOW](https://substack.com/redirect/1e26ae67-7fdf-404a-b917-fcf1925bad7d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
It is time now to do everything we can to deliver the victory that Georgians and the country are counting on.
I hope you'll join us. I need you by my side now more than ever.
Thank you so much,
Jon

country — from Nate Silver to Nate Cohn — are warning that the polls could
be overestimating Democrats' lead by several points.

After years of polls underestimating Trump, we cannot take anything for
granted.

That’s why Our Revolution is going all in on our final get-out-the-vote
